PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: Peer ID of the entitlement issuer/provider.

PROVIDER_SIGNATURE.description: Provider signature over the entitlement record.

SOURCE_ID.description: Reference to source imagery (e.g., SKI, GDI, EOO)

KEY_ID.description: Logical key identifier used across publication and grant records.

ROLE.description: Role the key bytes fulfill for the module flow.

ALGORITHM.description: Algorithm or key family for the key bytes.

ENCODING.description: Encoding of KEY_BYTES.

KEY_BYTES.description:
Explicit key bytes when a module must receive them on a port.
This may be field-encrypted using the SDS/da-flatbuffers header-first
encryption flow when transported to a specific recipient.

VERSION.description: Logical version of the key material.

EXPIRES_AT.description: Expiration time in unix milliseconds, or 0 if unbounded.

GNPName.description:
One name a place is known by, beside its primary NAME. Every attribute is
carried as the gazetteer publishes it; a consumer choosing a display name
applies its own policy over these flags and never has the choice baked in
by the publisher.

NAME.description: The alternate name verbatim, in its own script, unnormalized.

LANGUAGE.description:
ISO 639 language tag when the gazetteer states one. A gazetteer may also
state a non-language tag for a link or a postal, IATA, ICAO, or similar
coded name; that token is carried verbatim rather than discarded.

IS_PREFERRED.description: The gazetteer marks this as the preferred name for its language.

IS_SHORT.description: The gazetteer marks this as a short form.

IS_COLLOQUIAL.description: The gazetteer marks this as colloquial or unofficial.

IS_HISTORIC.description: The gazetteer marks this name as no longer in use.

VALID_FROM.description:
Period the name was in use, verbatim as the gazetteer states it. Not
normalized to RFC 3339: gazetteers publish partial and era-qualified
dates here, and coercion would invent precision.

GNPProvenance.description:
Dataset lineage and redistribution terms for one gazetteer place.

Required on every record: a redistributed place whose dataset, epoch, and
licence are unstated is not publishable. Dataset identity is DATA:
DATASET_ID, DATASET_NAME, and ATTRIBUTION carry verbatim what the gazetteer
states about itself. The standard names no gazetteer, dataset, or site.

DATASET_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the gazetteer this place was
taken from, unique within the publisher's own dataset registry. Never a
display name and never a URL.

DATASET_NAME.description: The dataset's own name, verbatim as its publisher states it.

DATASET_URL.description: Replayable URL of the dataset as published.

DATASET_EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond epoch of the dataset edition this place
was decoded from. The edition boundary, not the fetch: two records
carrying the same DATASET_ID and DATASET_EPOCH were cut from the same
bytes and are directly comparable.

DATASET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the exact dataset artifact, when the publisher
distributes one, so an epoch can be verified rather than trusted.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material within the dataset.

SOURCE_QUERY.description:
The exact query, filter, or file selection used, so the same rows can be
recovered by repeating the fetch.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond retrieval timestamp.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Required: there is no encoding for a
redistributed place whose terms are unstated. A dataset that publishes no
terms is recorded as publishing no terms; unknown terms are never public
domain and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as that dataset publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description:
Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.
Required whenever the terms are attribution-bearing, which is the common
case for open gazetteers, and carried verbatim so a downstream surface
can render it without composing its own credit line.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: The licence forbids commercial use.

SHARE_ALIKE.description: The licence obliges derived works to carry the same terms.

NATIVE_ID.description:
This gazetteer's own row identifier for the place, verbatim. The join key
back to the source dataset; never re-minted by the publisher.

NATIVE_MODIFIED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC date on which the gazetteer last modified this row, as the
gazetteer states it. Distinct from DATASET_EPOCH: an unchanged row keeps
its modification date across editions, which is what makes incremental
sync possible.

GNP.description:
Gazetteer Named Place

One named geographic place as a gazetteer publishes it: its names, its
position on WGS 84, its feature classification, its administrative
containment, and the dataset edition and licence it was redistributed
under. The record is a NAME-TO-PLACE lookup surface — place search,
geocoding, and administrative resolution — and is deliberately not a
facility, station, or emitter record: $SIT carries an operational
facility, $GST a geodetic tracking station, $TBS a terrestrial base-station
site. A place gains meaning from those records by being joined to, never by
being conflated with them.

Positions are decimal degrees on WGS 84 and elevations are metres,
unconverted. A consumer needing other units converts at the join,
explicitly.

ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier for this place record. Never the gazetteer's
own row identifier, which rides verbatim in SOURCE.NATIVE_ID.

NAME.description: Primary name of the place, verbatim in its own script, unnormalized.

ASCII_NAME.description:
Plain-ASCII rendering of NAME when the gazetteer publishes one. A search
and sort convenience, never a substitute for NAME.

ALTERNATE_NAMES.description: Every other name the gazetteer publishes for this place.

LATITUDE.description: Latitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive north.

LONGITUDE.description: Longitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive east.

ELEVATION_M.description:
Elevation in metres above the WGS 84 ellipsoid-referenced vertical datum
the gazetteer states, as published. Zero means unpublished, never sea
level; a place at sea level is distinguished by ELEVATION_PUBLISHED.

ELEVATION_PUBLISHED.description:
ELEVATION_M carries a published value. False marks a gazetteer that
publishes no elevation for this place.

DEM_ELEVATION_M.description:
Elevation in metres sampled from a digital elevation model, when the
gazetteer publishes a model-derived value beside or instead of a surveyed
one. Kept separate: a model sample is not a survey and the two must never
silently substitute for one another.

DEM_MODEL.description:
Name of the digital elevation model DEM_ELEVATION_M was sampled from,
verbatim as the gazetteer states it.

FEATURE_CLASS.description: Broad feature class this gazetteer assigns.

FEATURE_CLASS_CODE.description:
The gazetteer's own class token, verbatim, so a class outside
gnpFeatureClass survives a round trip.

FEATURE_CODE.description: The gazetteer's fine-grained feature code, verbatim.

FEATURE_NAME.description:
Human-readable expansion of FEATURE_CODE, as the gazetteer publishes it.
A display string, never a key.

COUNTRY_CODE.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase, as the gazetteer states it.

COUNTRY_NAME.description:
Country name as the gazetteer publishes it. A display name, never a key:
consumers key on COUNTRY_CODE.

ALTERNATE_COUNTRY_CODES.description:
Further ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for places the gazetteer reports as
spanning or being disputed between several countries. Order carries no
precedence and no sovereignty claim.

ADMIN1_CODE.description: First-order administrative division code within COUNTRY_CODE, verbatim.

ADMIN1_NAME.description:
Resolved name of that division. Carried beside the code so a consumer
need not hold the division tables to render a place.

ADMIN3_CODE.description:
Third- and fourth-order division codes, verbatim. Gazetteers publish
these as codes only; a name is carried when one is published.

POPULATION.description:
Population as the gazetteer publishes it. Zero means unpublished, never
uninhabited.

TIME_ZONE_ID.description: IANA time zone identifier for the place, verbatim.

TIME_ZONE_UTC_OFFSET_H.description:
Offset from UTC in hours the gazetteer states for that zone outside
daylight saving, and under it. Carried as published; a consumer needing
an instant-correct offset resolves TIME_ZONE_ID against a current tz
database rather than trusting these.

TIME_ZONE_DST_OFFSET_H.description: Offset from UTC in hours under daylight saving.

SOURCE.description:
Dataset lineage and redistribution terms. Required: a place with no named
dataset, epoch, and licence is not publishable.

BOOSTING.description: True if object is in boost phase

DROP_PT_IND.description: True if drop point indicator set

VECTOR_COMPONENTS.description: Number of components per vector (default 6: X, Y, Z, VX, VY, VZ)

VECTORS.description: Vector data as flat array [X0, Y0, Z0, VX0, VY0, VZ0, X1, ...]

AOU_RPT.description: AOU report data as flat array

LAUNCH_AOU.description: Launch AOU data as flat array

IMPACT_AOU.description: Impact AOU data as flat array

sbmFragment.description:
One debris fragment produced by a breakup event.

Vector components are expressed in the parent SBM.REF_FRAME axes.
Position and velocity are the fragment's state at SBM.EPOCH, i.e. the
parent state plus the ejection delta-V, before any propagation.

ORIGIN.description: Which parent body this fragment came from.

AM_RATIO_M2_PER_KG.description: Area-to-mass ratio in square meters per kilogram.

AREA_M2.description: Average cross-sectional area in square meters.

DELTA_V_MAG_M_PER_S.description: Magnitude of the ejection delta-V in meters per second.

DELTA_V_X_M_PER_S.description: Ejection delta-V X component in meters per second.

DELTA_V_Y_M_PER_S.description: Ejection delta-V Y component in meters per second.

DELTA_V_Z_M_PER_S.description: Ejection delta-V Z component in meters per second.

POSITION_X_KM.description: Fragment position X component in kilometers.

POSITION_Y_KM.description: Fragment position Y component in kilometers.

POSITION_Z_KM.description: Fragment position Z component in kilometers.

VELOCITY_X_KM_PER_S.description: Fragment velocity X component in kilometers per second.

VELOCITY_Y_KM_PER_S.description: Fragment velocity Y component in kilometers per second.

VELOCITY_Z_KM_PER_S.description: Fragment velocity Z component in kilometers per second.

SBM.description:
Satellite Breakup Model

One SBM record is a single on-orbit fragmentation event — an explosion or
a collision — together with the debris population a breakup model produced
for it. It carries the model inputs (parent states, masses, relative
velocity, object class, cutoff, seed) so the population is reproducible,
and the resulting fragments in FRAGMENTS.

Units on the wire: parent and fragment position are KILOMETERS, parent and
fragment velocity are KILOMETERS PER SECOND (matching $OMM, $OEM, $OCM and
$CDM state conventions); ejection delta-V, relative velocity and
characteristic length are METERS PER SECOND and METERS respectively
(matching the breakup-model literature). Every field name states its unit.

This record describes an ON-ORBIT breakup. Atmospheric reentry breakup and
demise stay in $RDM/$REM; a business-loss classification of the event stays
in $OOE.

CREATION_DATE.description: Message creation date in ISO 8601 UTC format.

OBJECT_CLASS.description: Parent object class used to select model coefficients.

EPOCH.description:
Event epoch in ISO 8601 UTC format. Fragment states are given at this
epoch.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used by all epochs.

REF_FRAME.description: Reference frame for all position, velocity and delta-V components.

OBJECT_ID.description: Target international designator or producer object identifier.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
Target satellite catalog number. Joins to CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID and
OMM.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

IMPACTOR_OBJECT_NAME.description: Impactor object name. COLLISION events only.

IMPACTOR_NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Impactor satellite catalog number. COLLISION events only. 0 when unbound.

IMPACTOR_MASS_KG.description: Impactor mass in kilograms. COLLISION events only.

IMPACTOR_L_C_M.description: Impactor characteristic length in meters. COLLISION events only.

RELATIVE_VELOCITY_M_PER_S.description: Collision relative velocity in meters per second. COLLISION events only.

CATASTROPHIC.description:
True when the collision energy-to-mass ratio met the catastrophic
threshold and both bodies were fully fragmented.

PARENT_POSITION_X_KM.description: Parent position X component in kilometers at EPOCH.

PARENT_POSITION_Y_KM.description: Parent position Y component in kilometers at EPOCH.

PARENT_POSITION_Z_KM.description: Parent position Z component in kilometers at EPOCH.

PARENT_VELOCITY_X_KM_PER_S.description: Parent velocity X component in kilometers per second at EPOCH.

PARENT_VELOCITY_Y_KM_PER_S.description: Parent velocity Y component in kilometers per second at EPOCH.

PARENT_VELOCITY_Z_KM_PER_S.description: Parent velocity Z component in kilometers per second at EPOCH.

MIN_LC_M.description:
Lower characteristic-length cutoff in meters. Fragments smaller than
this were not generated.

SEED.description:
Random number generator seed. A producer that reports the same
MODEL_NAME, MODEL_VERSION, inputs and SEED must reproduce FRAGMENTS
exactly.

FRAGMENT_COUNT.description:
Number of fragments generated. Equals the length of FRAGMENTS when the
population is carried in this record.

INPUT_MASS_KG.description: Total parent mass fed to the model in kilograms.

OUTPUT_MASS_KG.description: Total mass carried by the generated fragments in kilograms.

NCDSegmentDescriptor.description:
One independently addressed segment inside a native container.

A segmented binary ephemeris is not a single span: each segment has its own
body pair, frame, numeric type and time bounds, and a reader must choose
among them. $OEM carries the STATES; this carries the segment DESCRIPTOR
that says which states came from where and what must be written back.

NAME.description: Segment name as recorded in the container.

TARGET_NAIF_ID.description: Integer body code of the segment target.

CENTER_NAIF_ID.description: Integer body code of the segment centre.

FRAME_NAIF_ID.description: Integer reference frame code of the segment.

FRAME_NAME.description: Reference frame name as recorded in the container.

SEGMENT_TYPE.description:
Numeric segment data type, verbatim. The evaluation rule is a property of
this number (for example, Chebyshev position with fixed interval, or
discrete states with Lagrange interpolation); it is carried as the
container's own integer so a rewrite is exact.

START_SECONDS_PAST_J2000_TDB.description:
Segment coverage start, seconds past J2000 in the barycentric dynamical
time scale, as stored in the container.

INITIAL_ADDRESS.description: First addressed element of the segment inside the file.

FINAL_ADDRESS.description: Last addressed element of the segment inside the file.

POLYNOMIAL_DEGREE.description:
Polynomial degree or record size the segment type parameterises, when the
type carries one.

NCDSP3Header.description: Header block of a fixed-column satellite position container (SP3).

FILE_TYPE.description:
Record content indicator, e.g. "P" for positions only, "V" with
velocities.

SATELLITE_SYSTEM.description: Satellite system indicator recorded in the header.

ORBIT_TYPE.description: Orbit type as recorded, e.g. fitted, extrapolated, broadcast, helmert.

DATA_USED.description: Data used to produce the file, as recorded.

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Terrestrial reference frame name as recorded.

AGENCY.description:
Producing agency as recorded IN THE FILE. This is observed content, not a
classification.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system as recorded in the header.

GPS_WEEK.description: Week number of the first epoch in the file's own week counter.

SECONDS_OF_WEEK.description: Seconds of week of the first epoch.

MODIFIED_JULIAN_DAY_START.description: Modified Julian Day of the first epoch.

FRACTIONAL_DAY.description: Fractional day of the first epoch.

NUMBER_OF_EPOCHS.description: Number of epochs declared in the header.

SATELLITE_ACCURACY_EXPONENTS.description:
Per-satellite accuracy exponents, parallel to SATELLITE_IDS. The accuracy
is POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE raised to this power.

POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE.description:
Base for the position and velocity standard-deviation exponents carried
per state in $OEM.

CLOCK_RATE_BASE.description: Base for the clock bias and clock rate standard-deviation exponents.

COMMENT.description: Header comment lines in file order.

NCDScenarioEpochContainer.description: Parameters of a scenario-epoch text container.

SCENARIO_EPOCH.description: Epoch that every record offset is measured from, ISO 8601.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time scale the scenario epoch is expressed in.

DISTANCE_UNIT.description: Distance unit of the records, e.g. "Meters", "Kilometers".

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Named coordinate system of the records.

COORDINATE_AXES.description: Named coordinate axes, when stated separately from the system.

INTERPOLATION_SAMPLES_M1.description:
Interpolation order expressed as (samples - 1), which is how these
containers state it. Carried verbatim rather than converted, so a rewrite
reproduces the source exactly.

NUMBER_OF_EPHEMERIS_POINTS.description: Number of ephemeris points declared in the container.

SEGMENT_BOUNDARY_TIMES.description: Segment boundary offsets in seconds from SCENARIO_EPOCH, when present.

NCDCode500Header.description: Header words of a fixed-record binary ephemeris container.

SATELLITE_NAME.description: Object name as recorded in the header.

EPOCH_STEP_SECONDS.description: Uniform step between data records, seconds.

HEADER_WORDS.description:
The header record's packed words in file order, undecoded. A reader that
understands a word decodes it; a rewriter reproduces the record exactly
without having to.

NCD.description:
Native Container Descriptor.

The file-level facts of an ephemeris, attitude or tracking container that
are NOT properties of the messages inside it. $OEM, $AEM and $TDM carry the
states, attitudes and observations; none of them can carry the internal
file name, the comment area, the segment address ranges, the header accuracy
block or the interpolation order the source declared, because those describe
the CONTAINER. Without them a read-then-write cycle silently invents header
values, and a segmented binary file cannot be reproduced at all.

ONE record covers every container class rather than one record per format:
the file-level facts are the same kind of fact in each, and the
format-specific blocks are optional sub-tables selected by FORMAT. Only the
block matching FORMAT is populated.

PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME.description: Format name when FORMAT is PROVIDER_DEFINED. Empty otherwise.

FORMAT_VERSION.description: Version of the container format as declared by the file itself.

PRODUCER.description: Producing system or organization as recorded IN THE FILE.

CREATION_DATE.description: Creation date recorded in the file, ISO 8601.

INTERNAL_FILE_NAME.description:
Container-internal file name, which is stored inside the file and is
independent of the name on disk.

COMMENT_AREA.description:
Free-text comment area carried inside the container, one entry per line,
in file order.

NATIVE_FRAME_NAME.description:
Reference frame name as the container itself spells it, before any
mapping onto $RFM.

NATIVE_FRAME_ID.description: Integer reference frame code as the container stores it.

NATIVE_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system as the container itself spells it, before any mapping onto
the ratified time-scale vocabulary.

SEGMENTS.description:
Descriptors of the container's segments, in file order. Empty for a
single-span container.

SP3_HEADER.description: Header block when FORMAT is SP3_C or SP3_D.

SCENARIO_CONTAINER.description:
Parameters when FORMAT is SCENARIO_EPOCH_EPHEMERIS_TEXT or
SCENARIO_EPOCH_ATTITUDE_TEXT.

CODE_500_HEADER.description: Header words when FORMAT is CODE_500.

START_TIME.description: Total coverage start across all segments, ISO 8601.

STOP_TIME.description: Total coverage stop across all segments, ISO 8601.

SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH.description: Length of the described container in bytes.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the described container's exact bytes, lowercase hex. This is
what makes the descriptor checkable: a consumer can prove the descriptor
belongs to the file it holds.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier of the described container when it is addressed by
content rather than by path.

GST.description:
Ground/Tracking Station Definition — the geodetic identity and geometry of
one tracking station, sufficient to reduce a radiometric or laser
observation taken from it.

This is deliberately NOT $SEN. $SEN describes an SSA sensor site by
latitude/longitude/altitude with tasking plans and statistics; it carries no
terrestrial frame realization, no station velocity, no reference epoch, and
no antenna axis geometry. Station coordinates without a frame realization
and an epoch cannot be propagated for plate motion and are therefore not
usable for orbit determination.

STATION_ID.description: Stable station identifier as used by the operating network, e.g. "DSS-63".

DOMES_NUMBER.description: IERS DOMES number, when the station has one.

CDP_NUMBER.description: NASA CDP / SLR site number, when the station has one.

FRAME_REALIZATION.description: Terrestrial reference frame realization of POSITION_* and VELOCITY_*.

FRAME_REALIZATION_NAME.description: Free-text realization name, required when FRAME_REALIZATION is OTHER.

REFERENCE_EPOCH.description:
Epoch at which POSITION_* is valid, ISO 8601. Positions MUST be
propagated to the observation epoch with VELOCITY_* before use.

POSITION_X.description: Station position in the stated realization, metres.

VELOCITY_X.description:
Station velocity (plate motion) in the stated realization, metres per
year. Zero is a claim that the station does not move, not a default.

AXIS_OFFSET_M.description:
Distance between the two mount axes, metres. Zero for an intersecting-axis
mount.

ECCENTRICITY_X.description: Vector from the monument marker to the antenna reference point, metres.

ECCENTRICITY_FRAME.description:
Frame the eccentricity vector is expressed in, e.g. "XYZ" (geocentric
Cartesian) or "NEU" (local north-east-up).

TRANSMIT_BANDS.description: Uplink bands the station can transmit, e.g. ["S", "X", "Ka"].

RECEIVE_BANDS.description: Downlink bands the station can receive.

CLOCK_OFFSET_S.description: Station clock offset from the stated time scale, seconds.

CLOCK_RATE_S_PER_S.description: Station clock rate, seconds per second.

CLOCK_TIME_SCALE.description: Time scale the clock terms are referenced to, e.g. "UTC", "TAI".

VALID_FROM.description: Start of the interval over which this definition applies, ISO 8601.

VALID_TO.description: End of the interval over which this definition applies, ISO 8601.

SOURCE.description:
Provenance of these coordinates, e.g. "DSN 810-005 rev. E", an ILRS SINEX
file name, or a VLBI station catalogue identifier.

BEMProvenance.description: Provenance of a deployed-beam descriptor or hop schedule.

BEMHopSlot.description: One time slice of a periodic beam-hopping plan.

BEAM_ID.description:
Beam activated in this slot. May name this BEM.ID or another beam in a
coordinated schedule.

BEMHopSchedule.description: Periodic beam-hopping schedule carried by a deployed beam descriptor.

EPOCH.description: Seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC at which slot offsets begin.

GAIN.description: Gain level in dBi at this contour

EIRP.description: EIRP at beam center in dBW

G_OVER_T.description: G/T at beam center in dB/K

HOP_SCHEDULE.description: Time-sliced activation plan for this deployed beam.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this record was serialized.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over the size-prefixed FlatBuffer with both 64-byte
signature payloads zeroed while preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over canonical JSON with IDL field order and
capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both signature fields
omitted.

CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation name

RFB.description:
RF Band Specification

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE. Every frequency field in this table is MHz. Sources
that publish Hz (as open transmitter databases commonly do) MUST divide by
1e6 before encoding; sources
that publish kHz MUST divide by 1e3. BAUD is baud (symbols per second),
never kilobaud. Encoding a Hz value into a MHz field is a defect, not a
convention.

One RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION. A transceiver or
transponder is therefore represented as TWO RFB records — one UPLINK and
one DOWNLINK — sharing ID_TRANSMITTER, each carrying its own MODE,
FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and CENTER_FREQ.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalog number of the spacecraft carrying this emitter. Joins to
CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

ID_TRANSMITTER.description:
Identifier of the physical transmitter, transceiver or transponder this
record describes (e.g. an upstream transmitter database's UUID). Uplink
and downlink
records of the same device share this value.

LINK_DIRECTION.description: Direction of this emission relative to the spacecraft.

BAUD.description: Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud.

SERVICE.description: Regulatory/ITU service designation (e.g. Amateur, Earth Exploration).

INVERT.description: True when the modulation sideband is inverted.

IARU_COORDINATION.description: IARU frequency-coordination state (e.g. IARU Coordinated, Uncoordinated).

CITATION.description:
Attribution/citation string the source license requires this record to
carry downstream.

TIMCcsdsTimeCode.description: CCSDS time-code payload and preamble metadata.

PREAMBLE_FIELD2.description: Second CCSDS preamble field octet; ignored when not signaled by preamble 1.

AGENCY_DEFINED_EPOCH_ISO8601.description: Optional agency-defined epoch timestamp for agency epoch time codes.

CCSDS_EPOCH_ISO8601.description: Optional CCSDS epoch override timestamp; defaults to 1958-01-01T00:00:00 TAI.

TIMInstant.description: Numeric or textual instant tagged with its time system and representation.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system for this instant.

EPOCH_FORMAT.description: Interpretation of JULIAN_DATE, SECONDS, and ISO8601.

JULIAN_DATE.description: Julian Date or Modified Julian Date day value, selected by EPOCH_FORMAT.

SECONDS.description: Seconds for UNIX_SECONDS, GPS_SECONDS, GNSS_WEEK_SECONDS, or MISSION_ELAPSED_SECONDS.

ISO8601.description: ISO 8601 timestamp text for ISO8601 inputs or display outputs.

SUBSECOND_NANOS.description: Additional nanoseconds beyond the fractional scalar/text value.

EPOCH_LABEL.description: Optional application-defined epoch label for MET, MRT, or SCLK values.

GNSS_WEEK.description: GNSS week number when EPOCH_FORMAT is GNSS_WEEK_SECONDS.

GNSS_ROLLOVER_REFERENCE_ISO8601.description: Optional Orekit-style GNSS week rollover reference timestamp.

CCSDS_TIME_CODE.description: CCSDS time-code payload when EPOCH_FORMAT is CCSDS_TIME_CODE.

TIMConversionRequest.description: Request to convert one instant into another time system/representation.

TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS.description: Optional TAI-UTC override in seconds for the source instant.

HAS_TAI_MINUS_UTC.description: Whether TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS should override runtime leap-second data.

DUT1_SECONDS.description: Optional UT1-UTC override in seconds for UT1 conversions.

HAS_DUT1.description: Whether DUT1_SECONDS should override runtime Earth-orientation data.

TRACE_ID.description: Optional caller trace/correlation identifier.

TIMConversionResult.description: Result of a time conversion request.

DELTA_SECONDS.description: Target minus source offset in SI seconds for the requested conversion.

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Optional error detail when STATUS is not OK.

TRACE_ID.description: Caller trace/correlation identifier copied from the request when present.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Legacy time-system selector retained for existing TIM consumers.

RFLObstruction.description:
One obstacle interaction on one sample's path. SPARSE: entries exist only
where an interaction was computed, so a clear path is never encoded as a
row of zeroes.

This is the join that makes an arbitrary 3D object a first-class part of
the link budget: MATERIAL_ID names the `$RFS` record whose permittivity,
conductivity, penetration loss and roughness produced LOSS_DB, and
GEOMETRY_REF_ID names the exact mesh, face set, panel or analytic shape
inside it that was hit.

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this interaction applies to.

OBSTACLE_ID.description: Producer's identifier for the obstacle instance.

MATERIAL_ID.description:
`$RFS.MATERIAL_ID` of the surface that was hit. An obstruction loss with
no material is an unattributed number: a metal panel and a plasterboard
wall of the same size do entirely different things to a link.

VAM_ID.description:
`$VAM` asset identity of the obstacle mesh, when the obstacle is a
reviewed 3D asset.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the obstacle is a catalogued object (an
occulting spacecraft, a structure on another vehicle). 0 when unbound.

INCIDENCE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Angle between the incident ray and the surface normal, degrees [0-90).

PATH_LENGTH_IN_MATERIAL_M.description:
Path length travelled INSIDE the material, metres. With
`$RFS.ATTENUATION_DB_PER_M` this is what makes penetration loss
reproducible instead of a stated constant.

EXCESS_DELAY_S.description: Extra propagation delay of a reflected or scattered component, seconds.

FRESNEL_CLEARANCE_FRACTION.description:
Fraction of the first Fresnel zone still clear [0-1]. 1 means the zone is
untouched.

DISTANCE_FROM_TRANSMITTER_M.description: Distance from the transmitter to the interaction point, metres.

RFLEndpoint.description:
One endpoint of a link. Identity ONLY — position, antenna geometry and band
capability are NOT copied here; they are joined from the standard named by
ENDPOINT_KIND. A copied position silently goes stale against its source.

ENDPOINT_ID.description: Producer-stable identifier for this endpoint within the record.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the endpoint is an on-orbit object. 0 when
unbound — never a placeholder catalogue number.

OBJECT_ID.description: International designator, `$CAT.OBJECT_ID`.

RFB_ID.description:
`$RFB.ID` — the band specification (frequency, bandwidth, EIRP, gains,
polarization) this endpoint transmits or receives on.

RFE_ID.description: `$RFE.ID` — the parametric emitter description, when one exists.

IQC_ID.description: `$IQC` capture identifier, when the samples were derived from a recording.

CHANNEL_ID.description: Channel or carrier identifier within the beam.

POLARIZATION.description:
Polarization actually used on this link. Defaults to UNKNOWN explicitly:
`rfPolarization` ordinal 0 is LHCP, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as a real polarization.

RFLModCod.description:
One modulation-and-coding choice available to a link. The table carries
engineering capability only; catalogue or recommendation names belong in
ID / NAME and provenance data, never in the schema vocabulary.

MODCOD_ID.description: Stable identifier within the containing link's MODCOD_SET.

CODE_RATE.description: Information bits divided by coded bits, in (0,1].

REQUIRED_MARGIN_DB.description: Additional implementation margin required before this entry is selected.

MAXIMUM_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Optional ceiling imposed by framing or implementation, bits per second.

RFLLink.description: One link whose budget is sampled by this record.

LINK_ID.description:
Producer-stable link identifier. Joins `$ACI.ACIInterval.LINK_ID` and
`$LKS.ID` when the same link also has an operational-state record.

CENTER_FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Carrier centre frequency actually used, megahertz — the `$RFB` MHz
convention, NOT the `$IQC` hertz convention. A consumer joining the two
converts explicitly at the join. Band designation is NOT duplicated here:
it is joined from `$RFB.BAND`.

MODULATION.description: Modulation as the producer states it (e.g. "QPSK", "8PSK", "16APSK").

CODING.description: Forward error correction scheme as the producer states it.

CODE_RATE.description: Code rate as a fraction (0-1].

SYMBOL_RATE_BAUD.description:
Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud — the `$RFB.BAUD`
convention.

DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Information bit rate the budget is stated for, bits per second.

THRESHOLD_TERM.description:
Required threshold this link is evaluated against. THRESHOLD_TERM,
THRESHOLD_VALUE, THRESHOLD_UNITS and THRESHOLD_COMPARISON are meaningful
only together; a LINK_MARGIN_DB column without them states a margin
against an unstated requirement and MUST be refused.

RECEIVER_GROUP_ID.description:
Receiver group this link belongs to. Links sharing a RECEIVER_GROUP_ID
and CHANNEL_GROUP_ID are mutually interfering and MUST be evaluated
together; a producer that shards a link matrix MUST keep a group intact
within one shard.

CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation or network this link belongs to.

SERVICE.description: Operator-facing service or mission designation.

MODCOD_SET.description:
Ordered adaptive modulation-and-coding choices. Per-sample
SELECTED_MODCOD_INDEX indexes this vector for the sample's selected link.

ACM_ENABLED.description: Whether the producer evaluated adaptive selection for this link.

RFLInterferenceContribution.description:
One interfering contribution to one sample. SPARSE: entries exist only
where a contribution was computed, so a dense matrix is never forced into
existence to say "no interference computed".

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this contribution applies to.

SOURCE_ENDPOINT_ID.description:
Endpoint identifier of the interfering emitter, when it is an endpoint of
this record.

RFB_ID.description: `$RFB.ID` of the interfering emission.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Interfering object's catalogue number, 0 when unbound.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Received interfering power at the victim receiver, dBW.

TOPOCENTRIC_SEPARATION_DEG.description:
Angular separation between the wanted and interfering paths at the
victim receiver, degrees.

SPECTRAL_OVERLAP_FRACTION.description: Fraction of the victim's bandwidth overlapped by this emission [0-1].

POLARIZATION_ISOLATION_DB.description: Polarization isolation applied to this contribution, dB.

ANTENNA_DISCRIMINATION_DB.description: Discrimination applied from the victim antenna pattern, dB.

RFLModelParameter.description:
A named parameter of a model binding, with its unit stated. There is no
encoding for a parameter value without a unit.

TEXT_VALUE.description: Non-numeric parameter value, when the parameter is categorical.

RFLModelBinding.description:
Which model produced one term of the budget. A loss term without a model
binding is an unattributed number: rain attenuation from two different
recommendations differs by decibels, and a consumer must be able to tell
which one it is holding.

TERM.description: The budget term this binding produced.

MODEL_NAME.description:
Model or recommendation identifier as its publisher states it (e.g. an
ITU-R recommendation number with its revision).

MODULE_ID.description: `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` of the module that evaluated it.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact artifact that produced the values.

RFLProvenance.description: Where this sample set came from, stated once for the record.

SOURCE.description:
The producing system, dataset or measurement campaign. Required: a
budget time series with no stated source is not publishable.

SOURCE_QUERY.description: Replayable query or scenario reference that regenerates this set.

PROPAGATOR_ID.description:
Identifier of the propagator that produced the geometry columns. A record
whose METHOD is MODELED or HYBRID and which carries geometry columns MUST
name it: geometry is only as good as the propagator, and the propagator is
a pluggable choice, never an assumed default.

PROPAGATOR_CONFIGURATION.description: Force model or configuration identifier handed to the propagator.

SAMPLING_STEP_S.description: Uniform sampling step, seconds. Absent when SAMPLE_EPOCHS are irregular.

ENVIRONMENT_DATASET.description:
Weather or environment dataset the atmospheric terms were evaluated
against, when they were not evaluated against a statistical model.

TERRAIN_DATASET.description: Terrain or surface dataset the blockage terms were evaluated against.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this set was computed or recorded.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: Unix ms the upstream inputs were retrieved.

LICENSE.description:
Licence the source imposes on redistribution. An empty LICENSE means
UNKNOWN TERMS — never public domain, never a grant to redistribute.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: True when the licence forbids commercial use of this set.

CITATION.description: Attribution the licence requires this record to carry downstream.

MODULE_ID.description:
Primary `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` that produced this record.
MODELS remains the per-budget-term attribution surface.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact producing WASM artifact.

RFL_ID.description: Stable identifier of this sample set.

SCENARIO_ID.description:
Analysis or scenario grouping identifier shared with the `$ACI` and
`$CVP` products derived from this set.

LINKS.description: Link definitions. SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES index into this vector.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description:
Number of samples. Every present metric array MUST have exactly this
many entries.

SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES.description: Index into LINKS for each sample.

SAMPLE_EPOCHS.description:
Sample epochs, seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 in TIME_SYSTEM. Samples
need not be uniformly spaced and need not be grouped by link, but MUST be
non-decreasing within each link.

TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time scale SAMPLE_EPOCHS are expressed in. Defaults to UTC explicitly:
`timingStandard` ordinal 0 is GMST, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as sidereal time.

RANGE_RATE_M_S.description: Range rate, metres per second; positive is opening.

AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the receiving endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the receiving endpoint, degrees above the local horizon.

TRANSMIT_AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the transmitting endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

TRANSMIT_ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the transmitting endpoint, degrees.

DOPPLER_SHIFT_HZ.description:
Doppler shift of the carrier, hertz; positive is closing. Hertz, not the
MHz used for frequencies elsewhere in this record — a shift of a few kHz
on a GHz carrier is destroyed by an MHz encoding.

EIRP_DBW.description: Effective isotropic radiated power toward the receiver, dBW.

TRANSMIT_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Transmit antenna gain in the direction of the receiver, dBi.

RECEIVE_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Receive antenna gain in the direction of the transmitter, dBi.

GASEOUS_ABSORPTION_LOSS_DB.description: Gaseous (oxygen and water vapour) absorption, dB.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS_DB.description:
Total loss from 3D obstacles on the path, dB. The per-obstacle detail —
which object, which material, at what angle, through how much of it — is
in OBSTRUCTIONS.

TOTAL_PATH_LOSS_DB.description:
Total of all path terms actually applied, dB. Published as its own column
rather than left to the consumer to sum: a producer that applied a term
this schema has no column for MUST still report an honest total, and the
discrepancy against the itemised columns is then visible.

RECEIVED_POWER_DBW.description: Received carrier power at the receiver input, dBW.

GAIN_TO_NOISE_TEMPERATURE_DB_PER_K.description: Receiving system figure of merit G/T, dB/K.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_DB.description: Carrier-to-noise ratio C/N in the occupied bandwidth, dB.

ENERGY_PER_BIT_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Energy per bit to noise density Eb/N0, dB.

BIT_ERROR_RATE.description:
Bit error rate as a probability [0-1], NOT an exponent and NOT a
percentage. 1e-6 is encoded 1e-6.

LINK_MARGIN_DB.description:
Link margin against the link's stated threshold, dB. Meaningless without
RFLLink.THRESHOLD_TERM / THRESHOLD_VALUE / THRESHOLD_COMPARISON.

CHANNEL_CAPACITY_BPS.description: Achievable channel capacity, bits per second.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Aggregate received interfering power, dBW.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_PLUS_INTERFERENCE_DB.description: Carrier to noise-plus-interference ratio C/(N+I), dB.

OBSTRUCTIONS.description:
Per-interaction obstacle detail, sparse. Each entry names the `$RFS`
material it went through, reflected off or was blocked by.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS.description: The single condition that bound the link at each sample.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINT_NOTE.description: Verbatim description required when a LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS entry is OTHER.

PROVENANCE.description:
Provenance of the whole set. Required: an unattributed budget is not
publishable.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this record was serialized.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the producing `$EPM` over the size-prefixed
FlatBuffer projection with both 64-byte signature payloads zeroed while
preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the producing `$EPM` over canonical JSON with IDL
field order, IDL capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both
signature fields omitted.

SELECTED_MODCOD_INDEX.description:
Index into the selected link's RFLLink.MODCOD_SET for each sample.
SELECTED_MODCOD_VALID distinguishes index 0 from no selection.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY_BPS_HZ.description: Spectral efficiency delivered by the selected entry, bit/s/Hz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Delivered information rate after adaptive selection, bits per second.

ACM_MARGIN_DB.description: Margin above the selected entry's threshold, dB.

ENERGY_PER_SYMBOL_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Symbol energy to noise spectral density, dB.

EXCEEDANCE_PERCENT.description:
Percent of time a loss value is exceeded, in descending or ascending
order as stated by PROVENANCE. Every curve below has this length.

XPD_DB.description: Cross-polarization discrimination at each exceedance percentage, dB.

WORST_MONTH_EXCEEDANCE_PERCENT.description: Exceedance percentage used for the worst-month summary.

AVAILABILITY_PERCENT.description: Percentage of the analysis window meeting the stated link requirement.

OUTAGE_MINUTES_PER_YEAR.description: Annualized minutes not meeting the stated link requirement.

WORST_MONTH_OUTAGE_MINUTES.description: Worst-month outage minutes for the analysis window's month length.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over the size-prefixed FlatBuffer with both 64-byte
signature payloads zeroed while preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over canonical JSON with IDL field order and
capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both signature fields
omitted.

ESL.description:
Entity / Standards Link — join-table row connecting a host-local entity
metadata record to a standards record index row, enabling cascade-safe
mutation and cross-plugin query ownership.

LINK_KEY.description: Stable local link key for one entity / record association.

ENTITY_ID.description: Stable host-local entity id on the entity side of the association.

ENTITY_RECORD_KEY.description: Stable local entity metadata record key (for example `ENTITY:<id>`).

ENTITY_ROWID.description: FlatSQL row id for the linked entity metadata row when known.

RECORD_KEY.description: Stable local standards record key on the record side of the association.

SCHEMA_NAME.description: SDS schema family for the linked record (`OMM`, `CAT`, `OEM`, `CDM`, etc.).

RECORD_ROWID.description: FlatSQL row id for the linked standards record row when known.

CASCADE_DELETE.description: Whether entity deletion should cascade to the linked standards record.

UPDATED_AT_MS.description: Milliseconds since epoch when the association was last refreshed.

CPS.description:
Compressed Packet Stream — a run of fixed-length CCSDS packets losslessly
compressed as one stateful stream (CCSDS 124.0-B-1 POCKET+). Decoded output
is a sequence of PACKET_COUNT packets of PACKET_LENGTH bytes, each of which
projects to an $SPP record. This record carries a compressed packet stream
only; it is not a general-purpose compression envelope for SDS records.

ALGORITHM.description: Compression algorithm used to produce COMPRESSED_DATA.

PACKET_LENGTH.description:
Uncompressed length in bytes of EVERY packet in the stream. POCKET+ is
defined only for a fixed packet length; a length change starts a new
stream and therefore a new $CPS record.

PACKET_COUNT.description:
Number of uncompressed packets encoded in COMPRESSED_DATA. NORMATIVE:
this is the only output-size bound a decoder has. The compressed
bitstream alone does not bound the decoded size, and a compression-ratio
guess is unsafe in both directions. Decoders MUST reject a record whose
PACKET_COUNT is zero, and MUST allocate exactly
PACKET_COUNT * PACKET_LENGTH bytes of output.

ROBUSTNESS.description:
POCKET+ robustness level: the window depth in PACKETS, range 0-7. This is
a window depth, NOT a retransmission interval — it does not by itself
configure a decoder. See MASK_UPDATE_PERIOD / MASK_SEND_PERIOD /
REFERENCE_PERIOD, which are three independent periods.

MASK_UPDATE_PERIOD.description:
POCKET+ mask update period (pt), in packets. Independent of ROBUSTNESS,
MASK_SEND_PERIOD, and REFERENCE_PERIOD.

MASK_SEND_PERIOD.description:
POCKET+ mask send period (ft), in packets — how often the change mask is
transmitted. Independent of ROBUSTNESS, MASK_UPDATE_PERIOD, and
REFERENCE_PERIOD.

REFERENCE_PERIOD.description:
POCKET+ reference packet retransmission period (rt), in packets.
Independent of ROBUSTNESS, MASK_UPDATE_PERIOD, and MASK_SEND_PERIOD.

SELF_SYNCHRONIZING.description:
True only when the FIRST packet of COMPRESSED_DATA carries both rt=1 and
ft=1, i.e. it transmits a full reference packet and a full mask, so this
record decodes standalone without its predecessor. There is no
synchronization flag in the POCKET+ bitstream itself: this field is the
producer's assertion about the first packet, and defaults to false.

STREAM_ID.description:
Producer-defined stream identity. Records sharing STREAM_ID decode in
SEGMENT_INDEX order as one continuous POCKET+ stream. A missing segment
poisons every subsequent segment up to the next segment with
SELF_SYNCHRONIZING = true.

SEGMENT_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of this segment within STREAM_ID.

APID.description: CCSDS Application Process Identifier of the packets, when known.

SPACECRAFT_ID.description: Spacecraft identifier of the packets, when known.

START_EPOCH.description: UTC epoch of the first packet in the segment, ISO 8601.

STOP_EPOCH.description: UTC epoch of the last packet in the segment, ISO 8601.

COMPRESSED_DATA.description:
The POCKET+ compressed bitstream per CCSDS 124.0-B-1. Each compressed
packet is individually octet-aligned; padding is per PACKET, never per
stream. Bit-concatenating packets diverges from the reference
implementation and MUST NOT be done.

UNCOMPRESSED_LENGTH.description:
PACKET_LENGTH * PACKET_COUNT. Carried so a decoder can check its decoded
output length without recomputing the product from a corrupt header.

UNCOMPRESSED_CRC32.description: CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3) over the concatenated decompressed packets.

SHCVariableTerm.description:
One time-variable coefficient term: a rate or a periodic variation applied
to the static coefficient at DEGREE/ORDER.

C_VALUE.description: Coefficient of the variation for the cosine (C) and sine (S) terms.

PERIOD_YEARS.description: Period of a periodic term, years. Unused for a trend.

REFERENCE_EPOCH.description: Epoch the term is referenced to, ISO 8601.

SHC.description:
Spherical-Harmonic Coefficient Set — an actual gravity field, as opposed to
the NAME of one.

This is deliberately NOT $GRV. $GRV is a model SELECTOR: it names a model,
bounds its degree/order, toggles third-body and tidal effects, and carries
scalar J2..J6. It cannot carry a coefficient set, and a named model without
its coefficients is not interchange — it is a citation.

Coefficients are carried as four parallel arrays of equal length, indexed
together: entry i is the coefficient at DEGREES[i], ORDERS[i] with cosine
term C[i] and sine term S[i]. Parallel arrays rather than a table per
coefficient because a 200x200 field is ~40,000 coefficients and a
table-per-coefficient encoding is pathological in both size and decode cost.

MODEL_NAME.description: Identifier of the coefficient set, e.g. "EGM2008", "GGGRX1200".

CENTRAL_BODY_NAIF_ID.description:
Body the field describes, as a NAIF integer ID (399 = Earth, 301 = Moon,
499 = Mars). NAIF ID is normative; BODY_NAME is advisory. Note that a
barycenter (e.g. 4) is NOT the body (e.g. 499).

GM.description:
Gravitational parameter of the body, m^3/s^2. Part of the set: a field's
coefficients are only meaningful with the GM they were solved against.

REFERENCE_RADIUS.description: Reference radius of the expansion, metres. Also part of the set.

MAX_DEGREE.description: Maximum degree and order present in the arrays.

NORMALIZATION.description:
Normalization convention. A set published without this is unusable;
consumers MUST reject UNSPECIFIED rather than assuming a convention.

PERMANENT_TIDE_SYSTEM.description:
Permanent-tide system. Consumers MUST reject UNSPECIFIED for any
application sensitive at the 1e-9 level in C20.

REFERENCE_EPOCH.description:
Epoch the static coefficients are referenced to, ISO 8601. Required when
VARIABLE_TERMS is present.

DEGREES.description:
Parallel coefficient arrays. DEGREES, ORDERS, C and S MUST have identical
lengths; a record where they do not is invalid.

C_SIGMA.description: Optional 1-sigma uncertainties, parallel to C and S when present.

VARIABLE_TERMS.description: Optional time-variable terms applied on top of the static field.

SOURCE.description:
Tide-free/zero-tide conversion already applied, publication reference, or
any other provenance needed to reproduce the set.

CITATION.description: Citation for the field, e.g. the paper or data-centre DOI.

CryptoKey.description:
Represents cryptographic key information.

The publication paradigm is "literal public keys, not derivation
material": a published EPM carries the PUBLIC_KEY bytes that verify
the record's SIGNATURE (signing) or encrypt to the entity (encryption),
and NOTHING about how those keys were derived. XPUB, KEY_PATH and
KEY_ADDRESS are PRIVATE / operational — they belong to the wallet that
produced the keys, never to the record a peer resolves.

Requiredness is PROFILE-ENFORCED, never a flatc `(required)` attribute:
a `(required)` on PUBLIC_KEY would make the flatbuffers Verifier reject
every pre-flip secp256k1 record that legitimately omitted it (the
2026-07-27 dual-curve regime allowed xpub-derivation for secp at
non-hardened paths). A published record is self-describing instead —
PUBLIC_KEY present, XPUB/KEY_PATH/KEY_ADDRESS absent — and a conformance
checker asserts that profile (see scripts/check-epm-published-profile.mjs).

Rotation is by republish: a new signing or encryption key means a new
PUBLIC_KEY, a re-signed SIGNATURE, and a re-published EPM at the same
peer-addressed location. The PeerID (multihash of the libp2p identity
pubkey) is the stable anchor across rotations.

PUBLIC_KEY.description:
Public part of the cryptographic key, in hexadecimal format. AUTHORITATIVE
in a published record: this is the verifying/encrypting key, and no other
field yields it. Required-in-practice (profile-enforced, not flatc
`(required)`) so that pre-flip secp256k1 records without it still decode.

XPUB.description:
Extended public key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic
wallets), "Extended keys". PRIVATE / operational: present only in the
wallet that derived the keys, ABSENT from published records. A verifier
never derives a child key from XPUB — the PUBLIC_KEY is the verification
material.

PRIVATE_KEY.description: Private part of the cryptographic key in hexidecimal format, should be kept secret

XPRIV.description: Extended private key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic wallets), "Extended keys".

KEY_ADDRESS.description:
Address generated from the cryptographic key. PRIVATE / operational in a
published EPM: a chain address is bound through a ChainProof attestation,
not carried as a standalone KEY_ADDRESS on the CryptoKey. ABSENT from
published records.

ADDRESS_TYPE.description:
Type of the address generated from the cryptographic key. An address
format tag only — NOT a curve or algorithm designator; the algorithm
lives in ALGORITHM

KEY_TYPE.description: Type of the cryptographic key (signing or encryption)

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of this key from the entity root
(e.g., "m/44'/0'/0'/0/0" secp256k1 non-hardened, "m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'"
ed25519 hardened). PRIVATE / operational: how the key was derived belongs
to the wallet, not to a published record. ABSENT from published records.

ALGORITHM.description:
Key algorithm/curve (e.g., "ed25519", "secp256k1"). ABSENT means
ed25519: every record published before this field existed verifies
unchanged under that default. The verifier dispatches on ALGORITHM (not
on ADDRESS_TYPE, which is an address-format tag only).

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format produced by this key (e.g., "raw-ed25519",
"compact"). ABSENT means the canonical encoding of ALGORITHM
(raw-ed25519 for ed25519, compact for secp256k1)

REGION.description: Region of the address (e.g., state or province)

LOCALITY.description: Locality of the address (e.g., city or town)

ChainProof.description: Proves a blockchain key derives from the same HD wallet as the signing key

KEY_PATH.description: BIP-44 derivation path (e.g., "m/44'/0'/0'/0/0")

SIGNATURE.description: Signature over the attestation payload (hex-encoded)

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed (hex-encoded)

ENCODING.description: Signature encoding format (e.g., "compact", "raw-ed25519")

DomainProof.description:
Proves control of a DNS domain by the same HD wallet as the signing key —
the EPM-record mirror of the DNS TXT wire form (which is deliberately
NON-SDS: a base64 FlatBuffer would not fit a 255-byte TXT record). The
canonical statement is 6 fixed LF-terminated lines prefixed
"sdn-domain-proof/1", and it verifies by BYTE-REPLAY of the verbatim
SIGNED_PAYLOAD (ChainProof precedent) — never by JCS.

DOMAIN.description: Fully-qualified domain name the proof binds (e.g., "node.example.org")

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of the proving key. The signer is the
Ed25519 EPM/publication key at m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'

SIGNATURE.description: Signature over the attestation payload (hex-encoded)

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed, verbatim (hex-encoded)

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format. ABSENT means the canonical encoding of
ALGORITHM (raw-ed25519 for ed25519)

LEGAL_NAME.description: Common name of the entity (person or organization)

FAMILY_NAME.description: Family name or surname of the person

GIVEN_NAME.description: Given name or first name of the person

ADDITIONAL_NAME.description: Additional name or middle name of the person

HONORIFIC_PREFIX.description: Honorific prefix preceding the person's name (e.g., Mr., Dr.)

HONORIFIC_SUFFIX.description: Honorific suffix following the person's name (e.g., Jr., Sr.)

KEYS.description: Cryptographic keys associated with the entity

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Multiformat addresses associated with the entity

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature over canonical EPM content (hex), produced by the entity's
signing key under the algorithm declared in SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM
(absent declaration = Ed25519)

SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the EPM was signed

CHAIN_PROOFS.description: Chain binding proofs linking blockchain keys to the same HD wallet

ENTITY_TYPE.description: Type of entity represented by this profile

SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm that produced SIGNATURE (e.g., "ed25519",
"secp256k1"). ABSENT means ed25519 — this single default is what keeps
every EPM signed before this field existed verifying unchanged, so the
field MUST NOT be made required. The signing key is the first CryptoKey
in KEYS with KEY_TYPE Signing whose ALGORITHM matches this declaration
(an absent CryptoKey.ALGORITHM likewise means ed25519)

DOMAIN_PROOFS.description:
DNS domain binding proofs linking domains to the same HD wallet —
symmetric with CHAIN_PROOFS

CCTCategory.description:
One ratified category in the taxonomy.

DISPLAY_NAME, SUMMARY and SLUG are required: a category cannot be published
without the label a surface will render, the sentence a browse row will
show, and the route a link will target. This is what stops each consumer
from inventing its own wording for the same code.

CODE.description: The ratified category code. This is the join key every consumer uses.

DISPLAY_NAME.description:
Canonical human-readable label, rendered verbatim. MUST equal the display
name stated in the CODE member's doc comment.

SUMMARY.description: One-sentence description shown on browse rows and category headers.

SLUG.description:
Route-safe identifier: the CODE identifier lowercased with `_` replaced by
`-`. Published explicitly rather than derived so every surface routes
identically.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer editorial description for a category landing page.

PARENT.description:
Parent category for hierarchical browse. UNSPECIFIED means this is a
top-level category. A category MUST NOT name itself as its parent.

SORT_ORDER.description:
Presentation order within its parent, ascending. Ties break on
DISPLAY_NAME.

KEYWORDS.description:
Search synonyms and alternate phrasings that resolve to this category.
Feeds type-ahead; never rendered as the category label.

ICON_KEY.description:
Key of a self-hosted icon or capsule asset for this category. A KEY, not a
URL: consuming node surfaces load zero external-origin bytes, so the
consumer resolves this against its own local asset set.

CCTCategoryRollup.description:
An observed count of catalogue items in one category.

Counts are VOLATILE and are never part of the ratified taxonomy itself. A
rollup exists only with COUNTED_AT and SOURCE_CATALOG_ID, so a published
count can never omit when it was taken or what it was taken over. A consumer
that needs a live number computes it from the items; a consumer rendering a
published rollup MUST show it as of COUNTED_AT.

CODE.description: Category being counted.

ITEM_COUNT.description:
Number of catalogue items whose PRIMARY_CATEGORY or CATEGORIES include
CODE, counted over SOURCE_CATALOG_ID at COUNTED_AT.

SOURCE_CATALOG_ID.description: Identifier of the catalogue the count was taken over.

COUNTED_AT.description: Unix seconds when the count was taken.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

TAXONOMY_ID.description: Stable identifier of this taxonomy publication.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:
The ratified categories. Every capabilityClass member a consumer may
encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.

APPModuleRef.description:
One member WASM module of the app. References module identity; never
embeds the module artifact itself (delivery is the module-bundle lane).

ID.description:
App-local stable reference for this module. Required, unique within
the manifest.

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin identifier of the module as published in its plugin listing.

CONTENT_HASH.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the module's
portable (pre-AOT, publication-trailer-stripped) WASM bytes. This is
the identity capability policies and signature policies key on.

VERSION.description: Module version expected by the app.

ROLE.description: Free-text launcher hint, for example primary, worker, or ui-host.

MAX_WALL_CLOCK_MS.description:
Per-invocation wall-clock budget override in milliseconds. Zero means
the host runtime default applies.

MAX_COST_UNITS.description:
Per-invocation execution-cost (fuel) budget override. Zero means the
host runtime default applies.

MAX_MEMORY_PAGES.description:
Linear-memory ceiling override in 64 KiB WASM pages. Zero means the
host runtime default applies.

RUNTIME_TARGET.description:
Where this module is instantiated. PAGE or BOTH means the module also
loads in the browser: the page resolves its bytes by CONTENT_HASH over
IPFS and instantiates it through the SAME isomorphic module-sdk harness
ABI the SDN nodes use (manifest + plugin_invoke_stream) — never through
a bespoke page-only loader. Defaults to NODE to preserve the prior
node-only behavior of manifests written before this field existed.

APPDataRef.description:
One SDS record type the app produces and/or consumes. Names an existing
spacedatastandards.org schema by its established code; the app manifest
defines no data schemas of its own.

ID.description:
App-local stable reference for this data binding. Required, unique
within the manifest.

SDS_TYPE.description: Existing SDS schema code, for example OMM, CDM, or EPM. Required.

DIRECTION.description: Data flow relative to the app.

MODULE_ID.description:
When present, must equal an APPModuleRef.ID in the same manifest — the
member module responsible for this data binding.

APPSourceRef.description: One upstream data source the app depends on.

ID.description:
App-local stable reference for this source. Required, unique within
the manifest.

REF.description:
Source identifier: an APPModuleRef.ID when KIND is MODULE, otherwise a
URL or dataset identifier. Required.

APPUIPage.description:
One UI page of the app. Exactly one of the two delivery mechanisms must
be populated: inline CONTENT (with ENCODING describing its string form),
or MODULE_ID plus URL for a page served by a member module. Inline pages
must be fully self-contained — CSS and JS inlined, all assets embedded
as data URIs, zero external requests.

ID.description:
App-local stable reference for this page. Required, unique within the
manifest.

TITLE.description: Display title. Falls back to the app NAME when empty.

DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable summary. Falls back to the app DESCRIPTION when empty.

ICON.description: Launcher icon identifier or inline data URI.

COLOR.description: Launcher accent color, CSS color syntax.

TEXT_COLOR.description: Launcher text color, CSS color syntax.

CONTENT.description:
Inlined, self-contained page in the string form declared by ENCODING.
Empty when the page is module-served via MODULE_ID and URL.

ENCODING.description: String form of CONTENT.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: IANA media type of the decoded page bytes, for example text/html.

CONTENT_SHA256.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the decoded
page bytes, so a launcher can verify inline content after decoding.

ENTRY.description:
True for the page the launcher opens first. Exactly one page in an
app must set this when UI is present.

MODULE_ID.description:
When module-served, must equal an APPModuleRef.ID in the same
manifest — the member module that serves this page.

URL.description:
When module-served, the path or entrypoint the module serves the page
at.

APPDataflow.description:
One unit of the page's data contract: a named flow describing what data
enters or leaves the running page, the SDS standard it carries, how it is
transported, and — when applicable — the loaded module method port bound
to it. Standards-only rule: every flow payload is an SDS record (a
canonical size-prefixed FlatBuffer) or a CID pointing at one; this table
defines no data shapes of its own, it only references an existing
spacedatastandards.org schema by its established code. Locators are
content-addressed and IPFS-first.

NAME.description:
App-local stable name for this flow. Required, unique within the
manifest.

DIRECTION.description: Which way the payload crosses the page boundary at runtime.

SDS_SCHEMA.description:
Existing SDS schema code carried by this flow, for example OMM, OEM, or
PNM. Required. Mirrors APPDataRef.SDS_TYPE but named for the standard
the flow carries; the app defines no schema of its own.

TRANSPORT.description:
Transport that moves the payload. Defaults to IPFS_CID per the
content-addressed, IPFS-first rule.

LOCATOR.description:
Where to fetch or reach the payload, interpreted per TRANSPORT: a CID
for IPFS_CID, a gossip topic name for PUBSUB_TOPIC, or a same-origin
route template for GATEWAY_ROUTE.

MODULE_ID.description:
When present, must equal an APPModuleRef.ID in the same manifest — the
loaded module that produces or consumes this flow. Binds the flow to a
specific module method port together with METHOD_ID and PORT_ID.

METHOD_ID.description:
When present, the PLG.PLGMethodManifest.METHOD_ID on MODULE_ID that
this flow is bound to.

PORT_ID.description:
When present, the PLG.PLGPortManifest.PORT_ID on METHOD_ID that this
flow is bound to.

CONTENT_ENCODING.description:
String/compression form of the payload as it crosses the channel,
reusing the page content-encoding vocabulary. For flows carrying
canonical SDS FlatBuffer bytes (or a CID string), UTF8 denotes the raw
bytes/string with no extra wrapper; BASE64, BASE64_GZIP, and
BASE64_BROTLI denote a base64 text wrapper (optionally compressed)
applied when the channel is text-only.

APP.description: Application Package Manifest — one launchable app.

ID.description: Stable app identity, unique per publisher. Required.

MODULES.description:
Member WASM modules. Referential integrity: every MODULE_ID and every
MODULE-kind REF elsewhere in the manifest must resolve into this list.

DATA.description: SDS record types produced and consumed.

SOURCES.description: Upstream sources depended on.

UI.description: UI pages. Exactly one entry page when nonempty.

CREATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was created.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was last updated.

DATAFLOW.description:
The page's declarative data contract: what data enters and leaves the
running page and how. Referential integrity: every MODULE_ID here must
resolve into MODULES, and each MODULE_ID/METHOD_ID/PORT_ID triple must
name a method port advertised by that module's PLG manifest.

RUNTIME_CLASS.description:
App-wide runtime class, reusing appRuntimeTarget. Lets a pulled manifest
self-describe where the app as a whole is meant to run, instead of that
classification being supplied externally at install time. This is the
app-level DEFAULT/DECLARATION only: an individual APPModuleRef.
RUNTIME_TARGET still governs where that specific member module loads and
may specialize away from RUNTIME_CLASS (for example a NODE-class app
with one PAGE-capable module). Defaults to NODE to preserve the prior
node-only assumption of manifests written before this field existed.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified $CCT category this app is shelved under, using the same
vocabulary and the same semantics as PLG.PRIMARY_CATEGORY, so a storefront
or library shelf holds apps and modules together without translating
between two classification schemes. RUNTIME_CLASS says WHERE an app runs;
PRIMARY_CATEGORY says WHAT IT DOES. They are independent: a NODE-class app
and a PAGE-class app can share a category.
UNSPECIFIED means the publisher did not classify the app; a consumer
renders it ungrouped and never infers a class.

CATEGORIES.description:
Every ratified $CCT category this app belongs to, for browse, filter and
per-category counting. An app MAY carry several. If nonempty it MUST
include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Codes MUST NOT repeat.

sdfResult.description: Result of a single SDF point-in-volume query (24 bytes, 8-byte aligned).

SIGNED_DISTANCE.description: Signed distance (negative inside, zero on boundary, positive outside).

CLOSEST_DISTANCE.description: Distance to the closest boundary point (always positive).

sdfTimeRangeResult.description: Result of a time-range SDF query (40 bytes, 8-byte aligned).

ENTRY_TIME.description: Julian date when the entity entered the volume (0 == never entered).

EXIT_TIME.description: Julian date when the entity exited the volume (0 == still inside).

MIN_DISTANCE.description: Most negative signed distance (closest approach to center).

INNER_HALF_ANGLE.description: Inner half-angle for hollow cones (0 == solid).

FLAT_CAP.description: Use a flat cap (true) or a spherical cap (false).

INNER_RADIUS.description: Inner radius for hollow sphere (0 == solid).

SDFCustom.description: Custom SDF defined by a set of unit boundary-direction vectors.

DIRECTIONS.description: Unit vectors defining the boundary packed as [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, ...].

SDFComponent.description: Single component in a composed SDF.

PRIMITIVE.description: Root primitive type (useful when COMPONENTS[] is empty).

COMPONENTS.description: One or more components that may be combined via COMPOSITIONS[].

INPUT_OFFSET.description: Input buffer offset (arena bytes) where the Vec3[] of world points begins.

ENTITY_IDS_OFFSET.description: Entity-ids buffer offset corresponding to each point (optional).

OUTPUT_OFFSET.description: Output buffer offset where sdfResult[] is written.

INSIDE_COUNT.description: Number of points inside the volume.

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Optional error message when ERROR_CODE != 0.

SDF.description:
Signed Distance Field envelope message — carries a configuration, a batch
request, a batch response, or single / time-range result records.

TRH.description:
Tracking Hardware. Installations attach antennas, transmitters, receivers
and transponders to either a surface site or a tracked object. Delays are
seconds, frequencies hertz, temperatures kelvin and powers watts. JSON
projections preserve these IDL-capitalized field names exactly.

KEY_ID.description: Logical key identifier used across publication and grant records.

SLOT_ID.description: Host-managed key slot or key handle identifier.

ROLE.description: Role the referenced key fulfills for the module flow.

ALGORITHM.description: Algorithm or key family for the referenced key.

PUBLIC_KEY.description: Optional public bytes for verification or peer identity binding.

VERSION.description: Logical version of the referenced key.

EXPIRES_AT.description: Expiration time in unix milliseconds, or 0 if unbounded.

HOST_MANAGED.description: True when the secret material remains in the host key slot.

MESSAGE_TYPE.description: Distinguishes configuration inputs from runtime status outputs.

ROLE.description: Indicates whether the configuration/status applies to server/provider or requester/client behavior.

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: Peer ID advertised by the licensing provider.

PROVIDER_SIGNING_KEY.description: Host-managed long-lived signing key used for grant signatures.

PROVIDER_WRAPPING_KEY.description: Host-managed wrapping key used to protect per-publication content keys for requesters.

REQUESTER_SIGNING_KEY.description: Optional requester signing key reference for requester-hosted flows.

EXPIRES_AT.description: Runtime expiry in unix milliseconds, or 0 if unbounded.

MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS.description: Maximum accepted requester/provider clock skew in milliseconds.

CAPABILITY_TOKEN.description: Optional capability token bytes returned with successful grants.

INITIALIZED.description: Whether the runtime has been initialized successfully.

NEEDS_ROTATION.description: Whether the runtime needs issuer key rotation or refreshed configuration.

STATUS_CODE.description: Optional machine-readable status code for status/error responses.

STATUS_MESSAGE.description: Optional human-readable status or error message.

PRRMetadataEntry.description: String metadata key/value attached to a peer registry entry.

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Known libp2p/IPFS multiaddresses for this peer.

TRUST_LEVEL.description: Trust level assigned to this peer by the local registry.

GROUPS.description: Peer group names this peer belongs to.

ADDED_AT.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this peer was added.

LAST_SEEN.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this peer was last observed.

LAST_CONNECTED.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this peer last connected.

CONNECTION_COUNT.description: Number of successful connections observed by this node.

MESSAGES_RECEIVED.description: Number of messages received from this peer.

MESSAGES_SENT.description: Number of messages sent to this peer.

BYTES_RECEIVED.description: Number of bytes received from this peer.

BYTES_SENT.description: Number of bytes sent to this peer.

EPM_DATA.description: Optional EPM.fbs bytes for the peer identity profile.

VCARD_DATA.description: Optional vCard projection for compatibility views.

METADATA.description: Additional peer metadata as string key/value entries.

UPDATED_AT.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this registry record was last updated.

DELETED.description: True when this record tombstones the peer from the current registry.

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: Peer ID of the node/provider that issued this registry record.

PROVIDER_SIGNATURE.description: Provider signature over the peer registry record.

SHWUniform.description: Uniform descriptor — name + type + optional default value.

UNIFORM_DEFAULT_VALUE.description: Optional default value encoded as bytes in the native type layout.

SHWCompileRequest.description:
Compile request — one shader source (typically a fragment of a
larger stage) plus metadata for the host splice.

SHADER_NAME.description: Logical shader name (used in logs and uniform prefixing).

SHADER_INJECTION_POINT.description: Intended injection point in the host pipeline.

SHADER_UNIFORMS.description: Expected uniforms declared by the source.

SHWCompileResponse.description: Compile response — whether the shader compiled, with diagnostics.

COMPILED_BINARY.description: Optional compiled binary (if the compiler emits one).

LINKED_UNIFORMS.description: Echo of the uniforms the compiler actually linked.

SHW.description:
Shader Wire envelope — carries either a compile request or a compile
response across the runtime boundary.

MODULE_ID.description: Canonical module identifier

REQUESTER_XPUB.description: Requester account identity or wallet xpub

REQUESTED_AT.description: Request timestamp in milliseconds since epoch

EXPIRES_AT.description: Challenge expiration time in milliseconds since epoch

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: Provider peer identifier

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Structured error message

REQUESTER_EPM.description:
Requester's full $EPM (Entity Profile) FlatBuffer, re-sent per grant for
freshness. Verified in-module to bind the requester's xpub identity to its
authenticated ed25519 signing key (cross-curve attestation).

OPPProvenance.description:
Provenance for exactly one physical value.

This table is the mechanism by which the never-invent-data law is enforced
in the IDL rather than in prose: no physical quantity in an $OPP can be
expressed without one of these attached, so a value with no admissible
source cannot be encoded at all. Unknown values are ABSENT. They are never
zero, never a placeholder, and never carried forward from a different
object.

SOURCE.description:
Publisher of the value, named as the publisher names itself — a space
agency's object database, a public satellite catalogue, a third-party
satellite reference site, or the operator itself.

SOURCE_RECORD_ID.description:
The source's own identifier for the record this value was read from, such
as that database's object id. Verbatim, never normalized.

SOURCE_URL.description: Deep link to the exact source record when the source publishes one.

EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) of the
instant the value describes: the epoch at which the property held. A
design or as-built value that does not change over time omits EPOCH.

RETRIEVED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) when
this record retrieved the value from SOURCE.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: The source's own revision, edition or publication marker, verbatim.

LICENSE.description: Terms under which SOURCE permits redistribution of the value, verbatim.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution string the source requires be displayed with the value.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the exact source
payload bytes the value was parsed from.

NOTES.description: Free text qualifying the value, such as the source's own caveat.

OPPQuantity.description:
One scalar physical quantity, its unit and its own provenance.

PROVENANCE is required: an OPPQuantity that exists names where it came from.
Presence of the table is the signal that a value exists, so VALUE zero is a
real zero (0 dBsm is 1 m2) and an unknown quantity omits the whole table.

UNITS.description:
Unit symbol verbatim, never silently converted: "kg", "m", "m2", "m2/kg",
"kg/m2", "dBsm", "W", "mag". A converted value states the unit it was
converted to and records the conversion in PROVENANCE.NOTES with
PROVENANCE.METHOD DERIVED.

SIGMA.description:
1-sigma uncertainty in UNITS. Zero means the source stated no uncertainty;
a genuine stated sigma is never exactly zero.

OPPRadarCrossSection.description:
Radar cross-section as reported for one band, polarization and aspect
convention. Radar cross-section is band- and aspect-dependent, so an $OPP
carries a list of these and never a single scalar. A source publishing
minimum, average and maximum cross-sections becomes three entries with
ASPECT MINIMUM, AVERAGE and MAXIMUM sharing one SOURCE.

BAND.description:
Radar band designation verbatim from the source: "UHF", "L", "S", "C",
"X", "Ku". Empty when the source states no band.

FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Centre frequency [megahertz] when the source states one. Zero means
unstated.

POLARIZATION.description:
