IRMSource.description:
The source object a job is reading, and the validators that prove a resumed
read is reading the same bytes.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable locator of the source object, verbatim.

SOURCE_OBJECT_ID.description:
Source-native object, export, or product identifier verbatim, when the
provider names one independently of its locator.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier pinning the exact source bytes, when the source is
content-addressed.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: Media type of the source object verbatim as the provider states it.

TOTAL_BYTES.description:
Total length of the source object in bytes. 0 means the provider did not
state a length; it never means an empty object.

ENTITY_TAG.description: Opaque entity validator verbatim as the provider published it.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the complete source object as 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters, when the provider publishes one. Never computed from a partial
read.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: Provider-stated edition, revision, or release marker verbatim.

VALIDATOR_MATCH.description: What the publisher concluded when it last compared validators.

VALIDATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of that comparison.

IRMDecodeContext.description:
Everything a resuming reader needs to decode a chunk that does not begin at
offset 0. Required whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header.

FORMAT.description:
Format token the decoder dispatches on, verbatim and lowercase, e.g.
`text/csv`. A consumer that does not implement the format refuses the chunk
rather than guessing at a layout.

HEADER_LINE.description:
The source's header line verbatim, exactly as it appeared at offset 0 and
excluding its line terminator. This is the field that makes chunk N>0
decodable; without it a headerless chunk parses to zero rows and looks like
a clean tail.

HEADER_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length the header occupied at the start of the source, including its
terminator, so a reader can tell a header-bearing prefix from a data row.

COLUMN_NAMES.description:
Column names in source order, when the publisher parsed them. Advisory:
HEADER_LINE is authoritative and a disagreement is resolved in its favour.

CHARSET.description: Character encoding label verbatim as the provider states it.

COMPRESSION.description:
Stream-compression codec applied to the source bytes, verbatim and
lowercase. Empty means the ranged bytes are read as-is. Non-empty means
NEXT_OFFSET is a position in the COMPRESSED stream and DECODER_STATE,
WINDOW and PARTIAL_RECORD are all required to resume.

DECODED_OFFSET.description:
Position in the DECODED stream corresponding to NEXT_OFFSET, when the
source is compressed. 0 with a non-empty COMPRESSION means the decoded
stream has not been advanced.

DECODER_STATE.description:
Serialized, pointer-free image of the decoder at the seam — the state a
codec with no restart point needs in order to have one. Opaque to every
consumer but a decoder whose stamps match exactly. Never partially applied.

DECODER_STATE_FORMAT.description:
Layout identifier of DECODER_STATE, verbatim, naming the decoder struct the
image was taken from. A consumer that does not know the token restarts.

DECODER_STATE_VERSION.description: Version of that layout, verbatim. Any disagreement restarts the job.

DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length DECODER_STATE is expected to have. Carried even though the
vector knows its own size, so a size disagreement is detectable BEFORE the
image is loaded into a differently shaped struct.

DECODER_STATE_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of DECODER_STATE as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

DECODER_BUILD_ID.description:
Build identifier of the decoder that produced DECODER_STATE, verbatim, so
two builds of one codec version are still distinguishable.

DECODER_STATE_MEDIA_TYPE.description:
Media type of DECODER_STATE, so an unrelated decoder refuses it instead of
misreading it.

WINDOW.description:
The decoder's history window at the seam — the bytes that ARE the codec's
back-reference dictionary. Carried separately from DECODER_STATE because it
is bulk data of a size the codec fixes, not part of the struct image.

WINDOW_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length WINDOW is expected to have, for the same detect-before-load
reason as DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.

WINDOW_POSITION.description:
Offset into WINDOW at which the codec will next write, when the window is
a circular buffer whose contents cannot be interpreted without it.

PARTIAL_RECORD.description:
The bytes of the record that straddles the seam: everything the previous
chunk decoded of a record it could not finish. A resuming decoder prepends
these to the next chunk's decoded output before parsing. Carried as bytes,
not text, because a seam may fall inside a multi-byte character.

IRMChunk.description: One chunk that was read and durably committed.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based position of the chunk in the job's read sequence.

BATCH_ID.description:
Publisher-stable batch identifier the chunk's records were stored under,
verbatim, so a consumer can join the mark to the stored rows.

RANGE_FIRST_BYTE.description: First byte of the range that was read.

RANGE_LAST_BYTE.description:
Last byte of the range that was read. Interpreted per RANGE_MODE:
inclusive under INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE, exclusive under OFFSET_LENGTH.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Bytes the read actually returned, which may be shorter than the range
requested.

CHUNK_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

RECORDS_DECODED.description: Records the decoder produced from the chunk.

RECORDS_STORED.description:
Records the storage lane reported as durably committed. A chunk whose
stored count is 0 is not marked at all.

RECORDS_REJECTED.description: Records the storage lane rejected or collapsed as duplicates.

ATTEMPTS.description: Number of read attempts this chunk cost, including the successful one.

COMMITTED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the storage lane
confirmed the commit.

IRMFault.description: The last unrecovered error, carried so a resumed run can refuse to loop.

CODE.description: Publisher-stable error code verbatim.

MESSAGE.description: Human-readable message verbatim; never a substitute for CODE.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of the chunk the fault occurred on.

CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.description: Consecutive failed attempts at that chunk.

OCCURRED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of the fault.

RETRY_NOT_BEFORE.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp before which a consumer must not
retry. Empty means the publisher states no backoff.

JOB_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the ingest job. Together with the publishing
key it is the job's identity across every mark it emits.

SEQUENCE.description:
Monotonic version of this mark within JOB_ID. Highest wins per publishing
key. Never reused, never decremented.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the data provider being read, verbatim.
Publisher data: it may name a real provider.

INGESTOR_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS identifier of the ingest module or flow that owns the job, so
two pipelines reading one provider do not share a resume point.

SOURCE.description: The source object and its validators.

RANGE_MODE.description: How byte positions in this mark are addressed.

NEXT_OFFSET.description:
Byte offset at which the next read begins, in the SOURCE's own byte stream:
the compressed stream when DECODE_CONTEXT.COMPRESSION is non-empty, in
which case it is a record boundary only in company with the decoder state,
window and partial record. On an uncompressed source it is ALWAYS a
complete-record boundary, corrected backwards from the previous chunk's
byte budget. 0 is a valid value and means the job has committed nothing yet.

NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index of the next chunk to read. With PART_INDEX addressing this
is the only position.

CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET.description:
Byte budget the publisher reads per chunk. Records the ceiling the job
actually ran under, which a host may have clamped below the configured one.

DECODE_CONTEXT.description:
Everything needed to decode the chunk at NEXT_OFFSET. REQUIRED in practice
whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header; a consumer that finds
it absent there restarts from offset 0 rather than decoding blind.

LAST_CHUNK.description: The chunk this mark was advanced from — the last one durably committed.

CHUNKS_COMMITTED.description: Chunks durably committed by this job so far.

BYTES_COMMITTED.description: Source bytes accounted for by committed chunks.

RECORDS_COMMITTED.description: Records durably committed by this job so far, across every chunk.

TARGET_STANDARD.description:
Four-character standard code of the records this job writes, `$` included,
e.g. `$TBS`. Never a union ordinal.

RECONCILE_MODE.description:
Reconciliation mode the storage lane was called with, verbatim, e.g.
`append`. A chunked job never reconciles per batch: reconciling would delete
every earlier chunk as the next one arrived.

MERGE_POLICY.description: Deduplication or merge policy the job applied, verbatim.

FAULT.description: The last unrecovered error, when there is one.

CREATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job was created.

STARTED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the first chunk was read.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which this mark was published.
With JOB_ID and SEQUENCE this is the version key; SEQUENCE breaks ties.

COMPLETED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job reached COMPLETE.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp after which a consumer treats the
mark as stale and re-validates the source before resuming. Empty means the
publisher states no expiry.

TAGS.description: `namespace:value` facets, sorted and deduplicated. See TAG GRAMMAR above.

NOTES.description: Publisher note about this job; never a substitute for a field.

Entity Metadata — generic queryable metadata for a host-local entity.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Optional NORAD catalog id for standards-backed entities.

CCTCategory.description:
One ratified category in the taxonomy.

DISPLAY_NAME, SUMMARY and SLUG are required: a category cannot be published
without the label a surface will render, the sentence a browse row will
show, and the route a link will target. This is what stops each consumer
from inventing its own wording for the same code.

CODE.description: The ratified category code. This is the join key every consumer uses.

DISPLAY_NAME.description:
Canonical human-readable label, rendered verbatim. MUST equal the display
name stated in the CODE member's doc comment.

SUMMARY.description: One-sentence description shown on browse rows and category headers.

SLUG.description:
Route-safe identifier: the CODE identifier lowercased with `_` replaced by
`-`. Published explicitly rather than derived so every surface routes
identically.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer editorial description for a category landing page.

PARENT.description:
Parent category for hierarchical browse. UNSPECIFIED means this is a
top-level category. A category MUST NOT name itself as its parent.

SORT_ORDER.description:
Presentation order within its parent, ascending. Ties break on
DISPLAY_NAME.

KEYWORDS.description:
Search synonyms and alternate phrasings that resolve to this category.
Feeds type-ahead; never rendered as the category label.

ICON_KEY.description:
Key of a self-hosted icon or capsule asset for this category. A KEY, not a
URL: consuming node surfaces load zero external-origin bytes, so the
consumer resolves this against its own local asset set.

CCTCategoryRollup.description:
An observed count of catalogue items in one category.

Counts are VOLATILE and are never part of the ratified taxonomy itself. A
rollup exists only with COUNTED_AT and SOURCE_CATALOG_ID, so a published
count can never omit when it was taken or what it was taken over. A consumer
that needs a live number computes it from the items; a consumer rendering a
published rollup MUST show it as of COUNTED_AT.

CODE.description: Category being counted.

ITEM_COUNT.description:
Number of catalogue items whose PRIMARY_CATEGORY or CATEGORIES include
CODE, counted over SOURCE_CATALOG_ID at COUNTED_AT.

SOURCE_CATALOG_ID.description: Identifier of the catalogue the count was taken over.

COUNTED_AT.description: Unix seconds when the count was taken.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

TAXONOMY_ID.description: Stable identifier of this taxonomy publication.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:
The ratified categories. Every capabilityClass member a consumer may
encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.

PLGAcceptedTypeSet.description:
Accepted schema family for a port. When a port accepts multiple wire
formats (canonical FlatBuffer + aligned-binary), each ALLOWED_TYPE
entry carries its own TAB.FlatBufferTypeRef with the schema identity,
and the enclosing PLGPortManifest advertises both wire formats via
ALLOWED_WIRE_FORMATS. Per SDK contract: a port that advertises
aligned-binary MUST also advertise the canonical flatbuffer fallback
for the same schema and file identifier in the same set.

SET_ID.description: Stable type-set identifier within the port.

ALLOWED_TYPES.description: Specific FlatBuffer types accepted by the set.

ALLOWED_WIRE_FORMATS.description:
Wire formats this set accepts. If ALIGNED_BINARY is present,
FLATBUFFER MUST also be present for the same schemas.

DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable explanation of the accepted schema family.

PLGPortManifest.description: One input or output port on a method.

PORT_ID.description: Stable port identifier within the method.

DISPLAY_NAME.description: Human-readable name for UIs.

ACCEPTED_TYPE_SETS.description: Type sets accepted on this port.

MIN_STREAMS.description: Minimum number of streams that must be connected.

MAX_STREAMS.description: Maximum number of streams that may be connected.

REQUIRED.description: Whether the port must be connected for invocation.

PLGHostCapability.description: One host capability dependency (richer form of PluginCapability).

PLGTimerSpec.description: Timer entry declared by a plugin.

PLGProtocolSpec.description: Protocol handler declared by a plugin.

PLGBuildArtifact.description: Build artifact emitted by the plugin toolchain.

NAME.description: Function name as exported from WASM

PLGFlowNode.description:
One node in a composed flow graph. A degenerate flow IS a module: a leaf
module leaves the flow-graph fields on PLG empty; a composed flow populates
them. This is how flows reuse the module schema rather than a separate one.

NODE_ID.description: Stable node identifier within this flow

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin id of the module this node invokes

METHOD_ID.description: Method id invoked on the module

DISPATCH_MODEL.description:
Dispatch model: empty = linked-direct (in-wasm), "isomorphic" = an
independently instantiated signed WASM node, and "host-capability" = a
generic host adapter.

CONFIG.description: Opaque per-node configuration (FlatBuffer or raw bytes; never JSON)

CANONICAL_TYPE.description:
Canonical SDS identity carried by the edge. NOT `required`: an edge may
be opaque by design (see OPAQUE), and a signer must never be forced to
invent an identity to satisfy the schema. A contract MUST carry exactly
one of CANONICAL_TYPE or OPAQUE = true; a contract with neither, or with
both, is invalid and MUST be rejected by the compiler that signs the flow.

OPAQUE.description:
The edge carries bytes with no SDS identity BY DESIGN — an
application-blind host-capability adapter (an HTTP body, a raw file
chunk) or a timer TICK frame with no payload at all. This is a deliberate
signed assertion of opacity, which is why it is an explicit flag rather
than an absent CANONICAL_TYPE: a missing type must stay distinguishable
from a declared-opaque one. An opaque edge is ineligible for the aligned
route, so ALIGNED_ELIGIBLE MUST be false when OPAQUE is true.

PLGFlowEdge.description: One directed edge wiring a producer output port to a consumer input port.

CONTRACT.description:
Exact identity/layout and compile-time representation policy. NOT
`required`: marking a NEW field of an EXISTING table required makes the
FlatBuffers verifier reject every $PLG buffer written before 1.0.13,
which is a breaking change to a ratified standard. Presence is enforced
where it belongs — the flow compiler MUST refuse to SIGN a flow whose
edges lack a CONTRACT, and a verifier MUST reject a signed flow edge
without one. Buffers predating 1.0.13 stay readable and stay unsigned.

PLGFlowTrigger.description: One flow trigger (e.g. a host timer or HTTP route) that starts a drain.

DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS.description: Default firing interval in milliseconds (timer triggers)

PLGFlowTriggerBinding.description: Binds a trigger to the node + input port it delivers its frame to.

SUBSCRIPTION_PERIOD_DAYS.description: Subscription billing period length in days

LISTING_STATUS.description: Storefront publication state for this manifest version

SIGNATURE.description: Ed25519 signature from provider over manifest

INVOKE_SURFACES.description:
Canonical invoke surfaces this artifact exposes. A single plugin
MAY list both DIRECT and COMMAND when it supports both.

METHODS.description:
Rich per-method invoke manifests (port shape, drain semantics,
accepted wire formats). ENTRY_FUNCTIONS retains the slim
name+input_schemas+output_schema summary; METHODS carries the full
invoke-surface detail including aligned-binary advertisement.

HOST_CAPABILITIES.description:
Enum-typed host capability dependencies (richer than CAPABILITIES,
which is string-tagged metadata).

SCHEMAS_USED.description: FlatBuffer schemas this plugin depends on at the invoke surface.

BUILD_ARTIFACTS.description: Build artifacts emitted by the toolchain (WASM, bindings, etc.).

ALLOWED_XPUBS.description:
Allowed requester xpub identities (BIP-32 account xpubs) for module grants:
a requester whose verified EPM binds an xpub in this list is granted (PKI
identity authorization). Empty list = no xpub allowlist gate.

FLOW_NODES.description:
Composition graph (a degenerate flow is a module): the nodes this flow
invokes. Empty for a leaf module; populated for a composed flow. The flow
definition is this PLG FlatBuffer, not a bespoke JSON graph.

FLOW_EDGES.description: Composition-graph edges wiring node output ports to input ports.

FLOW_TRIGGERS.description: Flow triggers (timer/http) that start a drain.

FLOW_TRIGGER_BINDINGS.description: Bindings from triggers to the node + input port they deliver to.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified $CCT category this module is shelved under. This is the
category a storefront capsule, a library shelf and a breadcrumb show when
exactly one must be chosen. UNSPECIFIED means the publisher did not
classify the module; a consumer renders it ungrouped and never guesses.

This supersedes PLUGIN_TYPE for all storefront, library and search
surfaces. PLUGIN_TYPE remains on the wire and is not removed, but its
`pluginCategory` vocabulary mixes capability families with node-internal
plumbing, carries a legacy vendor-derived member, holds a real family at
ordinal 0, and admits only one value. Canonical migration, applied by a
publisher rewriting an old manifest:
Sensor->SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE, Propagator->PROPAGATION,
Renderer->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING,
Analysis->MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS,
DataSource->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, EW->ELECTRONIC_WARFARE,
Comms->RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS, Physics->SPACE_ENVIRONMENT,
Shader->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING, Parser->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST,
Validator->DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY, Interpolator->PROPAGATION,
Exporter->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, Foundation->FOUNDATION_AND_MATH,
Infrastructure->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE, Licensing->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING,
Storefront->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING, Publisher->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE,
Basilisk->PROPAGATION, Maneuver->MANEUVER_PLANNING,
Flow->FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION, Unspecified->UNSPECIFIED.
The mapping is one-way: PRIMARY_CATEGORY is never back-derived into
PLUGIN_TYPE.

CATEGORIES.description:
Every ratified $CCT category this module belongs to, for browse, filter
and per-category counting. A module MAY carry several. If nonempty it
MUST include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Codes MUST NOT repeat. An empty list with
a set PRIMARY_CATEGORY means the module belongs to that one category.

ROOT_TYPE.description: Optional root type name from the schema

REQUESTER_XPUB.description: Requester account identity or wallet xpub

EXPIRES_AT.description: Grant expiration time in milliseconds since epoch

WRAPPED_CONTENT_KEY_HEADER.description: Encryption header for the recipient-specific wrapped content-key payload.

Encrypted FlatBuffer payload containing the recipient-specific content key

GRANT_VERIFIER_PUBKEY.description: Provider public key used to verify the grant signature

PROVIDER_SIGNATURE.description: Provider signature over the grant

weightedEdge.description: Weighted directed edge (16 bytes, 8-byte aligned for zero-copy ingestion).

Optional vertex capacity for implicit graph creation.

BUILD_GRAPH.description: Build a CSR representation after ingest.

VERTEX_COUNT.description: Number of vertices in the graph.
Number of vertices in the solved graph.

PREDECESSORS.description: Predecessor array (length == VERTEX_COUNT; UINT32_MAX means none / source).

SOURCE.description: Source vertex index from the latest SSSP solve.

REACHABLE.description: Whether a path exists from SOURCE to TARGET.

DISTANCE.description: Total distance from SOURCE to TARGET (Infinity if unreachable).

FPC.description:
Fastest Path Compute — envelope message for weighted graph ingestion and

EPOCH.description: Observation epoch (ISO 8601)
Observation epoch (ISO 8601)

DENSITIES.description: Electron densities at each altitude in electrons/m^3

START_TIME.description: Observation start time (ISO 8601)

STOP_TIME.description: Observation stop time (ISO 8601)

FOES.description: foEs sporadic E critical frequency in MHz

HMF2.description: hmF2 peak height of F2 layer in km

HMF1.description: hmF1 peak height of F1 layer in km

HME.description: hmE peak height of E layer in km

NMF2.description: NmF2 peak density of F2 layer in electrons/m^3

MJD.description: Modified Julian Date in UTC, e.g., 58119

X_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS.description: x component of Pole Wander in radians, e.g., 2.872908911518888E-7

Y_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS.description: y component of Pole Wander in radians, e.g., 1.2003259523750447E-6

X_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS.description: x component of Celestial Pole Offset in radians, e.g., 5.720801437092525E-10

Y_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS.description: y component of Celestial Pole Offset in radians, e.g., -8.484239419416879E-10

UT1_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS.description: UT1 minus UTC in seconds, e.g., 0.2163567

TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS.description: TAI minus UTC in seconds, e.g., 37

LENGTH_OF_DAY_CORRECTION_SECONDS.description: Correction to Length of Day in seconds, e.g., 8.094E-4

SERIES.description:
Published series this row was taken from. Rows from different series are
NOT interchangeable at the microarcsecond level and must not be merged
without recording which series each row came from.

IAU_CONVENTION.description:
Precession-nutation model the celestial pole offsets are expressed
against. X_/Y_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS are CIP offsets in the GCRS
(dX, dY) under the IAU 2000/2006 conventions; a consumer cannot apply
them correctly without knowing which model produced them.

X_POLE_WANDER_UNCERTAINTY_RADIANS.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in x Pole Wander, radians.

Y_POLE_WANDER_UNCERTAINTY_RADIANS.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in y Pole Wander, radians.

X_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_UNCERTAINTY_RADI.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in the x Celestial Pole Offset, radians.

Y_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_UNCERTAINTY_RADI.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in the y Celestial Pole Offset, radians.

UT1_MINUS_UTC_UNCERTAINTY_SECONDS.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in UT1 minus UTC, seconds.

LENGTH_OF_DAY_UNCERTAINTY_SECONDS.description: 1-sigma uncertainty in the Length of Day correction, seconds.

X_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS_HP.description:
x component of Pole Wander in radians, double precision. Authoritative
over X_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS when present.

Y_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS_HP.description:
y component of Pole Wander in radians, double precision. Authoritative
over Y_POLE_WANDER_RADIANS when present.

X_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS_HP.description:
x component of the Celestial Pole Offset in radians, double precision.
Authoritative over X_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS when present.

Y_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS_HP.description:
y component of the Celestial Pole Offset in radians, double precision.
Authoritative over Y_CELESTIAL_POLE_OFFSET_RADIANS when present.

UT1_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS_HP.description:
UT1 minus UTC in seconds, double precision. Authoritative over
UT1_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS when present.

LENGTH_OF_DAY_CORRECTION_SECONDS_HP.description:
Correction to Length of Day in seconds, double precision. Authoritative
over LENGTH_OF_DAY_CORRECTION_SECONDS when present.

DATA_SET_EPOCH.description:
Epoch of the data set this row was published in, ISO 8601 UTC. Identifies
WHICH issue of the series a consumer is holding; two rows for the same
MJD from different data-set epochs are different values, not duplicates.

DATA_SET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the complete published data set this row was taken
from. Every frames consumer that must agree bit-for-bit records this so
the source is provable rather than assumed.

NUTATION_DPSI_RADIANS.description:
Nutation correction in longitude (dPsi) against the IAU 1980 model,
radians, as published beside the CIP offsets by combined rapid-service
series.

NUTATION_DEPS_RADIANS.description:
Nutation correction in obliquity (dEps) against the IAU 1980 model,
radians.

LONGITUDE_MIN.description: Western longitude boundary of slot (degrees east)

LONGITUDE_MAX.description: Eastern longitude boundary of slot (degrees east)

LOST_FLAG.description: True if object is lost/not tracked

EPOCH.description: Epoch of status (ISO 8601)

TXSProvenance.description:
Replayable provenance for ONE source's report of ONE facility, emission, or
scheduled transmission.

Every source consulted gets its own entry, including sources that returned
nothing, so a consumer can tell "not looked for" from "looked for and
returned nothing". Source identity is DATA: PROVIDER_ID and AUTHORITY carry
verbatim what that source states about itself.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the consulted source, unique
within the publisher's own source registry. Never a display name and
never a URL.

AUTHORITY.description:
The authority under which that source publishes, verbatim as the source
states it: a spectrum regulator, an international coordination register,
a licensee, a monitoring service, or an observer compilation. Never
inferred by the publisher.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material.

SOURCE_QUERY.description:
The exact query, filter, or request parameters used, so the same rows can
be recovered by repeating the fetch.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond retrieval timestamp.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Required: there is no encoding for a
redistributed record whose terms are unstated. A source that publishes no
terms is recorded as publishing no terms; unknown terms are never public
domain and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as that source publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description:
The licence forbids commercial use. Rides PER SOURCE because one record
may merge an open-terms lane beside a non-commercial cross-check, and the
strictest consulted lane governs any derived product.

NATIVE_ID.description: This source's own row, record, licence or file identifier, verbatim.

POSITION_AUTHORITY.description:
The class of authority this particular source speaks with about position.
Published per source because a record may merge a regulator lane with a
community lane; the record-level POSITION_AUTHORITY states which class the
PUBLISHED coordinate came from.

REPORTED_LATITUDE.description:
Position this source reported, in decimal degrees on WGS 84, before
reconciliation. Retained unrounded so the merge stays auditable. Absent
when the source was consulted and reported no position.

CONTRIBUTED.description:
This source's report materially contributed to the published record.
False marks a source that was consulted and either returned nothing or
was outvoted; its entry is published either way.

TXSConsensus.description:
How one facility's independent source reports were reduced to the single
published position, and how strongly those reports agreed.

Agreement is CORROBORATION and is never authority: five compilations that
copied one another agree perfectly and establish nothing. Read this table
beside POSITION_AUTHORITY, never instead of it.

PROVIDERS_CONSULTED.description:
Sources queried for this facility, including those that returned nothing.
Never fewer than the number of SOURCES entries.

PROVIDERS_AGREEING.description:
Sources whose reported position fell within the publisher's agreement
threshold. A value of 1 means the published position rests on a single
report and was never independently corroborated.

PROVIDERS_DISAGREEING.description:
Sources whose reported position fell OUTSIDE that threshold and were not
reconciled. Non-zero is the machine-readable form of a contested
position and is published alongside POSITION_DISPUTED.

WINNING_PROVIDER_ID.description:
PROVIDER_ID of the report the merge selected, copied verbatim from the
matching SOURCES entry. Absent when METHOD is CENTROID: a computed
position belongs to no single source.

POSITION_SPREAD_M.description:
Greatest surface distance in metres between any two agreeing reported
positions. Zero is meaningful only when PROVIDERS_AGREEING is 1.

CONFIDENCE.description:
The publisher's own confidence in the merged position, on [0,1]. Never a
source's figure and never a probability from a model this standard does
not name.

MERGED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond instant at which the merge was performed.

TXSPriorPosition.description:
A position the facility is asserted to have occupied and vacated, retained
so a relocation never silently rewrites history.

POSITION_AUTHORITY.description:
Class of authority behind THIS coordinate, which is frequently weaker
than the authority behind the current one.

POSITION_UNCERTAINTY_M.description:
One-sigma-equivalent horizontal envelope in metres, as the source states
it. Zero means unpublished.

VALID_FROM.description:
RFC 3339 UTC bounds over which the facility is asserted to have occupied
this position. Either bound is absent when unpublished.

PROVIDER_ID.description: PROVIDER_ID of the SOURCES entry asserting this position.

TXSEmission.description:
One documented emission of one facility: a carrier or channel the facility
is stated to radiate, with the power and antenna terms published for it.

A facility radiating many carriers carries many entries; a facility whose
frequency changes by season or hour carries the documented set here and the
time-bounded usage in `$STX`. Unknown terms are ABSENT.

EMISSION_ID.description: Publisher-stable identifier for this emission within its facility record.

FREQUENCY_KHZ.description:
Assigned or nominal centre frequency in kilohertz. Kilohertz is the base
unit for this family because it spans the low-frequency broadcasting
allocations to the microwave allocations without unit switching; a
consumer joining to `$RFB` or `$TBS`, which carry megahertz, or to
`$IQC`, which carries hertz, converts at the join, explicitly. Zero means
unpublished.

BANDWIDTH_KHZ.description:
Necessary or occupied bandwidth in kilohertz as the source states it.
Zero means unpublished.

EMISSION_DESIGNATOR.description:
ITU emission designator verbatim, e.g. the necessary-bandwidth and
class-of-emission string a licence record carries. Authoritative over
MODULATION whenever both are present.

SERVICE.description: Service class of THIS emission when it differs from the facility's.

TRANSMITTER_POWER_KW.description:
Transmitter output power at the antenna feed, kilowatts. Zero means
unpublished. Never derived from radiated power.

EFFECTIVE_RADIATED_POWER_KW.description:
Effective radiated power referenced to a half-wave dipole, kilowatts.
Zero means unpublished.

EIRP_KW.description:
Equivalent isotropically radiated power, kilowatts. Zero means
unpublished. Published alongside, never instead of, the dipole-referenced
figure: the two differ by the dipole gain and this standard never
converts between them.

ANTENNA_HEIGHT_AGL_M.description:
Antenna centre of radiation above ground level, metres. Zero means
unpublished.

ANTENNA_AZIMUTH_DEG.description:
Main-lobe bearing, degrees clockwise from true north. Absent for a
non-directional emission; a non-directional emission is stated by
OMNIDIRECTIONAL, never by a bearing of zero.

OMNIDIRECTIONAL.description: The emission is radiated without a preferred bearing.

BEAMWIDTH_DEG.description: Half-power beamwidth in degrees. Zero means unpublished.

ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description:
Antenna gain in decibels referenced to an isotropic radiator. Zero means
unpublished; a real 0 dBi figure is published as a source term in
provenance rather than being indistinguishable from absence.

STATION_IDENTITY.description:
Station identification radiated on this emission, verbatim: a callsign, a
spoken or keyed identifier, or the identity string the source publishes.
Never synthesized.

VALID_FROM.description:
RFC 3339 UTC bounds of the authorization or documented use of this
emission. Either bound is absent when unpublished.

ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier for this facility, unique within its record
set. Never a source's own identifier and never a coordinate string.

NATIVE_ID.description:
Winning source's native facility identifier, copied verbatim from the
SOURCES entry named by CONSENSUS.WINNING_PROVIDER_ID. Never a substitute
for ID and never stable across sources.

SITE_NAME.description:
Facility or structure name verbatim when a source publishes one. Never
synthesized from coordinates, licensee, or nearest settlement.

STATION_IDENTITY.description:
Station identification the facility as a whole answers to, verbatim: a
callsign, an assigned station identifier, or the identifier an observer
community records. Per-emission identity lives in
EMISSIONS[].STATION_IDENTITY.

LICENSEE.description:
Licensee, operator or responsible administration name verbatim as the
cited source states it. A display name, never an identifier: consumers
must not treat it as a stable key.

LICENSE_ID.description: Licence, assignment or authorization identifier verbatim.

SERVICE.description:
Primary service class of the facility. Individual emissions may state
their own.

COUNTRY_CODE.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase, as the source states it.

ADMIN_AREA.description: Administrative subdivision or locality verbatim as the source states it.

LATITUDE.description:
Published facility position, decimal degrees on WGS 84, produced by the
merge described in CONSENSUS. ABSENT when no source publishes a position:
a region centroid is never substituted. Per-source positions before
reconciliation live in SOURCES[].REPORTED_LATITUDE/REPORTED_LONGITUDE and
are never overwritten by this value.

POSITION_AUTHORITY.description:
The class of authority behind LATITUDE/LONGITUDE. A consumer that renders
a position without reading this field is rendering an unlabelled claim.

POSITION_UNCERTAINTY_M.description:
Horizontal envelope in metres within which the facility is asserted to
lie, as the publisher states it. Zero means unpublished — never that the
position is exact.

POSITION_DISPUTED.description:
Credible consulted sources place the facility in materially different
locations, or a source states the position is contested. The published
coordinate remains the publisher's best merge; this flag forbids a
consumer from presenting it as settled.

PRIOR_POSITIONS.description: Positions the facility is asserted to have vacated, most recent first.

GROUND_ELEVATION_AMSL_M.description:
Ground elevation at the facility, metres above mean sea level as the
source states it. Zero means unpublished.

STRUCTURE_HEIGHT_AGL_M.description:
Overall height of the antenna-supporting structure above ground level,
metres. Distinct from any emission's antenna height. Zero means
unpublished.

STRUCTURE_COUNT.description:
Number of antenna-supporting structures at the facility. Zero means
unpublished.

EMISSIONS.description: Every emission the facility is documented to radiate.

FIRST_OBSERVED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond bounds of the documentation or observation
window backing the published record.

SOURCES.description:
Every source consulted for this facility, including sources that returned
nothing. Required: a facility with no named sources is not publishable.

CONSENSUS.description:
How the entries in SOURCES were reduced to the published position.
Required: a published position always states the rule that produced it,
including SINGLE_SOURCE.

ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier for this schedule row, unique within its
record set.

SITE_ID.description:
`$TXS`.ID of the facility radiating this transmission. ABSENT when the
originating facility is unidentified or disputed; a row is publishable
without one and a consumer must not fabricate a join.

SITE_NATIVE_ID.description:
The source's own identifier for the transmitting facility, verbatim —
a register site code or a compilation's site abbreviation. Retained so a
row whose SITE_ID could not be resolved is still traceable.

STATION_NAME.description:
Station or service name verbatim as the source states it. A display name,
never an identifier.

STATION_IDENTITY.description:
Station identification radiated on this transmission, verbatim: a
callsign, a keyed or spoken identifier, or the identity string the source
publishes. Never synthesized and never inferred from frequency.

FREQUENCY_KHZ.description:
Assigned frequency in kilohertz, following the `$TXS` convention. Zero
means unpublished; a row whose frequency is unpublished is a facility
record, not a schedule row.

BANDWIDTH_KHZ.description:
Necessary or occupied bandwidth in kilohertz when the source states one
for this transmission. Zero means unpublished.

EMISSION_DESIGNATOR.description:
ITU emission designator verbatim. Authoritative over MODULATION whenever
both are present.

TIME_START_UTC.description:
Daily on-air window in Coordinated Universal Time, as four decimal digits
"HHMM". A window whose stop is not later than its start crosses midnight
and is read as continuing into the following day. Strings because the
register form is four digits with significant leading zeros and no date;
an integer would invite a consumer to treat 0000 as absence.

DAYS.description:
Days on which the window runs. An unset field means the source publishes
no day pattern.

IRREGULAR.description:
The transmission runs without a fixed daily window — as required, on
occurrence, or continuously. TIME_START_UTC and TIME_STOP_UTC are absent
in that case and are never filled with 0000/2400 to stand in for it.

VALID_FROM.description:
RFC 3339 UTC bounds over which this row is valid — the seasonal or
licence period. Either bound is absent when unpublished.

SEASON.description:
The source's own name for the validity period, verbatim: a season code, a
schedule edition, or a period label. Never parsed into VALID_FROM by this
standard.

TARGET_AREA.description:
Target area verbatim as the source states it, including its own zone or
region notation.

TARGET_ZONES.description:
Individual target zone identifiers verbatim when the source publishes a
list, one entry per zone, in source order.

TRANSMITTER_POWER_KW.description:
Transmitter output power for this transmission, kilowatts. Zero means
unpublished.

ANTENNA_AZIMUTH_DEG.description:
Main-lobe bearing for this transmission, degrees clockwise from true
north. Absent for a non-directional transmission, which is stated by
OMNIDIRECTIONAL and never by a bearing of zero.

ANTENNA_AZIMUTH_SECONDARY_DEG.description:
Secondary lobe bearing when the source publishes a slewed or dual-beam
antenna, degrees clockwise from true north.

OMNIDIRECTIONAL.description: The transmission is radiated without a preferred bearing.

ANTENNA_DESIGNATION.description:
Antenna designation verbatim as the source states it — a curtain-array
code, an antenna number, or a pattern identifier.

EMISSION_ID.description:
`$TXS`.EMISSIONS[].EMISSION_ID this row exercises, when the facility
record enumerates it.

FIRST_OBSERVED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond bounds of the observation window backing
the row, when observers rather than a register established it.

OBSERVATION_COUNT.description:
Independent observation reports behind the row. Zero means the source
publishes no count, never that the transmission was never heard.

SOURCES.description:
Every source consulted for this row, including sources that returned
nothing. Required: a schedule row with no named sources is not
publishable. The provenance table is the one this family already
publishes in `$TXS`; a schedule row and a facility carry provenance of
the same shape and are frequently reconciled from the same fetch.

PUBLISHER_EPM_CID.description: IPFS CID of the publisher `$EPM` that operates this broker

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: libp2p peer id of the publisher node hosting the broker

PROTOCOL_ID.description:
libp2p protocol the broker answers on
(e.g. "/space-data-network/module-delivery/1.0.0")

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESSES.description: Dialable multiformat addresses for the broker

BROKER_PUBLIC_KEY.description:
The broker's public key (from the key server's get_public_key) so the
buyer can pin it

LAST_HEARTBEAT_AT.description: Unix ms of the last successful probe/heartbeat

FIRST_SEEN_AT.description: Unix ms the store first saw this broker

UPDATED_AT.description: Unix ms this descriptor was last updated

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the publisher `$EPM` over the self-attested endpoint
fields; re-verified by the store's live probe

FSB.description:
FlatSQL Byte Stream — a bounded, typed chunk used for append/query and
opaque snapshot/WAL persistence. DATA carries at most one MiB so larger
inputs and snapshots are delivered as ordered chunks. The host may persist
canonical FSB bytes but must not interpret DATA as tables, rows, or SQL.

CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation name

RFB.description:
RF Band Specification

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE. Every frequency field in this table is MHz. Sources
that publish Hz (as open transmitter databases commonly do) MUST divide by
1e6 before encoding; sources
that publish kHz MUST divide by 1e3. BAUD is baud (symbols per second),
never kilobaud. Encoding a Hz value into a MHz field is a defect, not a
convention.

One RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION. A transceiver or
transponder is therefore represented as TWO RFB records — one UPLINK and
one DOWNLINK — sharing ID_TRANSMITTER, each carrying its own MODE,
FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and CENTER_FREQ.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalog number of the spacecraft carrying this emitter. Joins to
CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

ID_TRANSMITTER.description:
Identifier of the physical transmitter, transceiver or transponder this
record describes (e.g. an upstream transmitter database's UUID). Uplink
and downlink
records of the same device share this value.

LINK_DIRECTION.description: Direction of this emission relative to the spacecraft.

BAUD.description: Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud.

SERVICE.description: Regulatory/ITU service designation (e.g. Amateur, Earth Exploration).

INVERT.description: True when the modulation sideband is inverted.

IARU_COORDINATION.description: IARU frequency-coordination state (e.g. IARU Coordinated, Uncoordinated).

CITATION.description:
Attribution/citation string the source license requires this record to
carry downstream.

TIMCcsdsTimeCode.description: CCSDS time-code payload and preamble metadata.

PREAMBLE_FIELD2.description: Second CCSDS preamble field octet; ignored when not signaled by preamble 1.

AGENCY_DEFINED_EPOCH_ISO8601.description: Optional agency-defined epoch timestamp for agency epoch time codes.

CCSDS_EPOCH_ISO8601.description: Optional CCSDS epoch override timestamp; defaults to 1958-01-01T00:00:00 TAI.

TIMInstant.description: Numeric or textual instant tagged with its time system and representation.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system for this instant.

EPOCH_FORMAT.description: Interpretation of JULIAN_DATE, SECONDS, and ISO8601.

JULIAN_DATE.description: Julian Date or Modified Julian Date day value, selected by EPOCH_FORMAT.

SECONDS.description: Seconds for UNIX_SECONDS, GPS_SECONDS, GNSS_WEEK_SECONDS, or MISSION_ELAPSED_SECONDS.

ISO8601.description: ISO 8601 timestamp text for ISO8601 inputs or display outputs.

SUBSECOND_NANOS.description: Additional nanoseconds beyond the fractional scalar/text value.

EPOCH_LABEL.description: Optional application-defined epoch label for MET, MRT, or SCLK values.

GNSS_WEEK.description: GNSS week number when EPOCH_FORMAT is GNSS_WEEK_SECONDS.

GNSS_ROLLOVER_REFERENCE_ISO8601.description: Optional Orekit-style GNSS week rollover reference timestamp.

CCSDS_TIME_CODE.description: CCSDS time-code payload when EPOCH_FORMAT is CCSDS_TIME_CODE.

TIMConversionRequest.description: Request to convert one instant into another time system/representation.

TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS.description: Optional TAI-UTC override in seconds for the source instant.

HAS_TAI_MINUS_UTC.description: Whether TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS should override runtime leap-second data.

DUT1_SECONDS.description: Optional UT1-UTC override in seconds for UT1 conversions.

HAS_DUT1.description: Whether DUT1_SECONDS should override runtime Earth-orientation data.

TRACE_ID.description: Optional caller trace/correlation identifier.

TIMConversionResult.description: Result of a time conversion request.

DELTA_SECONDS.description: Target minus source offset in SI seconds for the requested conversion.

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Optional error detail when STATUS is not OK.

TRACE_ID.description: Caller trace/correlation identifier copied from the request when present.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Legacy time-system selector retained for existing TIM consumers.

RFLObstruction.description:
One obstacle interaction on one sample's path. SPARSE: entries exist only
where an interaction was computed, so a clear path is never encoded as a
row of zeroes.

This is the join that makes an arbitrary 3D object a first-class part of
the link budget: MATERIAL_ID names the `$RFS` record whose permittivity,
conductivity, penetration loss and roughness produced LOSS_DB, and
GEOMETRY_REF_ID names the exact mesh, face set, panel or analytic shape
inside it that was hit.

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this interaction applies to.

OBSTACLE_ID.description: Producer's identifier for the obstacle instance.

MATERIAL_ID.description:
`$RFS.MATERIAL_ID` of the surface that was hit. An obstruction loss with
no material is an unattributed number: a metal panel and a plasterboard
wall of the same size do entirely different things to a link.

VAM_ID.description:
`$VAM` asset identity of the obstacle mesh, when the obstacle is a
reviewed 3D asset.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the obstacle is a catalogued object (an
occulting spacecraft, a structure on another vehicle). 0 when unbound.

INCIDENCE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Angle between the incident ray and the surface normal, degrees [0-90).

PATH_LENGTH_IN_MATERIAL_M.description:
Path length travelled INSIDE the material, metres. With
`$RFS.ATTENUATION_DB_PER_M` this is what makes penetration loss
reproducible instead of a stated constant.

EXCESS_DELAY_S.description: Extra propagation delay of a reflected or scattered component, seconds.

FRESNEL_CLEARANCE_FRACTION.description:
Fraction of the first Fresnel zone still clear [0-1]. 1 means the zone is
untouched.

DISTANCE_FROM_TRANSMITTER_M.description: Distance from the transmitter to the interaction point, metres.

RFLEndpoint.description:
One endpoint of a link. Identity ONLY — position, antenna geometry and band
capability are NOT copied here; they are joined from the standard named by
ENDPOINT_KIND. A copied position silently goes stale against its source.

ENDPOINT_ID.description: Producer-stable identifier for this endpoint within the record.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the endpoint is an on-orbit object. 0 when
unbound — never a placeholder catalogue number.

OBJECT_ID.description: International designator, `$CAT.OBJECT_ID`.

RFB_ID.description:
`$RFB.ID` — the band specification (frequency, bandwidth, EIRP, gains,
polarization) this endpoint transmits or receives on.

RFE_ID.description: `$RFE.ID` — the parametric emitter description, when one exists.

IQC_ID.description: `$IQC` capture identifier, when the samples were derived from a recording.

CHANNEL_ID.description: Channel or carrier identifier within the beam.

POLARIZATION.description:
Polarization actually used on this link. Defaults to UNKNOWN explicitly:
`rfPolarization` ordinal 0 is LHCP, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as a real polarization.

RFLModCod.description:
One modulation-and-coding choice available to a link. The table carries
engineering capability only; catalogue or recommendation names belong in
ID / NAME and provenance data, never in the schema vocabulary.

MODCOD_ID.description: Stable identifier within the containing link's MODCOD_SET.

CODE_RATE.description: Information bits divided by coded bits, in (0,1].

REQUIRED_MARGIN_DB.description: Additional implementation margin required before this entry is selected.

MAXIMUM_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Optional ceiling imposed by framing or implementation, bits per second.

RFLLink.description: One link whose budget is sampled by this record.

LINK_ID.description:
Producer-stable link identifier. Joins `$ACI.ACIInterval.LINK_ID` and
`$LKS.ID` when the same link also has an operational-state record.

CENTER_FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Carrier centre frequency actually used, megahertz — the `$RFB` MHz
convention, NOT the `$IQC` hertz convention. A consumer joining the two
converts explicitly at the join. Band designation is NOT duplicated here:
it is joined from `$RFB.BAND`.

MODULATION.description: Modulation as the producer states it (e.g. "QPSK", "8PSK", "16APSK").

CODING.description: Forward error correction scheme as the producer states it.

CODE_RATE.description: Code rate as a fraction (0-1].

SYMBOL_RATE_BAUD.description:
Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud — the `$RFB.BAUD`
convention.

DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Information bit rate the budget is stated for, bits per second.

THRESHOLD_TERM.description:
Required threshold this link is evaluated against. THRESHOLD_TERM,
THRESHOLD_VALUE, THRESHOLD_UNITS and THRESHOLD_COMPARISON are meaningful
only together; a LINK_MARGIN_DB column without them states a margin
against an unstated requirement and MUST be refused.

RECEIVER_GROUP_ID.description:
Receiver group this link belongs to. Links sharing a RECEIVER_GROUP_ID
and CHANNEL_GROUP_ID are mutually interfering and MUST be evaluated
together; a producer that shards a link matrix MUST keep a group intact
within one shard.

CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation or network this link belongs to.

SERVICE.description: Operator-facing service or mission designation.

MODCOD_SET.description:
Ordered adaptive modulation-and-coding choices. Per-sample
SELECTED_MODCOD_INDEX indexes this vector for the sample's selected link.

ACM_ENABLED.description: Whether the producer evaluated adaptive selection for this link.

RFLInterferenceContribution.description:
One interfering contribution to one sample. SPARSE: entries exist only
where a contribution was computed, so a dense matrix is never forced into
existence to say "no interference computed".

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this contribution applies to.

SOURCE_ENDPOINT_ID.description:
Endpoint identifier of the interfering emitter, when it is an endpoint of
this record.

RFB_ID.description: `$RFB.ID` of the interfering emission.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Interfering object's catalogue number, 0 when unbound.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Received interfering power at the victim receiver, dBW.

TOPOCENTRIC_SEPARATION_DEG.description:
Angular separation between the wanted and interfering paths at the
victim receiver, degrees.

SPECTRAL_OVERLAP_FRACTION.description: Fraction of the victim's bandwidth overlapped by this emission [0-1].

POLARIZATION_ISOLATION_DB.description: Polarization isolation applied to this contribution, dB.

ANTENNA_DISCRIMINATION_DB.description: Discrimination applied from the victim antenna pattern, dB.

RFLModelParameter.description:
A named parameter of a model binding, with its unit stated. There is no
encoding for a parameter value without a unit.

TEXT_VALUE.description: Non-numeric parameter value, when the parameter is categorical.

RFLModelBinding.description:
Which model produced one term of the budget. A loss term without a model
binding is an unattributed number: rain attenuation from two different
recommendations differs by decibels, and a consumer must be able to tell
which one it is holding.

TERM.description: The budget term this binding produced.

MODEL_NAME.description:
Model or recommendation identifier as its publisher states it (e.g. an
ITU-R recommendation number with its revision).

MODULE_ID.description: `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` of the module that evaluated it.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact artifact that produced the values.

RFLProvenance.description: Where this sample set came from, stated once for the record.

SOURCE.description:
The producing system, dataset or measurement campaign. Required: a
budget time series with no stated source is not publishable.

SOURCE_QUERY.description: Replayable query or scenario reference that regenerates this set.

PROPAGATOR_ID.description:
Identifier of the propagator that produced the geometry columns. A record
whose METHOD is MODELED or HYBRID and which carries geometry columns MUST
name it: geometry is only as good as the propagator, and the propagator is
a pluggable choice, never an assumed default.

PROPAGATOR_CONFIGURATION.description: Force model or configuration identifier handed to the propagator.

SAMPLING_STEP_S.description: Uniform sampling step, seconds. Absent when SAMPLE_EPOCHS are irregular.

ENVIRONMENT_DATASET.description:
Weather or environment dataset the atmospheric terms were evaluated
against, when they were not evaluated against a statistical model.

TERRAIN_DATASET.description: Terrain or surface dataset the blockage terms were evaluated against.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this set was computed or recorded.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: Unix ms the upstream inputs were retrieved.

LICENSE.description:
Licence the source imposes on redistribution. An empty LICENSE means
UNKNOWN TERMS — never public domain, never a grant to redistribute.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: True when the licence forbids commercial use of this set.

CITATION.description: Attribution the licence requires this record to carry downstream.

MODULE_ID.description:
Primary `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` that produced this record.
MODELS remains the per-budget-term attribution surface.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact producing WASM artifact.

RFL_ID.description: Stable identifier of this sample set.

SCENARIO_ID.description:
Analysis or scenario grouping identifier shared with the `$ACI` and
`$CVP` products derived from this set.

LINKS.description: Link definitions. SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES index into this vector.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description:
Number of samples. Every present metric array MUST have exactly this
many entries.

SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES.description: Index into LINKS for each sample.

SAMPLE_EPOCHS.description:
Sample epochs, seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 in TIME_SYSTEM. Samples
need not be uniformly spaced and need not be grouped by link, but MUST be
non-decreasing within each link.

TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time scale SAMPLE_EPOCHS are expressed in. Defaults to UTC explicitly:
`timingStandard` ordinal 0 is GMST, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as sidereal time.

RANGE_RATE_M_S.description: Range rate, metres per second; positive is opening.

AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the receiving endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the receiving endpoint, degrees above the local horizon.

TRANSMIT_AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the transmitting endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

TRANSMIT_ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the transmitting endpoint, degrees.

DOPPLER_SHIFT_HZ.description:
Doppler shift of the carrier, hertz; positive is closing. Hertz, not the
MHz used for frequencies elsewhere in this record — a shift of a few kHz
on a GHz carrier is destroyed by an MHz encoding.

EIRP_DBW.description: Effective isotropic radiated power toward the receiver, dBW.

TRANSMIT_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Transmit antenna gain in the direction of the receiver, dBi.

RECEIVE_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Receive antenna gain in the direction of the transmitter, dBi.

LINK_MARGIN_DB.description:

NSTNode.description:
Node Status Record (NST)
Description
Presence and identity of the peers a node knows about, as a node reports
them to operator dashboards: who the peer is (its identity record fields),
how it can be reached, whether it is online, where it is, which software
and standards versions it runs, and how the row reached the board. The
SOURCE field is the provenance of the row itself so an operator can always
answer "how did this peer get here?": declared in configuration, pinned by
an operator, or seen on a live connection. A set carries every row the
emitting node currently admits and the emitting node's own row.
One known peer as reported by the emitting node.

DN.description: Distinguished name from the peer's identity record.

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Multiformat addresses the peer is known by.

LAST_SEEN.description: Unix seconds of last observation; 0 = never.

IS_SELF.description: True on the node emitting this set.

UPTIME_S.description: Seconds since the emitting process started (self only).

SOURCE.description:
How this row reached the board: exactly one of "config" (declared in the
node's configuration), "pinned" (pinned by an operator) or "connected"
(seen right now on a live connection).

PINNED.description:
True for configuration and operator pins; a pinned peer keeps its row
while unreachable.

PIN_NOTE.description:
For SOURCE "config" the configuration key an operator can edit; for
SOURCE "pinned" the operator's own note. Never a manufactured label.

CONNECTED_PEER_IDS.description: Peers this peer is currently connected to, for the connection graph.

STORAGE_DAEMON_VERSION.description: Version of the content-addressed storage daemon the peer runs.

Onion-service address when the peer is reachable over an anonymity
network.
