IQCGeolocation.description:
Geodetic position of the receiver at capture time.

A separate table because latitude/longitude 0,0 is a VALID coordinate: an
absent GEOLOCATION means "the source published no position", which a
zero-defaulted scalar pair could never express.

LATITUDE_DEG.description: Geodetic latitude, degrees, WGS-84, positive north.

LONGITUDE_DEG.description: Geodetic longitude, degrees, WGS-84, positive east.

ALTITUDE_M.description:
Height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, metres. Absent in most SigMF
recordings; SigMF `core:geolocation` is a GeoJSON Point whose third
ordinate is optional.

UNCERTAINTY_M.description: Reported position uncertainty, metres, when the source states one.

METHOD.description:
How the position was obtained, verbatim from the source (e.g. "GPS",
"station registry", "author-supplied"). Never inferred.

IQCHardware.description:
Receive chain that produced the samples.

Every field is a verbatim string. SigMF `core:hw` is free text and the
non-SigMF archives publish nothing more structured; splitting free text
into a manufacturer and a model by guessing is a defect.

DESCRIPTION.description:
SigMF `core:hw` verbatim, or the source's equivalent free-text
description of the receive chain.

MANUFACTURER.description: Receiver manufacturer, only when the source names it as its own field.

MODEL.description: Receiver model, only when the source names it as its own field.

ANTENNA.description: Antenna description, only when the source names it as its own field.

RECORDER.description: SigMF `core:recorder` — the SOFTWARE that wrote the recording.

IQCSegment.description:
One SigMF capture segment: the point in the sample stream at which the
listed tuning took effect. A retuned or frequency-hopped recording has
several; a single-tune recording has one.

SAMPLE_START.description: SigMF `core:sample_start` — index of the first sample of this segment.

GLOBAL_INDEX.description:
SigMF `core:global_index` — index of this sample in the receiver's
free-running sample counter.

HEADER_BYTES.description:
SigMF `core:header_bytes` — bytes preceding this segment in the data
file.

CENTER_FREQ_HZ.description: SigMF `core:frequency` — centre frequency of this segment, HERTZ.

DATETIME.description: SigMF `core:datetime` — ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of SAMPLE_START.

IQCAnnotation.description: One labelled region of the capture in time and frequency.

SAMPLE_START.description: SigMF `core:sample_start` — first sample of the annotated region.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description: SigMF `core:sample_count` — length of the annotated region in samples.

FREQ_LOWER_EDGE_HZ.description: SigMF `core:freq_lower_edge` — lower edge of the annotated band, HERTZ.

FREQ_UPPER_EDGE_HZ.description: SigMF `core:freq_upper_edge` — upper edge of the annotated band, HERTZ.

GENERATOR.description:
SigMF `core:generator` — the tool or person that produced the
annotation. An annotation asserted by an automatic classifier and one
asserted by a human are not interchangeable evidence; this field is how
a consumer tells them apart.

UUID.description: SigMF `core:uuid` — the annotation's own identifier, when present.

IQCExtension.description: A SigMF extension namespace the upstream metadata declares.

IS_OPTIONAL.description: True when the extension is declared optional for interpretation.

IQCPayloadRef.description:
A retrievable file belonging to this capture.

The record NEVER carries sample bytes. It carries where they are, how big
they are, and what they hash to, so a consumer can decide for itself
whether to fetch 400 kB or 127 GB.

FILE_NAME.description: File name as the source publishes it.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: IANA media type when the source declares one.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length. 0 means the source did not publish a size — it never means
an empty file.

BYTE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the exact bytes, lowercase hex. Populated only when computed
or published; never guessed.

BYTE_SHA512.description:
SHA-512 of the exact bytes, lowercase hex. SigMF `core:sha512` is a
SHA-512 over the dataset file, so it is carried in its own field rather
than converted or discarded.

CID.description: IPFS CIDv1 when, and only when, this SDN pinned the bytes.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC time at which URL was last confirmed retrievable.

IQC.description:
RF IQ Capture Metadata.

The description of ONE raw, un-demodulated complex-baseband recording held
in a public archive — a hosted IQ-capture repository, a crowdsourced
signal-identification catalog, an institutional dataset repository, an
SDR project's capture database, a general-purpose research data archive —
normalized onto the SigMF v1 core namespace, which is the only metadata
vocabulary these archive classes share.

$IQC is a POINTER RECORD. It exists so a capture is discoverable, joinable
and verifiable without anyone mirroring its payload: the samples stay where
their publisher put them and `PAYLOADS` says where that is, how large it
is, and what it hashes to. `iqcCustody.PINNED` is a deliberate per-capture
decision for small high-value recordings, never a default.

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE AND NAMED IN EVERY FIELD. SigMF publishes frequency and
sample rate in HERTZ, so every frequency and rate field here is `_HZ` and
carries the Hz value unconverted. This standard deliberately does NOT
follow $RFB's MHz convention — silently rescaling a SigMF value on ingest
is the exact defect the suffix exists to prevent. A consumer joining $IQC
to $RFB divides by 1e6 at the join, explicitly.

LICENCE IS NEVER ASSUMED. An empty `LICENSE` means the terms are UNKNOWN.
It does not mean public domain, it does not mean permissive, and it does
not authorize redistribution. Crowdsourced catalogs and hosted repositories
both carry third-party recordings, so licence is per RECORDING, never per
archive.

Division of labour: $RFO = a sensor's astrometric/RF observation of a
tracked object (azimuth, elevation, range); $RFE = the parametric emitter
description; $RFB = the emitter's band specification in MHz; $IQC = the
archived baseband recording itself. $DPM remains the manifest under which
THIS network publishes a shard of $IQC records; it does not describe an
upstream third party's capture.

CAPTURE_ID.description: The upstream archive's own identifier for this capture, verbatim.

SOURCE_NAME.description:
Name of the archive that publishes the capture, carried verbatim as that
archive states it. A string rather than an enum so a new archive lane
never requires a schema release.

SOURCE_URL.description: Landing page for the capture at the source.

SOURCE_RECORD_ID.description:
Identifier of the source record this was normalized from, when the
source exposes one distinct from CAPTURE_ID.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the raw upstream metadata bytes that produced this record,
lowercase hex. Makes the normalization auditable.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC time the source metadata was retrieved.

SIGMF_VERSION.description:
SigMF `core:version` — the SigMF specification version the upstream
metadata declares. Empty for captures normalized from a non-SigMF
source; that emptiness is itself informative.

COLLECTION.description:
SigMF `core:collection` — identifier of the collection this recording
belongs to.

DATATYPE.description:
SigMF `core:datatype` VERBATIM, e.g. "cf32_le", "ci16_le", "ru8". Never
re-spelled, never normalized to another vocabulary. A consumer that
cannot parse the token MUST refuse the samples rather than assume a
layout.

NUM_CHANNELS.description:
SigMF `core:num_channels`. 0 means unstated; 1 is the SigMF default and
MUST be written explicitly when known.

CENTER_FREQ_HZ.description:
Centre frequency of the FIRST capture segment, HERTZ, copied here for
indexing. `SEGMENTS` is normative whenever it is present.

FREQ_LOWER_EDGE_HZ.description:
Lowest occupied frequency across the recording, HERTZ, when the source
states it or its annotations bound it.

FREQ_UPPER_EDGE_HZ.description: Highest occupied frequency across the recording, HERTZ.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description:
Total complex samples in the recording. 0 means unstated — it is NOT to
be back-computed from BYTE_LENGTH unless DATATYPE and any header bytes
are both known.

DURATION_SECONDS.description:
Recording length in seconds, when stated or exactly derivable from
SAMPLE_COUNT and SAMPLE_RATE_HZ.

SAMPLE_OFFSET.description:
SigMF `core:offset` — index of the first sample in the recording's own
numbering.

METADATA_ONLY.description:
SigMF `core:metadata_only` — true when no dataset file accompanies the
metadata.

TRAILING_BYTES.description:
SigMF `core:trailing_bytes` — non-sample bytes at the end of the data
file.

CAPTURE_START.description:
ISO 8601 UTC start of the recording (the first segment's
`core:datetime`).

CAPTURE_STOP.description: ISO 8601 UTC end of the recording, when stated or exactly derivable.

LABELS.description:
Archive-level tags, categories or keywords, carried verbatim in whatever
vocabulary the publishing archive uses.

GEOLOCATION.description: Receiver position. Absent when the source published none.

SIGNAL_NAME.description:
Signal designation the source states, verbatim ("LoRa", "DVB-S2",
"ADS-B", "VOR"). Not an enum: these archives catalogue the whole radio
world, and $RFE's `signalModulation` is a radar-emitter vocabulary that
would force every civil waveform into UNKNOWN.

MODULATION.description: Modulation the source states, verbatim. Never inferred from the samples.

BAND.description:
Band designation the source states. Shares $RFB's `rfBandDesignation`, so
an HF or VHF capture is designated identically on both records.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalogue number of the transmitting spacecraft when the capture
is of a known space object. Joins to $CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

OBJECT_ID.description: International designator of the transmitting spacecraft, when known.

EMITTER_ID.description: $RFE.ID of the emitter this capture is of, when identified.

RFB_ID.description:
$RFB.ID of the band specification this capture exercises, when
identified.

LICENSE.description:
SPDX identifier when the source states one, otherwise the source's
licence name verbatim. EMPTY MEANS UNKNOWN TERMS — never public domain.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the licence text the source points at.

ATTRIBUTION.description:
Attribution/citation string the licence requires this record and any
derived product to carry downstream.

CREATED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC creation time of this record.

UPDATED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC last-update time of this record.

SUPERSEDES_IQC_CID.description:
CID of the $IQC this record replaces, when the upstream capture's
metadata changed.

IRMSource.description:
The source object a job is reading, and the validators that prove a resumed
read is reading the same bytes.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable locator of the source object, verbatim.

SOURCE_OBJECT_ID.description:
Source-native object, export, or product identifier verbatim, when the
provider names one independently of its locator.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier pinning the exact source bytes, when the source is
content-addressed.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: Media type of the source object verbatim as the provider states it.

TOTAL_BYTES.description:
Total length of the source object in bytes. 0 means the provider did not
state a length; it never means an empty object.

ENTITY_TAG.description: Opaque entity validator verbatim as the provider published it.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the complete source object as 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters, when the provider publishes one. Never computed from a partial
read.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: Provider-stated edition, revision, or release marker verbatim.

VALIDATOR_MATCH.description: What the publisher concluded when it last compared validators.

VALIDATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of that comparison.

IRMDecodeContext.description:
Everything a resuming reader needs to decode a chunk that does not begin at
offset 0. Required whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header.

FORMAT.description:
Format token the decoder dispatches on, verbatim and lowercase, e.g.
`text/csv`. A consumer that does not implement the format refuses the chunk
rather than guessing at a layout.

HEADER_LINE.description:
The source's header line verbatim, exactly as it appeared at offset 0 and
excluding its line terminator. This is the field that makes chunk N>0
decodable; without it a headerless chunk parses to zero rows and looks like
a clean tail.

HEADER_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length the header occupied at the start of the source, including its
terminator, so a reader can tell a header-bearing prefix from a data row.

COLUMN_NAMES.description:
Column names in source order, when the publisher parsed them. Advisory:
HEADER_LINE is authoritative and a disagreement is resolved in its favour.

CHARSET.description: Character encoding label verbatim as the provider states it.

COMPRESSION.description:
Stream-compression codec applied to the source bytes, verbatim and
lowercase. Empty means the ranged bytes are read as-is. Non-empty means
NEXT_OFFSET is a position in the COMPRESSED stream and DECODER_STATE,
WINDOW and PARTIAL_RECORD are all required to resume.

DECODED_OFFSET.description:
Position in the DECODED stream corresponding to NEXT_OFFSET, when the
source is compressed. 0 with a non-empty COMPRESSION means the decoded
stream has not been advanced.

DECODER_STATE.description:
Serialized, pointer-free image of the decoder at the seam — the state a
codec with no restart point needs in order to have one. Opaque to every
consumer but a decoder whose stamps match exactly. Never partially applied.

DECODER_STATE_FORMAT.description:
Layout identifier of DECODER_STATE, verbatim, naming the decoder struct the
image was taken from. A consumer that does not know the token restarts.

DECODER_STATE_VERSION.description: Version of that layout, verbatim. Any disagreement restarts the job.

DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length DECODER_STATE is expected to have. Carried even though the
vector knows its own size, so a size disagreement is detectable BEFORE the
image is loaded into a differently shaped struct.

DECODER_STATE_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of DECODER_STATE as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

DECODER_BUILD_ID.description:
Build identifier of the decoder that produced DECODER_STATE, verbatim, so
two builds of one codec version are still distinguishable.

DECODER_STATE_MEDIA_TYPE.description:
Media type of DECODER_STATE, so an unrelated decoder refuses it instead of
misreading it.

WINDOW.description:
The decoder's history window at the seam — the bytes that ARE the codec's
back-reference dictionary. Carried separately from DECODER_STATE because it
is bulk data of a size the codec fixes, not part of the struct image.

WINDOW_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length WINDOW is expected to have, for the same detect-before-load
reason as DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.

WINDOW_POSITION.description:
Offset into WINDOW at which the codec will next write, when the window is
a circular buffer whose contents cannot be interpreted without it.

PARTIAL_RECORD.description:
The bytes of the record that straddles the seam: everything the previous
chunk decoded of a record it could not finish. A resuming decoder prepends
these to the next chunk's decoded output before parsing. Carried as bytes,
not text, because a seam may fall inside a multi-byte character.

IRMChunk.description: One chunk that was read and durably committed.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based position of the chunk in the job's read sequence.

BATCH_ID.description:
Publisher-stable batch identifier the chunk's records were stored under,
verbatim, so a consumer can join the mark to the stored rows.

RANGE_FIRST_BYTE.description: First byte of the range that was read.

RANGE_LAST_BYTE.description:
Last byte of the range that was read. Interpreted per RANGE_MODE:
inclusive under INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE, exclusive under OFFSET_LENGTH.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Bytes the read actually returned, which may be shorter than the range
requested.

CHUNK_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

RECORDS_DECODED.description: Records the decoder produced from the chunk.

RECORDS_STORED.description:
Records the storage lane reported as durably committed. A chunk whose
stored count is 0 is not marked at all.

RECORDS_REJECTED.description: Records the storage lane rejected or collapsed as duplicates.

ATTEMPTS.description: Number of read attempts this chunk cost, including the successful one.

COMMITTED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the storage lane
confirmed the commit.

IRMFault.description: The last unrecovered error, carried so a resumed run can refuse to loop.

CODE.description: Publisher-stable error code verbatim.

MESSAGE.description: Human-readable message verbatim; never a substitute for CODE.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of the chunk the fault occurred on.

CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.description: Consecutive failed attempts at that chunk.

OCCURRED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of the fault.

RETRY_NOT_BEFORE.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp before which a consumer must not
retry. Empty means the publisher states no backoff.

JOB_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the ingest job. Together with the publishing
key it is the job's identity across every mark it emits.

SEQUENCE.description:
Monotonic version of this mark within JOB_ID. Highest wins per publishing
key. Never reused, never decremented.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the data provider being read, verbatim.
Publisher data: it may name a real provider.

INGESTOR_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS identifier of the ingest module or flow that owns the job, so
two pipelines reading one provider do not share a resume point.

SOURCE.description: The source object and its validators.

RANGE_MODE.description: How byte positions in this mark are addressed.

NEXT_OFFSET.description:
Byte offset at which the next read begins, in the SOURCE's own byte stream:
the compressed stream when DECODE_CONTEXT.COMPRESSION is non-empty, in
which case it is a record boundary only in company with the decoder state,
window and partial record. On an uncompressed source it is ALWAYS a
complete-record boundary, corrected backwards from the previous chunk's
byte budget. 0 is a valid value and means the job has committed nothing yet.

NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index of the next chunk to read. With PART_INDEX addressing this
is the only position.

CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET.description:
Byte budget the publisher reads per chunk. Records the ceiling the job
actually ran under, which a host may have clamped below the configured one.

DECODE_CONTEXT.description:
Everything needed to decode the chunk at NEXT_OFFSET. REQUIRED in practice
whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header; a consumer that finds
it absent there restarts from offset 0 rather than decoding blind.

LAST_CHUNK.description: The chunk this mark was advanced from — the last one durably committed.

CHUNKS_COMMITTED.description: Chunks durably committed by this job so far.

BYTES_COMMITTED.description: Source bytes accounted for by committed chunks.

RECORDS_COMMITTED.description: Records durably committed by this job so far, across every chunk.

TARGET_STANDARD.description:
Four-character standard code of the records this job writes, `$` included,
e.g. `$TBS`. Never a union ordinal.

RECONCILE_MODE.description:
Reconciliation mode the storage lane was called with, verbatim, e.g.
`append`. A chunked job never reconciles per batch: reconciling would delete
every earlier chunk as the next one arrived.

MERGE_POLICY.description: Deduplication or merge policy the job applied, verbatim.

FAULT.description: The last unrecovered error, when there is one.

CREATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job was created.

STARTED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the first chunk was read.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which this mark was published.
With JOB_ID and SEQUENCE this is the version key; SEQUENCE breaks ties.

COMPLETED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job reached COMPLETE.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp after which a consumer treats the
mark as stale and re-validates the source before resuming. Empty means the
publisher states no expiry.

MDPEncounterStage.description:
One encounter stage of the body sequence: the set of bodies admissible at
this position in the sequence, and the epoch grid searched for it.

Bodies are named by NAIF integer ID, which is normative. SDS carries no
body enum and $GRV.CentralBody is gravity-model-scoped and incomplete, so it
must not be repurposed here. Note that a barycenter and a body center are
different objects (4 is the Mars barycenter, 499 is Mars) and the
distinction is operationally load-bearing.

STAGE_INDEX.description: Zero-based position in the ordered sequence.

ALLOWED_BODY_NAIF_IDS.description: NAIF integer IDs admissible at this stage. A single entry pins the body.

ALLOWED_BODY_NAMES.description: Advisory names, parallel to ALLOWED_BODY_NAIF_IDS when present.

EPOCH_WINDOW_START.description: Earliest and latest epoch searched at this stage, ISO 8601.

EPOCH_GRID_STEP_DAYS.description: Epoch grid step searched within the window, days.

V_INFINITY_MIN_KM_S.description: Bounds on hyperbolic excess speed at this encounter, km/s.

MIN_FLYBY_ALTITUDE_KM.description: Minimum admissible flyby altitude above the body's reference surface, km.

MAX_POWERED_FLYBY_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on powered-flyby delta-V applied at this encounter, km/s.

MDPFlightTimeBound.description:
Time-of-flight bound between two encounters. Adjacent stages give per-leg
bounds; non-adjacent stages give cumulative bounds such as
"Earth to Mars to Earth within 3 years".

FROM_STAGE_INDEX.description: Stage indices the bound spans. TO_STAGE_INDEX > FROM_STAGE_INDEX.

MIN_DAYS.description: Inclusive bounds on elapsed time between those two encounters, days.

MDP.description:
Mission Design Problem — the definition of a patched-conic broad search over
an ordered sequence of body encounters.

This is the PROBLEM, not a solution: it states what is being searched and
under what constraints. Candidate trajectories produced by solving it are
carried in $MDS. Nothing existing covers this: $LMS is a single Lambert
boundary-value problem with no body/epoch grid and no sequence, $MPE is an
Earth mean-element targeter, $MNF is an Earth manifold sweep, and $MNV is an
SSA-detected maneuver on a catalogued Earth object.

PROBLEM_ID.description: Stable identifier for this problem definition.

ENCOUNTER_STAGES.description: Ordered encounter stages. Order in this vector IS the body sequence.

MAX_TOTAL_FLIGHT_TIME_DAYS.description: Cap on total mission duration, days.

MAX_LAUNCH_C3_KM2_S2.description: Cap on launch characteristic energy C3, km^2/s^2.

MAX_TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on total post-launch delta-V, km/s.

MAX_DSM_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on the magnitude of any single deep-space maneuver, km/s.

DSM_GRID_STEP_KM_S.description: Grid step used when searching deep-space maneuver magnitude, km/s.

MAX_REVOLUTIONS.description:
Lambert controls: maximum number of complete revolutions considered on a
leg, and the admissible transfer direction.

OUTPUT_TIME_BIN_DAYS.description:
Output decimation: width of the time bin within which only the best
candidate is retained. Zero means no decimation.

MAX_THRUST_N.description: Optional spacecraft propulsion limits constraining admissible solutions.

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description:
Ephemeris source the search was posed against, e.g. a SPICE kernel set
identifier. Recorded so a solution set can be reproduced.

MDSEncounter.description:
One body encounter along a candidate trajectory.

Encounter-indexed rather than leg-indexed on purpose. A search implementation
typically emits leg-indexed arrays: for nE encounters there are nL = nE - 1
legs, the departure v-infinity of leg i is the OUTGOING vector at encounter
i, and the arrival v-infinity of leg i is the INCOMING vector at encounter
i + 1. Carrying both vectors on the encounter they physically occur at
removes that off-by-one from every consumer.

BODY_NAIF_ID.description:
Body encountered, NAIF integer ID (normative). A barycenter is not the
body: 4 is the Mars barycenter, 499 is Mars.

EPOCH_ET_S.description:
Encounter epoch as ephemeris time, seconds past J2000 TDB. This is the
form solvers work in and is carried verbatim to avoid a lossy round trip.

EPOCH_UTC.description:
Same epoch in ISO 8601 (UTC), for consumers that do not carry an
ephemeris time implementation. Advisory; EPOCH_ET_S is normative.

INCOMING_V_INFINITY_X_KM_S.description:
Incoming hyperbolic excess velocity vector, km/s. Absent at the first
encounter.

OUTGOING_V_INFINITY_X_KM_S.description:
Outgoing hyperbolic excess velocity vector, km/s. Absent at the final
encounter.

TURN_ANGLE_RAD.description: Turn angle between incoming and outgoing asymptotes, radians.

PERIAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description: Flyby periapsis radius measured from the body's center, km.

POWERED_FLYBY_DELTA_V_KM_S.description:
Delta-V applied at periapsis for a powered flyby, km/s. Zero for an
unpowered (ballistic) flyby.

LAMBERT_SOLUTION_INDEX.description:
Index of the Lambert solution selected for the leg DEPARTING this
encounter, as reported by the solver.

FLYBY_SOLUTION_INDEX.description:
Index of the flyby solution branch selected at this encounter, as
reported by the solver.

MDSDeepSpaceManeuver.description: One deep-space maneuver on a transfer leg.

LEG_INDEX.description:
Zero-based leg the maneuver occurs on. Leg i connects encounter i to

ARC_FRACTION.description: Position along the leg as a fraction of its flight time, in [0, 1].

EPOCH_ET_S.description:
Maneuver epoch as ephemeris time, seconds past J2000 TDB, when the solver
reports it directly.

DELTA_V_X_KM_S.description: Maneuver vector when the solver reports one, km/s.

CANDIDATE_ID.description: Solver-assigned trajectory identifier, unique within the set.

DEEP_SPACE_MANEUVERS.description: Deep-space maneuvers, ordered by LEG_INDEX then ARC_FRACTION.

TOTAL_FLIGHT_TIME_DAYS.description: Total flight time from first to last encounter, days.

ARRIVAL_V_INFINITY_KM_S.description: Hyperbolic excess speed at arrival, km/s.

ESCAPE_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Reference escape delta-V from the departure body, km/s.

INSERTION_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Reference insertion delta-V at the arrival body, km/s.

NON_DOMINATED.description:
True when this candidate is non-dominated within the set. A set MAY carry
dominated candidates for context; a consumer plotting a front MUST filter

MDS.description:
Mission Design Solution Set — a set of candidate trajectories produced by
solving a mission design broad search, typically a Pareto front over
competing objectives (total delta-V against total flight time).

SDS had no multi-candidate container of any kind before this record. The
closest existing carrier for a single planned burn is OCM.Maneuver, whose
payload is untyped DATA:[string] with MAN_UNITS:[string] and which has no
v-infinity, turn angle, flyby periapsis radius, or C3.

SOLUTION_SET_ID.description: Stable identifier for this solution set.

PROBLEM_ID.description:
PROBLEM_ID of the $MDP this set solves. A solution set whose problem
definition is unknown is not reproducible.

OBJECTIVES.description:
Objectives the front is expressed over, e.g.
["TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S", "TOTAL_FLIGHT_TIME_DAYS"]. Names MUST be field
names of MDSCandidate.

SOLVER.description: Solver identity and version that produced the set.

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description: Ephemeris source used, e.g. a SPICE kernel set identifier.

CREATION_DATE.description: When the set was generated, ISO 8601.

MEMErrorModel.description:
Noise, bias and editing rules for one observable. Standard deviations and
biases use the observable's SI unit. ANGLE observables use radians.

MEMEditingDecision.description:
One deterministic editing decision. The observation identity is carried
from the tracking-data input so rejected sets can be compared exactly.

MEMAttestation.description:
Dual-form signature. Presence means both signatures are required and both
MUST verify independently; an invalid member rejects the record rather
than downgrading it to unsigned.

MEM.description:
Measurement Error Model. JSON projections preserve these IDL-capitalized
field names exactly. The FlatBuffer signature covers the size-prefixed
buffer with both signature vectors zeroed; the canonical-JSON signature
covers RFC 8785 canonical JSON with both signature fields omitted.

One independently addressed segment inside a native container.

A segmented binary ephemeris is not a single span: each segment has its own

that says which states came from where and what must be written back.

Numeric segment data type, verbatim. The evaluation rule is a property of
this number (for example, Chebyshev position with fixed interval, or
discrete states with Lagrange interpolation); it is carried as the
container's own integer so a rewrite is exact.

START_SECONDS_PAST_J2000_TDB.description:
Segment coverage start, seconds past J2000 in the barycentric dynamical

INITIAL_ADDRESS.description: First addressed element of the segment inside the file.

FINAL_ADDRESS.description: Last addressed element of the segment inside the file.

POLYNOMIAL_DEGREE.description:
Polynomial degree or record size the segment type parameterises, when the
type carries one.

NCDSP3Header.description: Header block of a fixed-column satellite position container (SP3).

Record content indicator, e.g. "P" for positions only, "V" with

SATELLITE_SYSTEM.description: Satellite system indicator recorded in the header.

ORBIT_TYPE.description: Orbit type as recorded, e.g. fitted, extrapolated, broadcast, helmert.

DATA_USED.description: Data used to produce the file, as recorded.

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Terrestrial reference frame name as recorded.

AGENCY.description:
Producing agency as recorded IN THE FILE. This is observed content, not a
classification.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system as recorded in the header.

GPS_WEEK.description: Week number of the first epoch in the file's own week counter.

SECONDS_OF_WEEK.description: Seconds of week of the first epoch.

MODIFIED_JULIAN_DAY_START.description: Modified Julian Day of the first epoch.

FRACTIONAL_DAY.description: Fractional day of the first epoch.

NUMBER_OF_EPOCHS.description: Number of epochs declared in the header.

SATELLITE_ACCURACY_EXPONENTS.description:
Per-satellite accuracy exponents, parallel to SATELLITE_IDS. The accuracy
is POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE raised to this power.

POSITION_VELOCITY_BASE.description:
Base for the position and velocity standard-deviation exponents carried
per state in $OEM.

CLOCK_RATE_BASE.description: Base for the clock bias and clock rate standard-deviation exponents.

COMMENT.description: Header comment lines in file order.

NCDScenarioEpochContainer.description: Parameters of a scenario-epoch text container.

SCENARIO_EPOCH.description: Epoch that every record offset is measured from, ISO 8601.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time scale the scenario epoch is expressed in.

DISTANCE_UNIT.description: Distance unit of the records, e.g. "Meters", "Kilometers".

COORDINATE_SYSTEM.description: Named coordinate system of the records.

COORDINATE_AXES.description: Named coordinate axes, when stated separately from the system.

INTERPOLATION_SAMPLES_M1.description:
Interpolation order expressed as (samples - 1), which is how these
containers state it. Carried verbatim rather than converted, so a rewrite
reproduces the source exactly.

NUMBER_OF_EPHEMERIS_POINTS.description: Number of ephemeris points declared in the container.

SEGMENT_BOUNDARY_TIMES.description: Segment boundary offsets in seconds from SCENARIO_EPOCH, when present.

NCDCode500Header.description: Header words of a fixed-record binary ephemeris container.

SATELLITE_NAME.description: Object name as recorded in the header.

EPOCH_STEP_SECONDS.description: Uniform step between data records, seconds.

HEADER_WORDS.description:
The header record's packed words in file order, undecoded. A reader that
understands a word decodes it; a rewriter reproduces the record exactly
without having to.

NCD.description:
Native Container Descriptor.

The file-level facts of an ephemeris, attitude or tracking container that
are NOT properties of the messages inside it. $OEM, $AEM and $TDM carry the
states, attitudes and observations; none of them can carry the internal
file name, the comment area, the segment address ranges, the header accuracy
block or the interpolation order the source declared, because those describe
the CONTAINER. Without them a read-then-write cycle silently invents header
values, and a segmented binary file cannot be reproduced at all.

ONE record covers every container class rather than one record per format:
the file-level facts are the same kind of fact in each, and the
format-specific blocks are optional sub-tables selected by FORMAT. Only the
block matching FORMAT is populated.

PROVIDER_DEFINED_FORMAT_NAME.description: Format name when FORMAT is PROVIDER_DEFINED. Empty otherwise.

FORMAT_VERSION.description: Version of the container format as declared by the file itself.

PRODUCER.description: Producing system or organization as recorded IN THE FILE.

CREATION_DATE.description: Creation date recorded in the file, ISO 8601.

INTERNAL_FILE_NAME.description:
Container-internal file name, which is stored inside the file and is
independent of the name on disk.

COMMENT_AREA.description:
Free-text comment area carried inside the container, one entry per line,
in file order.

NATIVE_FRAME_NAME.description:
Reference frame name as the container itself spells it, before any
mapping onto $RFM.

NATIVE_FRAME_ID.description: Integer reference frame code as the container stores it.

NATIVE_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system as the container itself spells it, before any mapping onto
the ratified time-scale vocabulary.

SEGMENTS.description:
Descriptors of the container's segments, in file order. Empty for a
single-span container.

SP3_HEADER.description: Header block when FORMAT is SP3_C or SP3_D.

SCENARIO_CONTAINER.description:
Parameters when FORMAT is SCENARIO_EPOCH_EPHEMERIS_TEXT or
SCENARIO_EPOCH_ATTITUDE_TEXT.

CODE_500_HEADER.description: Header words when FORMAT is CODE_500.

START_TIME.description: Total coverage start across all segments, ISO 8601.

STOP_TIME.description: Total coverage stop across all segments, ISO 8601.

SOURCE_BYTE_LENGTH.description: Length of the described container in bytes.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the described container's exact bytes, lowercase hex. This is
what makes the descriptor checkable: a consumer can prove the descriptor
belongs to the file it holds.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier of the described container when it is addressed by
content rather than by path.

NDSSchemaStat.description: One standard's record footprint in the node store.

NEWEST_EPOCH_MS.description: Newest record epoch held, Unix milliseconds; 0 = unknown.

OLDEST_EPOCH_MS.description: Oldest record epoch held, Unix milliseconds; 0 = unknown.

One (standard, provider, source, batch) ingest lane's live progress and

UPDATED_AT.description: Unix seconds; 0 = unknown.

WINDOW_RECORDS.description: Records observed in the current rolling window.

PRIOR_WINDOW_RECORDS.description: Records observed in the immediately preceding rolling window.

PRODUCER_PEER_ID.description:
Peer identifier of the producer whose signed identity covers this lane's

PRODUCER_EPM_CID.description: Content identifier of the producer's identity record.

ORIGIN_ID.description:
Upstream publisher the producer retrieved the records from, as a host

ORIGIN_NAME.description: Display name of the upstream publisher.

SOURCE_URL.description: Upstream URL the records were retrieved from.

LICENSE.description: Licence under which the upstream publisher offers the records.

CONNECTOR_ID.description: Ingest connector that produced this lane (`$ICN` CONNECTOR_ID).

PUBLISHER_RUNG.description: Verification rung of the producer claim.

EVIDENCE.description: Evidence references supporting PUBLISHER_RUNG (record CIDs, proof ids).

LAST_PUBLICATION_CID.description: Content identifier of the lane's newest publication manifest.

LAST_PNM_CID.description: Content identifier of the lane's newest publish notification.

NDSIngestEvent.description: One source-ingest transition surfaced to the dashboard.

AT.description: Unix seconds when the transition occurred.

NDSTopicStat.description: Live traffic for one publish/subscribe topic.

NDSModuleStat.description: Runtime counters for one installed module or flow.

NDSTrustEngineStat.description: Counters for the node's trust rule evaluation engine.

MIN_INTERVAL_MS.description: Minimum interval between evaluation passes, milliseconds.

NDS.description: Node Data Statistics - one node's data-plane snapshot.

GENERATED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this snapshot was assembled.

STALE.description:
True when the assembling read hit its store budget and this snapshot
carries the last-known-good numbers.

AS_OF.description: Unix seconds the store numbers were last true; 0 = never read.

NSTNode.description:
Node Status Record (NST)
Description
Presence and identity of the peers a node knows about, as a node reports
them to operator dashboards: who the peer is (its identity record fields),
how it can be reached, whether it is online, where it is, which software
and standards versions it runs, and how the row reached the board. The
SOURCE field is the provenance of the row itself so an operator can always
answer "how did this peer get here?": declared in configuration, pinned by
an operator, or seen on a live connection. A set carries every row the
emitting node currently admits and the emitting node's own row.
One known peer as reported by the emitting node.

DN.description: Distinguished name from the peer's identity record.

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Multiformat addresses the peer is known by.

LAST_SEEN.description: Unix seconds of last observation; 0 = never.

LATENCY_MS.description: Round-trip latency to the peer, milliseconds; 0 = unknown.

VCARD.description: Full vCard 4.0 text derived from the peer's identity record.

IS_SELF.description: True on the node emitting this set.

UPTIME_S.description: Seconds since the emitting process started (self only).

SOURCE.description:
How this row reached the board: exactly one of "config" (declared in the
node's configuration), "pinned" (pinned by an operator) or "connected"
(seen right now on a live connection).

PINNED.description:
True for configuration and operator pins; a pinned peer keeps its row
while unreachable.

PIN_NOTE.description:
For SOURCE "config" the configuration key an operator can edit; for
SOURCE "pinned" the operator's own note. Never a manufactured label.

CONNECTED_PEER_IDS.description: Peers this peer is currently connected to, for the connection graph.

SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY.description: Signing public key from the peer's identity record.

ENCRYPTION_PUBLIC_KEY.description: Encryption public key from the peer's identity record.

EPM_CID.description: Content identifier of the peer's identity record.

STORAGE_DAEMON_VERSION.description: Version of the content-addressed storage daemon the peer runs.

ONION_ADDRESS.description:
Onion-service address when the peer is reachable over an anonymity
network.

NST.description: Node Status Record - the set of peers a node reports.

GENERATED_AT.description: Unix milliseconds when this set was generated.

SOURCE_PEER_ID.description: Peer identifier of the emitting node.

CARRY_ERROR.description: When true, PREVIOUS_ERROR is added to STATE before discretization.

PREVIOUS_ERROR.description: Optional prior discretization error vector from an earlier result.

TRACE_ID.description: Optional trace/correlation identifier.

NUMVectorDiscretizeResult.description: Result of one component-wise vector discretization operation.

DISCRETIZATION_ERROR.description: Input-minus-output error after any requested carried error was applied.

TRACE_ID.description: Caller trace/correlation identifier copied from the request when present.

NUMScalarInterpolationRequest.description: Request for one scalar interpolation operation.

NUMGaussMarkovRequest.description: Request for one first-order Gauss-Markov random sequence.

NUMGaussMarkovResult.description: Result of one first-order Gauss-Markov random sequence.

FINAL_STATE.description: State after the final generated sample.

TRACE_ID.description: Caller trace/correlation identifier copied from the request when present.

odSensorContribution.description: Sensor contribution to an orbit determination solution

SENSOR_ID.description: Sensor identifier

Reference Frame
Typically TEMEOFDATE

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time System [M, UTC]

SEMI_MAJOR_AXIS.description: Semi-major axis in km or Mean Motion in rev/day

EPHEMERIS_TYPE.description:
TLE Related Parameters (Only if MEAN_ELEMENT_THEORY=SGP/SGP4)
EPHEMERIS_TYPE Default=0

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: NORAD_CAT_ID (integer) [O if SGP/SGP4]

MEAN_MOTION_DOT.description: MEAN_MOTION_DOT in rev/day**2 [C if SGP or PPT3]

MEAN_MOTION_DDOT.description: MEAN_MOTION_DDOT in rev/day**3 if SGP/PPT3 or AGOM in m**2/kg if SGP4-XP [C]

Position/Velocity Covariance Matrix (6x6 Lower Triangular) [C if any covariance provided]

DESCRIPTION.description: Description of why object is of interest

QUANTITY.description: Number of solar arrays of this type

AREA.description: Total array area in square meters

POWER_BOL.description: Beginning of life power output in Watts

POWER_EOL.description: End of life power output in Watts

DEGRADATION_RATE.description: Degradation rate per year as fraction

PROPELLANT.description: Propellant type (e.g., HYDRAZINE, XENON, KRYPTON, MMH_NTO, N2, GN2)

OPPProvenance.description:
Provenance for exactly one physical value.

This table is the mechanism by which the never-invent-data law is enforced
in the IDL rather than in prose: no physical quantity in an $OPP can be
expressed without one of these attached, so a value with no admissible
source cannot be encoded at all. Unknown values are ABSENT. They are never
zero, never a placeholder, and never carried forward from a different
object.

SOURCE.description:
Publisher of the value, named as the publisher names itself — a space
agency's object database, a public satellite catalogue, a third-party
satellite reference site, or the operator itself.

SOURCE_RECORD_ID.description:
The source's own identifier for the record this value was read from, such
as that database's object id. Verbatim, never normalized.

SOURCE_URL.description: Deep link to the exact source record when the source publishes one.

EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) of the
instant the value describes: the epoch at which the property held. A
design or as-built value that does not change over time omits EPOCH.

RETRIEVED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) when
this record retrieved the value from SOURCE.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: The source's own revision, edition or publication marker, verbatim.

LICENSE.description: Terms under which SOURCE permits redistribution of the value, verbatim.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution string the source requires be displayed with the value.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the exact source
payload bytes the value was parsed from.

NOTES.description: Free text qualifying the value, such as the source's own caveat.

OPPQuantity.description:
One scalar physical quantity, its unit and its own provenance.

PROVENANCE is required: an OPPQuantity that exists names where it came from.
Presence of the table is the signal that a value exists, so VALUE zero is a
real zero (0 dBsm is 1 m2) and an unknown quantity omits the whole table.

UNITS.description:
Unit symbol verbatim, never silently converted: "kg", "m", "m2", "m2/kg",
"kg/m2", "dBsm", "W", "mag". A converted value states the unit it was
converted to and records the conversion in PROVENANCE.NOTES with
PROVENANCE.METHOD DERIVED.

SIGMA.description:
1-sigma uncertainty in UNITS. Zero means the source stated no uncertainty;
a genuine stated sigma is never exactly zero.

OPPRadarCrossSection.description:
Radar cross-section as reported for one band, polarization and aspect
convention. Radar cross-section is band- and aspect-dependent, so an $OPP
carries a list of these and never a single scalar. A source publishing
minimum, average and maximum cross-sections becomes three entries with
ASPECT MINIMUM, AVERAGE and MAXIMUM sharing one SOURCE.

BAND.description:
Radar band designation verbatim from the source: "UHF", "L", "S", "C",
"X", "Ku". Empty when the source states no band.

FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Centre frequency [megahertz] when the source states one. Zero means
unstated.

POLARIZATION.description:
Polarization verbatim from the source: "HH", "VV", "HV", "RCRC". Empty
when the source states none.

CROSS_SECTION.description:
The cross-section itself. UNITS is "m2" or "dBsm" as the source published
it; the two are never mixed within one entry and never silently converted.

SIZE_CLASS.description:
Size bucket verbatim when a source publishes a bucket instead of a number,
such as a public catalogue's "SMALL", "MEDIUM", "LARGE". A bucket is never
turned into a number.

SENSOR.description: Sensor or facility that produced the measurement, when stated.

OPPMass.description:
Mass breakdown. Each component is independently sourced; a wet mass and a
dry mass may legitimately come from different publishers and epochs.

WET.description: Mass with propellant, at the stated epoch [kg].

LAUNCH.description: Mass at separation from the launch vehicle [kg].

PROPELLANT.description: Propellant mass at the stated epoch [kg].

PAYLOAD.description: Payload mass carried by the bus [kg].

CURRENT.description: Best current estimate of mass at the record's epoch [kg].

OPPDimensions.description:
Physical envelope. Every extent is a sourced quantity. Extents measured off
3D-asset geometry carry PROVENANCE.METHOD MODEL_DERIVED and describe the
model, not the flight article.

BODY_X.description: Extents along the object's own body axes [m].

HEIGHT.description: Envelope terms as an object database publishes them [m].

SHAPE.description:
Gross geometric shape verbatim from the source, such as a shape string
of the form "Box + 1 Pan" or "Cyl". Never parsed into geometry.

SHAPE_PROVENANCE.description: Provenance of SHAPE. Present whenever SHAPE is nonempty.

OPPAreas.description: Projected areas and the ratios derived from them.

CROSS_SECTIONAL_AVERAGE.description: Average projected cross-sectional area over all aspects [m2].

AREA_TO_MASS_RATIO.description:
Area-to-mass ratio [m2/kg], only when a source publishes one directly or
the publisher derives it with PROVENANCE.METHOD DERIVED.

OPPSurface.description:
One exterior surface of the object: what it is made of, how large it is and
how it interacts with light.

$PNL carries the articulated panel model used for solar-radiation-pressure
propagation; an $OPP surface is the sourced material inventory. When both
exist, PANEL_ID joins this surface to its $PNL panel. GLTF_MATERIAL_NAME and
GLTF_MATERIAL_INDEX join it to the exact glTF material in the asset variant
named by OPP.ASSET.

ID.description: Stable identifier for this surface within the record.

MATERIAL.description:
Material name verbatim from the source, in whatever designation the
source uses: a multi-layer-insulation film, a photovoltaic cell
chemistry, an alloy temper designation. Empty when unstated.

COUNT.description:
How many identical surfaces this entry represents, such as two solar-array
wings.

PROVENANCE.description:
Provenance of MATERIAL, MATERIAL_CLASS, KIND and COUNT. Every dimensioned
field below carries its own.

AREA.description: Area of one surface, not of COUNT surfaces [m2].

SPECULAR_REFLECTIVITY.description: Fraction of incident radiation reflected specularly, dimensionless.

DIFFUSE_REFLECTIVITY.description: Fraction of incident radiation reflected diffusely, dimensionless.

PANEL_ID.description:
Join key to the $PNL panel representing this surface; holds that record's
PNLPanel.PANEL_ID verbatim. Empty when no $PNL panel exists.

GLTF_MATERIAL_NAME.description:
Name of the glTF material that renders this surface, verbatim, in the
variant named by OPP.ASSET.VARIANT_ID. Empty when the surface is not
represented in the asset.

GLTF_MATERIAL_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index into the glTF materials array of that same variant.
Negative one means no glTF material corresponds to this surface.

OPPAssetRef.description:
Binding to the exact 3D asset bytes this record accompanies.

Every field is copied verbatim from the $VAM that governs the asset, so an
$OPP is valid for exactly one reviewed variant. Different bytes are a
different asset: mint a new $OPP and set SUPERSEDES_OPP_CID rather than
repointing an existing one.

VAM_CID.description: CIDv1 containing a multihash of the exact $VAM bytes.

VARIANT_ID.description: $VAMVariant.ID verbatim: the specific glTF or GLB this record describes.

ASSET_SHA256.description:
$VAMVariant.BYTE_SHA256 verbatim: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
encoding SHA-256 of the exact asset file bytes.

GEOMETRY_MATCHES_PHYSICAL.description:
True only when the asset geometry was authored or rescaled to the physical
dimensions in this record. False, the default, means the asset is
representative and its geometry is not a source of physical dimensions.

METERS_PER_ASSET_UNIT.description:
Metres per asset unit for the named variant. Restates
$VAMTransform.METERS_PER_SOURCE_UNIT for consumers that read only $OPP.

OPP.description:
Object Physical Properties - the sourced physical description of one space
object and, when one exists, of the exact 3D asset that represents it.

Division of labour with the neighbouring standards. $CAT is catalogue
identity and orbit, and its RCS, SIZE and MASS scalars are unattributed
convenience fields carried from the catalogue publisher. $BUS is the bus
DESIGN, shared by every object built on it. $VAM is the asset manifest: the
bytes, the licence, the review and the geometry metrics. $PNL is the
articulated panel model consumed by solar-radiation-pressure propagation.
$OPP is the per-object physical truth in which EVERY value names its own
source, epoch and method. $OPP never restates orbital elements and never
duplicates bus-design values; a per-object value that came from the bus
design is stated here with METHOD INFERRED_FROM_FAMILY so a consumer can see
that it is an approximation.

Joins. NORAD_CAT_ID and OBJECT_ID join to $CAT. BUS_ID joins to $BUS.
ASSET joins to the exact reviewed $VAM variant. ENTITY_ID is the stable
non-catalogue key shared with $VAM for objects that have no catalogue entry.

Never-invent law, enforced by the shape rather than by prose: a physical
quantity exists only as an OPPQuantity and OPPQuantity.PROVENANCE is
required, so there is no encoding for a mass, dimension, area or
cross-section that does not name where it came from. Unknown values are
absent. A consumer that finds a field missing has learned that no admissible
source published it.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 record-format version, not a content revision.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: $CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID verbatim. Zero when the object has no catalogue number.

OBJECT_ID.description: $CAT.OBJECT_ID verbatim: the COSPAR international designator.

OBJECT_NAME.description: $CAT.OBJECT_NAME verbatim, for display only. Never a join key.

ENTITY_ID.description:
Stable non-catalogue entity key, such as an asset catalogue entity path.
MUST equal ASSET.ENTITY_ID when ASSET is present.

BUS_ID.description:
Join key to the $BUS record describing this object's bus design; holds
that record's BUS.ID verbatim. Empty when the bus is unknown or has no
$BUS record.

BUS_FAMILY.description:
Bus or platform family name verbatim from BUS_FAMILY_PROVENANCE.SOURCE,
for objects whose family is known but has no $BUS record.

BUS_FAMILY_PROVENANCE.description: Provenance of BUS_FAMILY. Present whenever BUS_FAMILY is nonempty.

MANUFACTURER.description: Manufacturer or prime contractor as stated by MANUFACTURER_PROVENANCE.

MANUFACTURER_PROVENANCE.description: Provenance of MANUFACTURER. Present whenever MANUFACTURER is nonempty.

RADAR_CROSS_SECTIONS.description:
One entry per band, polarization and aspect the sources publish. Empty
means no source published a radar cross-section for this object.

VISUAL_MAGNITUDE.description:
Visual magnitude, UNITS "mag", with the observing conditions in
PROVENANCE.NOTES.

ASSET.description:
Binding to the exact reviewed 3D asset this record accompanies. Absent for
an object with no asset; the physical values remain valid without it.

SOURCES.description:
Every source consulted while building this record, including sources that
yielded no value. Lets a consumer distinguish "not looked for" from
"looked for and not published".

CREATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) when
the record was created.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) when
the record was last updated.

SUPERSEDES_OPP_CID.description: CIDv1 containing a multihash of the exact superseded $OPP bytes.

IS_STABLE.description: Indicates whether the observation is stable or not

OBJECT_ID.description: Unique identifier for the object being observed

PASS_DURATION.description: Duration of the observation pass in seconds

PAPElement.description: One array element and its applied complex weight.

PAPGainCut.description: One one-dimensional gain cut through the synthesized pattern.

PAPNull.description: One requested adaptive null and its achieved result.

HOP_SCHEDULE_ID.description: BEMHopSchedule.SCHEDULE_ID evaluated by this synthesis, when applicable.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over the size-prefixed FlatBuffer with both 64-byte
signature payloads zeroed while preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over canonical JSON with IDL field order and
capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both signature fields
omitted.

PGMMetadataEntry.description: String metadata key/value attached to a peer group.

DEFAULT_TRUST_LEVEL.description: Default trust level for peers in this group.

MEMBERS.description: libp2p peer IDs that belong to this group.

CREATED_AT.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this group was created.

UPDATED_AT.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when this group record was last updated.

METADATA.description: Additional group metadata as string key/value entries.

DELETED.description: True when this record tombstones the group from the current registry.

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: Peer ID of the node/provider that issued this group record.

PROVIDER_SIGNATURE.description: Provider signature over the peer group record.

INPUTS.description:
Input frames. Each TAB.TYPE_REF names the payload schema and each
TAB.WIRE_FORMAT selects FLATBUFFER or ALIGNED_BINARY. TAB.OFFSET
is arena-relative into PAYLOAD_ARENA (or an absolute pointer when
PAYLOAD_ARENA is empty).

PAYLOAD_ARENA.description:
Optional arena backing the INPUTS payload bodies. Empty means the
caller manages arena state out-of-band.

TRACE_ID.description: Optional trace identifier for request correlation.

OUTPUT_STREAM_CAP.description:
Optional yield-budget hint. Plugins MAY pause queued work after
draining this many output frames and return YIELDED for the caller
to resume. 0 = no hint.

STATUS_CODE.description: Method-specific status code. Zero conventionally indicates success.

YIELDED.description: True when the method yielded before fully draining queued work.

BACKLOG_REMAINING.description:
Outstanding frame count remaining after this response. Non-zero
only when STATUS == YIELDED.

OUTPUTS.description: Output frames. Each TAB carries schema identity and wire format.

PAYLOAD_ARENA.description: Optional arena backing OUTPUTS payload bodies.

ERROR_CODE.description: Stable machine-readable error code when STATUS == FAILED.

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Human-readable diagnostic when STATUS == FAILED.

TRACE_ID.description: Echo of the request's TRACE_ID for correlation.

PIV.description:
Envelope — carries either a request or a response. Either REQUEST or
RESPONSE is populated per message; both populated is undefined.

PUBLISHER_EPM_CID.description: IPFS CID of the publisher `$EPM` that operates this broker

PROVIDER_PEER_ID.description: libp2p peer id of the publisher node hosting the broker

PROTOCOL_ID.description:
libp2p protocol the broker answers on
(e.g. "/space-data-network/module-delivery/1.0.0")

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESSES.description: Dialable multiformat addresses for the broker

BROKER_PUBLIC_KEY.description:
The broker's public key (from the key server's get_public_key) so the
buyer can pin it

LAST_HEARTBEAT_AT.description: Unix ms of the last successful probe/heartbeat

FIRST_SEEN_AT.description: Unix ms the store first saw this broker

UPDATED_AT.description: Unix ms this descriptor was last updated

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the publisher `$EPM` over the self-attested endpoint
fields; re-verified by the store's live probe

PLK.description:
Plugin License Key - Issued license for plugin access
Uses ECIES: both parties derive symmetric key via X25519 ECDH
Key derivation: X25519(private, peer_public) → HKDF-SHA256 → AES-256-GCM

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin ID this license is for

ISSUER_PUBKEY.description:
Issuer's X25519 public key (32 bytes)
Used with licensee's private key to derive shared secret via ECDH

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix timestamp when license was issued

VALID_FROM.description: Unix timestamp when license becomes valid

EXPIRES_AT.description: Unix timestamp when license expires (0 = never expires)

ISSUER_PEER_ID.description: Peer ID of the license issuer (OrbPro)

SIGNATURE.description: Ed25519 signature from issuer over all fields (except SIGNATURE)

PMMTrustAnchor.description:
The single key identity every signature in this manifest resolves to, and
the two external anchors that give that key its weight: the DNS proof that
binds it to the domain, and the Adversarial-Security bond that prices
trust in it.

PROVIDER_DOMAIN.description:
Domain the node key is bound to. MUST equal `PMM.PROVIDER_DOMAIN` and
MUST equal the origin the manifest was fetched from.

NODE_PEER_ID.description: libp2p peer id of the provider node.

NODE_XPUB.description:
BIP-32 account xpub of the node identity, verbatim as advertised in the
node's `$EPM`.

SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY.description:
Hex-encoded public key that verifies `PMM.SIGNATURE` and every
`PMMModuleEntry.ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE`, derived from the node key.

SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm identifier, e.g. "ed25519",
"secp256k1-compact-ethereum". Empty means "ed25519".

EPM_CID.description: IPFS CID of the provider node's `$EPM`.

DNS_PROOF_RECORD_NAME.description:
Fully-qualified DNS name of the TXT record carrying the signed
domain-to-nodekey proof, e.g. "_sdnkey.example.org". A verifying client
resolves this itself (DNS-over-HTTPS) rather than trusting the copy
below.

DNS_PROOF_TXT.description:
Verbatim TXT value of that proof, carried only so a client can detect
disagreement with what DNS returns. The resolved record always wins.

DNS_PROOF_STATEMENT.description:
The canonical statement the DNS proof signs, verbatim, when the proof
format keeps it out of the TXT value.

BOND_ADDRESSES.description:
Chain addresses derived from this same node key that hold the provider's
Adversarial-Security bond. Each entry proves, through `ChainProof`, that
the address derives from the key that signed this manifest.

BOND_ATTESTATION_URL.description:
Optional URL of a machine-readable bond attestation (bonded value,
duration unspent) for clients that price trust rather than gate on it.

MODULE_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS module identity, e.g. "com.orbpro.sgp4-propagator". Stable
across versions. Required and unique within the manifest.

PLUGIN_ID.description:
`$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` of the full listing for this module, when one is
published.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the offered artifact.

EPOCH.description:
Monotonic publication counter for this MODULE_ID. Increases on every
re-publication, including a rebuild at the same VERSION.

CONTENT_HASH.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the module's
portable (pre-AOT, publication-trailer-stripped) WASM bytes. Identical
in meaning to `$APP.APPModuleRef.CONTENT_HASH`: this is the identity
capability and signature policies key on.

ARTIFACT_SIZE_BYTES.description: Size of those portable WASM bytes.

ARTIFACT_PATH.description:
Path, relative to the provider origin, from which the artifact is
fetched. Relative on purpose: the bytes must come from the same origin
whose domain the DNS proof binds.

ARTIFACT_CID.description: IPFS CID of the artifact, for content-addressed retrieval.

ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE.description:
Detached signature by the key in `PMMTrustAnchor.SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY`
over the 32 raw bytes of `CONTENT_HASH`. Lets a client reject an entry
before spending a byte of bandwidth. The artifact's own publication
trailer remains authoritative after download.

DEFAULT_ENABLED.description:
True when the provider ships this module enabled by default. A recorded
user choice overrides it permanently.

ACCESS_POLICY.description: What the client must hold to fetch and run it.

RUNTIME_TARGETS.description:
Opaque runtime-target tags this artifact is built for, e.g. "browser",
"wasmedge". Same vocabulary as `$PLG.RUNTIME_TARGETS`.

REQUIRED_SCHEMAS.description: SDS schema codes at this module's invoke surface, e.g. "OMM", "OEM".

MIN_PERMISSIONS.description:
Minimum host permissions the module needs, same vocabulary as
`$PLG.MIN_PERMISSIONS`. Surfaced so a client can show what an
anonymously-loaded CORE module is allowed to do.

LICENSE.description: SPDX license identifier of the module.

SUPERSEDES_CONTENT_HASH.description: `CONTENT_HASH` this entry replaces, when it supersedes an earlier build.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) of
the last change to this entry.

PLUGIN_TYPE.description:
Family this module belongs to. Mirrors `$PLG.PLUGIN_TYPE` verbatim and
is the ONLY sanctioned way to group an offering: a client grouping a
catalogue MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer family from the shape
of `MODULE_ID`, which carries no normative structure. Defaults to
`Unspecified`, which a client MUST render as ungrouped — never silently
as `Sensor`. Present here, rather than only on
the linked `$PLG`, so an anonymous client can section the catalogue at
boot without fetching one `$PLG` per module.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified `$CCT` category this module is shelved under. Mirrors
`$PLG.PRIMARY_CATEGORY` verbatim and SUPERSEDES `PLUGIN_TYPE` as the
sanctioned way to group an offering: `pluginCategory` is single-valued,
holds a real family at ordinal 0, mixes capability families with
node-internal plumbing, and carries a deprecated vendor-derived member.
Present here, rather than only on the linked `$PLG`, so an anonymous
client can section the catalogue at boot without fetching one `$PLG` per
module. `UNSPECIFIED` MUST render as ungrouped, never as a real category.

SIGNATURE SEAM — normative. Under the `SDN-MODULE-MANIFEST-V1` canonical
statement this field is NOT covered by `PMM.SIGNATURE`, exactly like
`NAME`, `DESCRIPTION` and `ICON_URL`. It is an UNVERIFIED PROVIDER CLAIM
resting on a signed content hash. A consumer that shelves, filters or
counts by this field MUST NOT present the resulting grouping as
authenticated, and MUST keep the verified identity (`MODULE_ID`,
`CONTENT_HASH`, `ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE`, `TRUST_TIER`) visually separable
from provider-supplied presentation. Extending the canonical statement to
cover presentation fields is a `SDN-MODULE-MANIFEST-V2` change that moves
every verifier in lockstep and is not made implicitly by adopting this
field.

CATEGORIES.description:
Every ratified `$CCT` category this module belongs to, for browse, filter
and per-category counting. Mirrors `$PLG.CATEGORIES`. If nonempty it MUST
include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Carries the same unsigned-claim caveat as
PRIMARY_CATEGORY.

PMM.description:
Provider Module Manifest — what one provider node offers, signed by that
node's key.

PROVIDER_DOMAIN.description:
Domain of the provider, e.g. "node.example.org". Required. MUST equal
the origin the manifest was served from.

DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable summary of what the provider serves.

EPOCH.description:
Monotonic manifest epoch. A client MUST reject an epoch lower than the
highest it has already verified for `PROVIDER_DOMAIN`.

TRUST.description: The key identity and its external anchors.

CANONICAL_URL.description: Canonical absolute URL this manifest is served from.

CREATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was created.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was last signed.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
after which a verifier MUST refuse anonymous CORE loading from this
manifest and re-fetch. Required in practice for anonymous trust: an
unexpiring signed manifest cannot be withdrawn.

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature by `TRUST.SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY` over the canonical statement
defined in this file's header.

SIGNED_STATEMENT.description:
The canonical statement, verbatim. A verifier MUST rebuild it from this
record and reject any difference.

PNLPanel.description:
One flat panel of a macro model.

The reflection coefficients describe how incident radiation is disposed of:
SPECULAR_REFLECTIVITY + DIFFUSE_REFLECTIVITY + ABSORPTIVITY should sum to
1 for a physically consistent panel. Producers SHOULD state the source of
the optical properties in the parent record's SOURCE field; a panel model
whose coefficients have no provenance is worse than none.

PANEL_ID.description: Stable panel identifier within the model.

NORMAL_X.description: Outward panel normal in the body frame, unit vector.

SPECULAR_REFLECTIVITY.description: Fraction of incident radiation reflected specularly.

EMISSIVITY.description: Infrared emissivity of the panel surface.

INSTANTANEOUS_RERADIATION.description:
True when absorbed energy is re-radiated instantaneously (no thermal
lag). False means the consumer must model thermal inertia.

DRAG_COEFFICIENT.description: Panel drag coefficient, when the model is used for aerodynamic forces.

MATERIAL_NAME.description: Material name, for traceability back to a materials table.

PNL.description:
Panelled (box-wing) Spacecraft Macro Model — the surface geometry and
optical properties needed to compute non-conservative forces (solar
radiation pressure, atmospheric drag, thermal re-radiation) on one object.

This is deliberately NOT $VAM, $BUS or $PHY. $VAM ranks visual assets for
rendering and a render mesh is not a force model; $BUS/$OOD are descriptive
inventory; $PHY is simulation configuration (integration method, force-type
toggles). None of them carries per-panel area, normal, and optical
coefficients.

OBJECT_ID.description: Object this macro model describes.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Satellite catalog number, when the object is catalogued.

BODY_FRAME.description: Body-fixed frame the panel normals are expressed in, e.g. "SC_BODY".

TOTAL_MASS_KG.description: Total spacecraft mass the model corresponds to, kilograms.

EPOCH.description:
Epoch the model is valid at, ISO 8601. Mass and panel configuration
change over a mission; a macro model without an epoch is ambiguous.

REFERENCE_AREA_M2.description:
Reference cross-sectional area used by a consumer that falls back to a
cannonball model, square metres.

SOURCE.description: Provenance of the geometry and the optical coefficients.

HD_KEY_PATH.description: Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) derivation path for the program's key, used in cryptocurrency wallets

MESSAGE_TYPES.description: Vector of standard message types used by the program

USERS.description: Vector of users associated with the program, each user can have assigned message types

PRWInit.description:
Propagator initialization request — assigns TLE / OMM / Keplerian /
polynomial inputs to entity handles.

The actual per-entity source record is carried inline as raw bytes
tagged with SOURCE_KIND and, where useful, a SDS file_identifier.
Callers encode `OMM`, `OCM`, or a one-off Keplerian set and pass the
bytes verbatim; the propagator uses SOURCE_KIND to decide how to
consume them.

ENTITY_HANDLES.description: Entity handles to assign results to (same order as SOURCES[]).

SOURCES.description: Per-entity source records, encoded as SDS FlatBuffers.

MU.description: Gravitational parameter of the central body (km^3 / s^2).

RAAN.description: Right ascension of the ascending node (radians).

EPOCH.description: Epoch as Julian date.

NORAD_ID.description: NORAD catalog number parsed from the TLE.

BYTES.description: Encoded source record as a FlatBuffer (consumed per KIND).

KEPLERIAN.description: Convenience inline form when KIND == KEPLERIAN.

TLE.description: Convenience inline form when KIND == TLE.

PRWBatchRequest.description:
Batch propagation request — propagate every entity in ENTITY_HANDLES[] to
EPOCH and write the result StateVector stream to OUTPUT_OFFSET in the
shared arena.

EPOCH.description: Target epoch as a Julian date (TIME_SYSTEM is configured on the host).

ENTITY_HANDLES.description: Entity handles to propagate (empty = all initialized entities).

OUTPUT_OFFSET.description: Output buffer offset in the arena where the StateVector stream begins.

MAX_COUNT.description: Maximum entities to process in this call (0 = unbounded).

TARGET_FRAME.description:
Target reference frame for the output state stream. Matches enum
values in SDS `RFM`. If zero, the propagator chooses its native frame.

PRWBatchResponse.description:
Batch propagation response header — describes the stream written to
OUTPUT_OFFSET and reports errors. The stream itself is
`STATE_VECTOR_SIZE`-tuple rows in the SDS `OCM` STATE_DATA layout.

OUTPUT_OFFSET.description: Offset in the arena where the state-vector stream begins.

STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.description: Components per state vector (6 = PV, 9 = PVA). Mirrors OCM.STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame for the stream (SDS `RFM`-compatible string tag).

FLAGS.description: Per-entity status flags (same cardinality as COUNT).

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Optional error message when ERROR_CODE != OK.

PRW.description:
Propagator Runtime Wire — envelope that carries either an init request,
a batch request, or a batch response across a runtime boundary.

SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY.description: Literal Ed25519 public key, encoded as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over the size-prefixed FlatBuffer with both signature
payloads zeroed while preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over canonical JSON in IDL field order and capitalization,
with both signature fields omitted.

QEMTokenVector.description: One pruned-vocabulary token's static embedding row.

TOKEN.description: WordPiece token text, verbatim including any ## continuation marker.

TOKEN_ID.description:
Vocabulary row index. Row order in TOKENS is not guaranteed stable
across MODEL_VERSION; look up by TOKEN_ID, not array position.

VECTOR_INT8.description:
Row values when the parent QEM.ENCODING is INT8. Length equals
QEM.DIMENSIONS.

SCALE.description:
Per-row dequantization scale: original value ~= VECTOR_INT8[i] * SCALE.
Unused when ENCODING is FLOAT32.

VECTOR_FLOAT32.description:
Row values when the parent QEM.ENCODING is FLOAT32. Length equals

IDF.description: Inverse document frequency weight for this token.

QEM.description:
Query Encoder Model.

One QEM publishes the pruned static token-embedding table a lightweight
client (e.g. a browser) loads to encode a search query into the same
vector space a paired $CES shard's rows live in, without shipping a full
transformer. A consumer pools the rows of the query's tokens (per
POOLING_METHOD) into a query vector, then dot-products it against
CES.ROWS.

A QEM is compatible with a CES only when MODEL_ID, MODEL_VERSION,
MODEL_WEIGHTS_SHA256, POOLING_METHOD and TEMPLATE_VERSION all match; a
mismatch on any one means the two vector spaces are not comparable.

MODEL_ID.description: Encoder model identifier/name. Compared verbatim against CES.MODEL_ID.

MODEL_VERSION.description: Encoder model version. Compared verbatim against CES.MODEL_VERSION.

MODEL_WEIGHTS_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the encoder weights, lowercase hex. Same convention as
DPMAsset.BYTE_SHA256. Compared verbatim against CES.MODEL_WEIGHTS_SHA256.

POOLING_METHOD.description:
Sentence/document pooling method the encoder uses. Compared verbatim
against CES.POOLING_METHOD.

TEMPLATE_VERSION.description:
Version of the text template documents were rendered from before
encoding. Compared verbatim against CES.TEMPLATE_VERSION.

DIMENSIONS.description: Fixed embedding dimensionality; must equal the paired CES.DIMENSIONS.

ENCODING.description: Row element encoding used across TOKENS.

VOCAB_SIZE.description: Number of tokens in the pruned vocabulary.

TOKENS.description: One row per pruned vocabulary token.

QRPFilter.description: One field filter of a request.

VALUE.description: Value as text; for In, values separated by commas.

QRPColumn.description: One column descriptor of a page, in record field order.

TYPE.description:

UNIT.description: Unit of the field when the standard declares one, else empty.

SORTABLE.description: True when the serving node can order the page by this column.

QRP.description: Query Page - request, page header or error frame.

SBM.description:
Satellite Breakup Model

One SBM record is a single on-orbit fragmentation event — an explosion or
a collision — together with the debris population a breakup model produced
for it. It carries the model inputs (parent states, masses, relative
velocity, object class, cutoff, seed) so the population is reproducible,
and the resulting fragments in FRAGMENTS.

Units on the wire: parent and fragment position are KILOMETERS, parent and
fragment velocity are KILOMETERS PER SECOND (matching $OMM, $OEM, $OCM and
$CDM state conventions); ejection delta-V, relative velocity and
characteristic length are METERS PER SECOND and METERS respectively
(matching the breakup-model literature). Every field name states its unit.

This record describes an ON-ORBIT breakup. Atmospheric reentry breakup and
demise stay in $RDM/$REM; a business-loss classification of the event stays
in $OOE.

SHC.description:
Spherical-Harmonic Coefficient Set — an actual gravity field, as opposed to
the NAME of one.

This is deliberately NOT $GRV. $GRV is a model SELECTOR: it names a model,
bounds its degree/order, toggles third-body and tidal effects, and carries
scalar J2..J6. It cannot carry a coefficient set, and a named model without
its coefficients is not interchange — it is a citation.

Coefficients are carried as four parallel arrays of equal length, indexed
together: entry i is the coefficient at DEGREES[i], ORDERS[i] with cosine
term C[i] and sine term S[i]. Parallel arrays rather than a table per
coefficient because a 200x200 field is ~40,000 coefficients and a
table-per-coefficient encoding is pathological in both size and decode cost.

CENTRAL_BODY_NAIF_ID.description:
