Recipient of an on-chain revenue split. The identity binds to an `$EPM`
via CHAIN_PROOFS so a payout address is provably the recipient's.

EPM_CID.description: IPFS CID of the recipient's Entity Profile Message (`$EPM`)

ADDRESS.description: On-chain payout address (EVM 0x / SOL base58 / BTC address)

XPUB.description: Account xpub the address derives from

SCX.description:
Chain Settlement / Smart-Contract Descriptor. The forward description of the
exact established splitter contract/program a buyer's wallet targets so
payment and platform commission settle atomically on-chain. Referenced by
`$CMT.CONTRACTS` and echoed into a store `checkout` quote. Commission is
realized by the splitter contract itself when the buyer pays it; there is no
off-chain or manual settlement step.

SPLITTER_STANDARD.description:
Established split standard id, e.g. "0xsplits.v2" (ETH) or the SOL
splitter program name. An audited off-the-shelf standard, not a custom
contract.

SPLITTER_ADDRESS.description:
Deployed splitter contract address (ETH) or splitter program id (SOL) the
buyer's payment routes into

SPLIT_CONFIG_ID.description:
The specific split configuration (recipient set + basis points) registered
with the splitter

TOKEN_ADDRESS.description: ERC-20 / SPL mint address for stablecoin settlement; empty = native asset

SPLIT_RECIPIENTS.description:
The recipient set the split configuration encodes (platform + publisher…),
mirrored here for independent verification

MIN_CONFIRMATIONS.description: Confirmations required before the payment is accepted

MEMO_SCHEME.description: How the order reference is bound on-chain for replay-safe matching

CCTCategory.description:
One ratified category in the taxonomy.

DISPLAY_NAME, SUMMARY and SLUG are required: a category cannot be published
without the label a surface will render, the sentence a browse row will
show, and the route a link will target. This is what stops each consumer
from inventing its own wording for the same code.

CODE.description: The ratified category code. This is the join key every consumer uses.

DISPLAY_NAME.description:
Canonical human-readable label, rendered verbatim. MUST equal the display
name stated in the CODE member's doc comment.

SUMMARY.description: One-sentence description shown on browse rows and category headers.

SLUG.description:
Route-safe identifier: the CODE identifier lowercased with `_` replaced by
`-`. Published explicitly rather than derived so every surface routes
identically.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer editorial description for a category landing page.

PARENT.description:
Parent category for hierarchical browse. UNSPECIFIED means this is a
top-level category. A category MUST NOT name itself as its parent.

SORT_ORDER.description:
Presentation order within its parent, ascending. Ties break on
DISPLAY_NAME.

KEYWORDS.description:
Search synonyms and alternate phrasings that resolve to this category.
Feeds type-ahead; never rendered as the category label.

ICON_KEY.description:
Key of a self-hosted icon or capsule asset for this category. A KEY, not a
URL: consuming node surfaces load zero external-origin bytes, so the
consumer resolves this against its own local asset set.

CCTCategoryRollup.description:
An observed count of catalogue items in one category.

Counts are VOLATILE and are never part of the ratified taxonomy itself. A
rollup exists only with COUNTED_AT and SOURCE_CATALOG_ID, so a published
count can never omit when it was taken or what it was taken over. A consumer
that needs a live number computes it from the items; a consumer rendering a
published rollup MUST show it as of COUNTED_AT.

CODE.description: Category being counted.

ITEM_COUNT.description:
Number of catalogue items whose PRIMARY_CATEGORY or CATEGORIES include
CODE, counted over SOURCE_CATALOG_ID at COUNTED_AT.

SOURCE_CATALOG_ID.description: Identifier of the catalogue the count was taken over.

COUNTED_AT.description: Unix seconds when the count was taken.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

TAXONOMY_ID.description: Stable identifier of this taxonomy publication.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:
The ratified categories. Every capabilityClass member a consumer may
encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.

RFMOrigin.description:
The point a coordinate system is centred on. Body and barycentre
identifiers are integer ephemeris body codes; text NAME is descriptive
only and is never the machine key.

CELESTIAL_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code when KIND is CELESTIAL_BODY.

BARYCENTRE_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the barycentre when KIND is BARYCENTRE.

LIBRATION_POINT.description: Which libration point, when KIND is LIBRATION_POINT.

LIBRATION_PRIMARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system primary.

LIBRATION_SECONDARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system secondary.

OBJECT_ID.description: Identifier of the space object when KIND is SPACE_OBJECT.

SITE_ID.description: Identifier of the surface site when KIND is GROUND_SITE.

SITE_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the body the site sits on.

SITE_LATITUDE.description: Geodetic latitude of the site, degrees, positive north.

SITE_LONGITUDE.description: Geodetic longitude of the site, degrees, positive east.

SITE_ALTITUDE.description: Height of the site above the reference ellipsoid, metres.

RFMObjectReferencedAxes.description:
Axes built from the relative geometry of two objects. Exactly two of the
three axis assignments are independent; the third completes the triad.

RFMLocalAlignedConstrainedAxes.description:
Axes built by aligning one vector with a reference direction and using a
second vector as a constraint. Vectors are 3-element, expressed in the
coordinate system named by REFERENCE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM_NAME.

RFMCoordinateSystem.description:
A fully specified coordinate system: an axis set, an origin, and the epoch
and time system the axis set is evaluated at. This is the unit a frames
consumer needs; the pre-existing RFMUnion members name an axis convention
alone and cannot express an origin.

NAME.description: Stable name for this coordinate system within the producing data set.

AXIS_REFERENCE_BODY_ID.description:
Ephemeris body code whose equator/rotation defines the axes, for the
body-referenced axis types. Independent of ORIGIN.

EPOCH.description:
Reference epoch the axis set is evaluated at, ISO 8601. Required for the
of-date and of-epoch axis types; ignored by the inertial ones.

EPOCH_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system the EPOCH is expressed in, named by the $TIM timingStandard
member name (for example "UTC", "TAI", "TT", "TDB", "A1").

KERNEL_FRAME_NAME.description: Kernel-declared frame name for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

KERNEL_FRAME_ID.description: Kernel-declared numeric frame id for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

EOP_DATA_SET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the Earth-orientation data set used to realise
this system, when the axis chain requires one. Recorded so that two
consumers can prove they used the same table rather than assume it.

FrequencyRange.description: Frequency range with lower and upper limits

StokesParameters.description: Stokes parameters, representing different aspects of polarization

U.description: Another linear polarization, orthogonal to Q

Band.description: Table representing a frequency band with a name and frequency range

DATA_MODE.description: Mode of the data (real, simulated, synthetic)

POWER_TYPE.description: Type of power (eg. AC or DC)

TRANSMIT.description: Indicates if the EMT can transmit

RECEIVE.description: Indicates if the EMT can receive

TASKABLE.description: Indicates if the site is taskable

CLASSIFICATION.description: Classification marking of the data in IC/CAPCO Portion-marked format.

OB_TIME.description: Ob detection time in ISO 8601 UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ssssssZ), up to microsecond precision.

CORR_QUALITY.description: Correlation score of the observation when compared to a known orbit state.

ID_ON_ORBIT.description: Server will auto-populate with SAT_NO if available.

SENSOR_ID.description: Unique ID of the sensor. Must have a corresponding sensor record on the server.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: 18SDS satellite number. Only list if correlated against the 18SDS catalog.

TASK_ID.description: Identifier for the collectRequest message if the collection was in response to tasking.

TRANSACTION_ID.description: Optional identifier to track a transaction.

IMAGE_SET_ID.description: The user-defined set ID of a sequence of images.

IMAGE_SET_LENGTH.description: The number of images in an image set.

SEQUENCE_ID.description: The sequence ID of an image within an image set.

OB_POSITION.description: The position of this observation within a track (FENCE, FIRST, IN, LAST, SINGLE).

ORIG_OBJECT_ID.description: Provider maintained ID. May not be consistent with 18SDS SAT_NO.

UCT.description: Required if correlation is attempted. Indicates whether correlation succeeded.

AZIMUTH.description: Line of sight azimuth angle in degrees and topocentric frame.

AZIMUTH_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight azimuth angle, in degrees.

AZIMUTH_BIAS.description: Sensor line of sight azimuth angle bias in degrees.

AZIMUTH_RATE.description: Rate of change of the line of sight azimuth in degrees per second.

ELEVATION.description: Line of sight elevation in degrees and topocentric frame.

ELEVATION_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight elevation angle, in degrees.

ELEVATION_BIAS.description: Sensor line of sight elevation bias in degrees.

ELEVATION_RATE.description: Rate of change of the line of sight elevation in degrees per second.

RANGE.description: Line of sight range in km. Reported value should include all applicable corrections.

RANGE_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight range, in km.

RANGE_BIAS.description: Sensor line of sight range bias in km.

RANGE_RATE.description: Range rate in km/s. Reported value should include all applicable corrections.

RANGE_RATE_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight range rate, in km/sec.

RA.description: Right ascension in degrees. Required metric reporting field for EO observations.

RA_RATE.description: Line of sight right ascension rate of change, in degrees/sec.

RA_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight right ascension angle, in degrees.

RA_BIAS.description: Sensor line of sight right ascension bias in degrees.

DECLINATION.description: Declination in degrees. Required metric reporting field for EO observations.

DECLINATION_RATE.description: Line of sight declination rate of change, in degrees/sec.

DECLINATION_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line of sight declination angle, in degrees.

DECLINATION_BIAS.description: Sensor line of sight declination angle bias in degrees.

LOSX.description: X-component of the unit vector representing the line-of-sight direction in the observer's reference frame.

LOSY.description: Y-component of the unit vector representing the line-of-sight direction in the observer's reference frame.

LOSZ.description: Z-component of the unit vector representing the line-of-sight direction in the observer's reference frame.

LOS_UNC.description: One sigma uncertainty in the line-of-sight direction vector components.

LOSXVEL.description: X-component of the velocity vector along the line of sight, in km/s.

LOSYVEL.description: Y-component of the velocity vector along the line of sight, in km/s.

LOSZVEL.description: Z-component of the velocity vector along the line of sight, in km/s.

SENLAT.description: WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees at the time of the observation.

SENLON.description: WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees at the time of the observation.

SENALT.description: Sensor height in km relative to the WGS-84 ellipsoid at the time of the observation.

SENX.description: Cartesian X position in km at the time of the observation.

SENY.description: Cartesian Y position in km at the time of the observation.

SENZ.description: Cartesian Z position in km at the time of the observation.

FOV_COUNT.description: Total number of satellites in the field of view.

FOV_COUNT_UCTS.description: Number of uncorrelated satellites in the field of view (JCO).

EXP_DURATION.description:
Image exposure duration in seconds. For observations performed using frame stacking or synthetic tracking methods,
the exposure duration should be the total integration time. This field is highly recommended / required if the
observations are going to be used for photometric processing.

NET_OBJ_SIG_UNC.description: Net object signature uncertainty = counts uncertainty / EXP_DURATION.

MAG.description: Measure of observed brightness calibrated against the Gaia G-band.

GEOLAT.description:
Computed estimate of the latitude, positive degrees north. It should be computed based on the assumed slant range
and corresponding viewing geometry. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEOLON.description:
Computed estimate of the longitude as +/- 180 degrees east. It should be computed based on the assumed slant range
and viewing geometry. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEOALT.description: Computed estimate of satellite altitude in km at the reported location. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEORANGE.description: Computed estimate of the slant range in km. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

SKY_BKGRND.description:
Average Sky Background signal, in Magnitudes. Sky Background refers to the incoming light from an apparently
empty part of the night sky.

PRIMARY_EXTINCTION.description:
Primary Extinction Coefficient, in Magnitudes. Primary Extinction is the coefficient applied to the airmass
to determine how much the observed visual magnitude has been attenuated by the atmosphere. Extinction, in general,
describes the absorption and scattering of electromagnetic radiation by dust and gas between an emitting astronomical
object and the observer.

PRIMARY_EXTINCTION_UNC.description: Primary Extinction Coefficient Uncertainty, in Magnitudes.

SOLAR_PHASE_ANGLE.description:
The angle, in degrees, between the target-to-observer vector and the target-to-sun vector. Recommend using the
calculation listed in the EOSSA documentation, pg 106 of the EOSSA spec.

SOLAR_EQ_PHASE_ANGLE.description:
The angle, in degrees, between the projections of the target-to-observer vector and the target-to-sun vector
onto the equatorial plane. The convention used is negative when closing (i.e., before the opposition)
and positive when opening (after the opposition).

SOLAR_DEC_ANGLE.description: Angle from the sun to the equatorial plane.

RAW_FILE_URI.description: Optional URI location in the document repository of the raw file parsed by the system to produce this record.

INTENSITY.description: Intensity of the target for IR observations, in kw/sr/em.

BG_INTENSITY.description: Background intensity for IR observations, in kw/sr/um.

DESCRIPTOR.description: Optional source-provided and searchable metadata or descriptor of the data.

ORIGIN.description:
Originating system or organization which produced the data, if different from the source.
The origin may be different than the source if the source was a mediating system which forwarded
the data on behalf of the origin system. If null, the source may be assumed to be the origin.

DATA_MODE.description: Indicator of whether the data is EXERCISE, REAL, SIMULATED, or TEST.

CREATED_AT.description: Time the row was created in the database, auto-populated by the system.

CREATED_BY.description: Application user who created the row in the database, auto-populated by the system.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: EO observations are assumed to be topocentric J2000 coordinates ('J2000') as defined by the IAU, unless otherwise specified.

SEN_REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
The sensor reference frame is assumed to be the International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF),
unless otherwise specified. (ITRF is equivalent to Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) for this purpose).
Lat / long / height values should be reported using the WGS-84 ellipsoid, where applicable.

UMBRA.description: Boolean indicating that the target object was in umbral eclipse at the time of this observation.

PENUMBRA.description:
Boolean indicating that the target object was in a penumbral eclipse at the time of this observation.
This field is highly recommended if the observations will be used for photometric processing.

ORIG_NETWORK.description: The originating source network on which this record was created, auto-populated by the system.

SOURCE_DL.description: The source from which this record was received.

AZIMUTH_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if azimuth is reported.

ELEVATION_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if elevation is reported.

RANGE_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if range is reported.

RANGERATE_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if range-rate is reported.

RA_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if right ascension is reported.

DECLINATION_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if declination is reported.

NIIRS.description: National Imagery Interpretability Rating Scale (NIIRS). Ranging from 0 (lowest) to 9 (highest).

METERS_PER_PIXEL.description: Ground sample distance in meters per pixel.

IMAGE_SNR.description: Signal-to-noise ratio of the image. Higher values indicate cleaner imagery.

IMAGE_WIDTH.description: Width of the image in pixels.

IMAGE_HEIGHT.description: Height of the image in pixels.

IMAGE_COMPRESSION.description: Compression type used for the image, e.g., "JPEG", "PNG", "RAW", etc.

IMAGE_COMPRESSION_RATIO.description: Compression ratio used (original size / compressed size), if applicable.

PROCESSED_IMAGE_URI.description: URI to the processed image used for this observation.

IMAGE_AUTO_ENHANCED.description: Flag indicating whether the image was auto-enhanced (e.g., contrast stretch, denoise).

MULTI_FRAME_STACKED.description: True if the observation was taken with multiple frames stacked into one image.

SYNTHETIC_TRACKING_USED.description: True if synthetic tracking was used to create the image.

IMAGE_SHARPNESS.description: Sharpness metric of the image based on the Tenengrad method or variance of Laplacian. Higher values indicate sharper images.

IMAGE_NOISE_STDDEV.description: Noise level of the image, estimated via pixel intensity variance in background regions.

IMAGE_CONTRAST.description: Contrast metric of the image, such as Michelson contrast or RMS contrast.

IMAGE_DYNAMIC_RANGE.description: Dynamic range of the image (max pixel value / min pixel value), indicating tonal spread.

IMAGE_ENTROPY.description: Entropy of the image, representing the richness of information content. Higher entropy suggests higher texture detail.

BACKGROUND_UNIFORMITY.description: Background uniformity metric (e.g., mean gradient in background areas). Lower values indicate more uniform background.

BACKGROUND_MEAN_LEVEL.description: Mean background level, computed from non-object regions in pixel units.

SATURATED_PIXEL_PERCENT.description: Percentage of saturated pixels in the image. Indicates overexposure when high.

DEAD_PIXEL_PERCENT.description: Percentage of dead or zero-value pixels in the image. Indicates sensor defects or underexposure.

PSF_FWHM.description: Estimated Point Spread Function (PSF) Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) in pixels. Indicates image blur or focus.

CLOUD_COVER_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of cloud cover in the image. Derived using cloud detection algorithms such as Fmask or machine learning classifiers.

CLOUD_DETECTION_CONFIDENCE.description: Confidence score of the cloud detection result, from 0 (low confidence) to 1 (high confidence).

HAZE_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of the image obscured by haze or atmospheric scattering effects.

AEROSOL_OPTICAL_THICKNESS.description: Estimated aerosol optical thickness (AOT) at 550 nm, indicating particulate matter in the atmosphere affecting image clarity.

WATER_VAPOR_CONTENT.description: Estimated water vapor content (e.g., total column precipitable water) at the time of imaging, in mm.

SUN_ELEVATION.description: Sun elevation angle at the time of image capture, in degrees above the horizon.

SUN_AZIMUTH.description: Sun azimuth angle at the time of image capture, in degrees from true north.

VIEW_ZENITH_ANGLE.description: View zenith angle (sensor line-of-sight angle from nadir), in degrees.

VIEW_AZIMUTH_ANGLE.description: View azimuth angle (direction of sensor relative to north), in degrees.

OFF_NADIR_ANGLE.description: Off-nadir angle of the sensor at the time of image capture, in degrees.

SWATH_WIDTH_KM.description: Ground coverage width of the image swath in kilometers.

MEAN_TERRAIN_ELEVATION.description: Mean terrain elevation in the image footprint, in meters above sea level.

TERRAIN_ELEVATION_STDDEV.description: Standard deviation of terrain elevation in the image footprint, in meters.

SHADOW_COVER_PERCENT.description: Percentage of the image affected by shadows, derived via topographic or object shadow detection.

SUNGLINT_PRESENT.description: Flag indicating whether sunglint is present in the image (true if high reflectance from water surface due to sun geometry).

SUNGLINT_PERCENT.description: Percentage of image affected by sunglint.

SNOW_ICE_COVER_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of snow or ice coverage in the image footprint.

VALID_DATA_AREA_KM2.description: Total area covered by valid data (non-masked, usable imagery) in square kilometers.

ANTENNA_TYPE.description: Antenna type (e.g., PARABOLIC, PHASED_ARRAY, HORN, HELICAL, DIPOLE, PATCH, YAGI)

QUANTITY.description: Number of antennas of this type

BAND.description: Operating frequency band (e.g., UHF, L, S, C, X, Ku, Ka, V, W)

APERTURE.description: Antenna diameter or aperture in meters

POLARIZATION.description: Polarization type (e.g., LINEAR, CIRCULAR, DUAL, RHCP, LHCP)

SLEW_RATE.description: Maximum slew rate in degrees per second

PURPOSE.description: Purpose or function (e.g., TT_C, PAYLOAD, CROSSLINK, GPS)

TBSProvenance.description:
Replayable provenance for ONE provider's report of ONE site.

Every provider consulted gets its own entry, including providers that
returned nothing, so a consumer can tell "not looked for" from "looked for
and returned nothing". Provider identity is DATA: PROVIDER_ID and AUTHORITY
carry verbatim what that provider states about itself. The standard names
no provider, dataset, or site.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the consulted provider,
unique within the publisher's own provider registry. Never a display
name and never a URL.

AUTHORITY.description:
The authority under which that provider publishes, verbatim as the
provider states it: a spectrum regulator, a network operator, a
crowd-sourced observation programme, or a research dataset. Never
inferred by the publisher.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material.

SOURCE_QUERY.description:
The exact query, filter, or request parameters used, so the same rows can
be recovered by repeating the fetch.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond retrieval timestamp.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Required: there is no encoding for a
redistributed site whose terms are unstated. A provider that publishes no
terms is recorded as publishing no terms; unknown terms are never public
domain and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as that provider publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description:
The licence forbids commercial use. Rides PER SOURCE because one record
may merge an open-terms lane beside a non-commercial cross-check, and the
strictest consulted lane governs any derived product.

NATIVE_ID.description: This provider's own row, cell, or site identifier, verbatim.

REPORTED_LATITUDE.description:
Position this provider reported, in decimal degrees on WGS 84, before
reconciliation. Retained unrounded so the merge stays auditable. Absent
when the provider was consulted and reported no position.

CONTRIBUTED.description:
This provider's report materially contributed to the published CONSENSUS
position. False marks a provider that was consulted and either returned
nothing or was outvoted; its entry is published either way.

TBSConsensus.description:
How one site's independent provider reports were reduced to the single
published position, and how strongly those reports agreed.

PROVIDERS_CONSULTED.description:
Providers queried for this site, including those that returned nothing.
Never fewer than the number of SOURCES entries.

PROVIDERS_AGREEING.description:
Providers whose reported position fell within the publisher's agreement
threshold. A value of 1 means the published position rests on a single
report and was never independently corroborated.

WINNING_PROVIDER_ID.description:
PROVIDER_ID of the report the merge selected, copied verbatim from the
matching SOURCES entry. Absent when METHOD is CENTROID: a computed
position belongs to no single provider.

POSITION_SPREAD_M.description:
Greatest surface distance in metres between any two agreeing reported
positions. Zero is meaningful only when PROVIDERS_AGREEING is 1.

CONFIDENCE.description:
The publisher's own confidence in the merged position, on [0,1]. Never a
provider's figure and never a probability from a model this standard does
not name.

MERGED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond instant at which the merge was performed.

TBS.description:
Terrestrial Base Station Site.

One record describes ONE terrestrial cellular base-station site as
reconciled from every provider the publisher consulted. It is the wire
record for terrestrial mobile-network infrastructure, and it is not an
emitter model ($RFE), a band specification ($RFB), a geodetic tracking
station ($GST), a satellite ground station ($SIT), or an observation.

A site cannot be re-serialized unattributed. SOURCES and CONSENSUS are both
required, so every published position carries the providers it came from and
the rule that reconciled them; a consumer that strips attribution has to
leave the standard to do it. Unknown values are ABSENT — never zero, never a
placeholder, never carried across from a neighbouring site.

Identity is ID, the publisher's own. The network addressing fields are the
mobile network's, are assigned by its operator, and are reused worldwide;
none of them is a global key on its own.

ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier for this site, unique within its record set.
Recommended form: "<mcc>-<mnc>-<area-code>-<cell-id>".

NATIVE_ID.description:
Winning provider's native site identifier, copied verbatim from the
SOURCES entry named by CONSENSUS.WINNING_PROVIDER_ID. Never a substitute
for ID and never stable across providers.

MCC.description:
Mobile country code from the international mobile-subscriber identity
numbering plan. Zero means the source published none.

MNC.description:
Mobile network code within MCC. Carried as an integer, so decimal leading
zeros are NOT preserved: a two- versus three-digit network code is
distinguished by the numbering plan of MCC, and the source's own text is
retained verbatim in TBSProvenance.NATIVE_ID. Zero means unpublished.

LAC.description:
Location area code, used by GSM-, CDMA- and UMTS-class access. Zero means
unpublished. A site published with a location area code does not also
carry a tracking area code; publishing both asserts two access
generations for one cell.

TAC.description:
Tracking area code, used by LTE- and NR-class access. Zero means
unpublished.

CELL_ID.description:
Cell identity verbatim from the source. A string because width, radix and
leading zeros are significant and differ by access class: a 16-bit cell
identity, a 28-bit evolved cell identity and a 36-bit new-radio cell
identity are not interchangeable integers, and this field never converts
between them.

LATITUDE.description:
Reconciled site position in decimal degrees on WGS 84, produced by the
merge described in CONSENSUS. Per-provider positions before
reconciliation live in SOURCES[].REPORTED_LATITUDE/REPORTED_LONGITUDE and
are never overwritten by this value.

RANGE_M.description:
Radius in metres of the area within which the site's observations were
collected — a positional-uncertainty envelope, not a transmission range,
not a coverage guarantee, and never converted from another unit. Zero
means unpublished.

SAMPLES.description:
Independent observations behind the winning report. Zero means the source
publishes no observation count, never that the site was never observed.

AVERAGE_SIGNAL_DBM.description:
Mean received signal strength in dBm across those observations, as the
source publishes it. Carried in dBm unconverted; a consumer needing watts
converts at the join, explicitly. Zero means unpublished.

FIRST_OBSERVED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond bounds of the observation window backing
the winning report.

OPERATOR.description:
Network operator name verbatim as the cited source states it. A display
name, never an identifier: consumers must not treat it as a stable key.

FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Operating centre frequency in MHz, following the $RFB convention. A
consumer joining to $IQC, which carries hertz, converts at the join,
explicitly. Zero means unpublished.

SITE_NAME.description:
Site or structure name verbatim when the source publishes one. Never
synthesized from coordinates, operator, or cell identity.

COUNTRY_CODE.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase, as the source states it.
Derived from MCC only when the source itself derives it.

SOURCES.description:
Every provider consulted for this site, including providers that returned
nothing. Required: a site with no named sources is not publishable.

CONSENSUS.description:
How the entries in SOURCES were reduced to LATITUDE/LONGITUDE. Required:
a published position always states the rule that produced it, including
SINGLE_SOURCE.

RFMOrigin.description:
The point a coordinate system is centred on. Body and barycentre
identifiers are integer ephemeris body codes; text NAME is descriptive
only and is never the machine key.

CELESTIAL_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code when KIND is CELESTIAL_BODY.

BARYCENTRE_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the barycentre when KIND is BARYCENTRE.

LIBRATION_POINT.description: Which libration point, when KIND is LIBRATION_POINT.

LIBRATION_PRIMARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system primary.

LIBRATION_SECONDARY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the libration system secondary.

OBJECT_ID.description: Identifier of the space object when KIND is SPACE_OBJECT.

SITE_ID.description: Identifier of the surface site when KIND is GROUND_SITE.

SITE_BODY_ID.description: Ephemeris body code of the body the site sits on.

SITE_LATITUDE.description: Geodetic latitude of the site, degrees, positive north.

SITE_LONGITUDE.description: Geodetic longitude of the site, degrees, positive east.

SITE_ALTITUDE.description: Height of the site above the reference ellipsoid, metres.

RFMObjectReferencedAxes.description:
Axes built from the relative geometry of two objects. Exactly two of the
three axis assignments are independent; the third completes the triad.

RFMLocalAlignedConstrainedAxes.description:
Axes built by aligning one vector with a reference direction and using a
second vector as a constraint. Vectors are 3-element, expressed in the
coordinate system named by REFERENCE_COORDINATE_SYSTEM_NAME.

RFMCoordinateSystem.description:
A fully specified coordinate system: an axis set, an origin, and the epoch
and time system the axis set is evaluated at. This is the unit a frames
consumer needs; the pre-existing RFMUnion members name an axis convention
alone and cannot express an origin.

NAME.description: Stable name for this coordinate system within the producing data set.

AXIS_REFERENCE_BODY_ID.description:
Ephemeris body code whose equator/rotation defines the axes, for the
body-referenced axis types. Independent of ORIGIN.

EPOCH.description:
Reference epoch the axis set is evaluated at, ISO 8601. Required for the
of-date and of-epoch axis types; ignored by the inertial ones.

EPOCH_TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time system the EPOCH is expressed in, named by the $TIM timingStandard
member name (for example "UTC", "TAI", "TT", "TDB", "A1").

KERNEL_FRAME_NAME.description: Kernel-declared frame name for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

KERNEL_FRAME_ID.description: Kernel-declared numeric frame id for EPHEMERIS_KERNEL_DEFINED axes.

EOP_DATA_SET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the Earth-orientation data set used to realise
this system, when the axis chain requires one. Recorded so that two
consumers can prove they used the same table rather than assume it.

TDMTransmitRamp.description:
One uplink transmitter frequency ramp applying over a closed time interval.

SDS EXTENSION beyond CCSDS 503.0-B-1: the base standard carries a single
TRANSMIT_FREQ_1 per segment, which cannot express a ramped uplink. Deep-space
radiometric archives carry an explicit ramp table and the Doppler observables
are NOT reconstructible without it. Ramps are optional; a record that omits
TRANSMIT_RAMPS is exactly a CCSDS-conformant TDM.

Frequency over the interval is the linear polynomial
f(t) = FREQUENCY_HZ + FREQUENCY_RATE_HZ_PER_S * (t - REFERENCE_TIME)
which is the common form of the two archive representations: DSN ODF
(TRK-2-18, table 3-5) supplies ramp start frequency, ramp rate, and ramp
start/end time, so REFERENCE_TIME equals START_TIME; ESA IFMS supplies a
ramp reference time with constant and linear transmission-frequency terms,
so REFERENCE_TIME is that reference time and may precede START_TIME.
Producers MUST set REFERENCE_TIME explicitly rather than letting a consumer
assume which convention was used.

START_TIME.description: Start of the interval over which this ramp applies, ISO 8601.

END_TIME.description: End of the interval over which this ramp applies, ISO 8601.

REFERENCE_TIME.description: Epoch at which FREQUENCY_HZ is the instantaneous value, ISO 8601.

FREQUENCY_RATE_HZ_PER_S.description: Constant ramp rate over the interval, Hz per second.

TRANSMITTING_STATION_ID.description:
Identifier of the transmitting station the ramp applies to. Must match
the PARTICIPANT_n naming used by the segment when both are present.

TRANSMIT_BAND.description:
Uplink band the ramp applies to, using the same vocabulary as
TRANSMIT_BAND (e.g. "S", "X", "Ka", "Ku").

TDMObservation.description:
ONE CCSDS TDM observation: a single data-section line.

A TDM data section is NOT a uniform grid. Every line in every published
example (CCSDS 503.0-B-2 Cor.1 annex E, 18 figures) has the literal form

KEYWORD = <epoch> <value>

and the epochs are chosen INDEPENDENTLY PER KEYWORD. Figure E-17 (ground
based radar tracking with RCS) is decisive: RANGE, ANGLE_1, ANGLE_2 and
CARRIER_POWER share epochs, while the final RCS line repeats the EARLIER
epoch 2011-05-11T10:26:33.7008 after a 10:26:33.9686 line. No single
OBSERVATION_START_TIME + i * OBSERVATION_STEP_SIZE grid can express that,
which is why the parallel observation arrays on the TDM root cannot
round-trip a conformant TDM.

KEYWORD is the CCSDS data keyword verbatim and case-exact, e.g. "RANGE",
"ANGLE_1", "CARRIER_POWER", "RCS", "DOPPLER_INTEGRATED", "PR_N0",
"RECEIVE_FREQ_1", "TRANSMIT_PHASE_CT_1", "VLBI_DELAY", "DOR", "MAG",
"CLOCK_BIAS", "STEC", "TROPO_DRY", "PRESSURE". Carrying the keyword rather
than a fixed field per observable is what lets this form transport the whole
503.0-B-2 data vocabulary, including keywords a future issue adds, without
a wire change and without inventing a name the standard does not define.

Units are those the standard assigns to that keyword; RANGE additionally
depends on RANGE_UNITS, which is metadata, not data.

KEYWORD.description: CCSDS data keyword, verbatim and case-exact.

EPOCH.description: Epoch of this single observation, ISO 8601, in the segment TIME_SYSTEM.

TDMSegment.description:
One TDM metadata + data segment.

A TDM file may carry MANY segments, each with its own META_START/META_STOP
block and its own DATA_START/DATA_STOP block (503.0-B-2 Cor.1 annex E,
figures E-16 and E-18). The TDM root models a SINGLE segment, so a
multi-segment file cannot be represented without this vector.

COMMENT.description: Comments carried in this segment's metadata block, in file order.

OBSERVATIONS.description:
The segment's observations, in FILE ORDER. This is the authoritative
data-section representation.

TRANSMIT_RAMPS.description:
Uplink frequency ramp table applying to this segment. SDS EXTENSION;
absent (not empty) for a ramp-free, exactly CCSDS-conformant segment.

DATA_TYPES.description: Comma-separated list of the data keywords present in the data section.

PATH.description:
Signal path through the participants as an ordered comma-separated list,
e.g. "1,2,1". Distinct from the numbered PATH_1 / PATH_2 above.

EPHEMERIS_NAME_1.description: Name of the ephemeris used to generate the data, per participant.

RANGE_UNITS.description:
Units of the RANGE observable: "km", "s" or "RU" (range units).
RANGE is meaningless without it.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
Reference frame for angle and position data, as the verbatim CCSDS
keyword value (503.0-B-2 annex B).

INTERPOLATION.description: Recommended interpolation method for the observations.

FREQ_OFFSET.description: Frequency offset applied to the observations, Hz.

RECEIVE_DELAY_1.description:
Receive delay for the first participant, s. (RECEIVE_DELAY_2 and
RECEIVE_DELAY_3 already exist on the TDM root.)

DOPPLER_COUNT_ROLLOVER.description: Whether the Doppler counter rolls over (CCSDS YES/NO).

CORRECTION_RANGE.description:
Corrections that a consumer must apply, or that were applied when
CORRECTIONS_APPLIED is "YES". Units follow the corrected observable.

OBSERVER_ID.description: Unique identifier for the observation OBSERVER -  [Specific CCSDS Document]

OBSERVER_X.description: Cartesian X coordinate of the OBSERVER location in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_Y.description: Cartesian Y coordinate of the OBSERVER location in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_Z.description: Cartesian Z coordinate of the OBSERVER location in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_VX.description: Cartesian X coordinate of the OBSERVER velocity in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_VY.description: Cartesian Y coordinate of the OBSERVER velocity in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_VZ.description: Cartesian Z coordinate of the OBSERVER velocity in chosen reference frame

OBSERVER_POSITION_REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame used for OBSERVER location Cartesian coordinates (e.g., ECEF, ECI)

OBS_REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame used for obs location Cartesian coordinates (e.g., ECEF, ECI)

EPOCH.description: Epoch time or observation time, in ISO 8601 UTC format -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1

OBSERVATION_STEP_SIZE.description:
Time interval between observations in seconds (required).
Time reconstruction: time[i] = OBSERVATION_START_TIME + (i * OBSERVATION_STEP_SIZE)

OBSERVATION_START_TIME.description: Start time for observation time reconstruction (ISO 8601 UTC format).

CCSDS_TDM_VERS.description: TDM version number -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

COMMENT.description: Comments regarding TDM -  various sections, e.g., Page D-9

CREATION_DATE.description: Date of TDM creation -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

ORIGINATOR.description: Originator of the TDM -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

META_START.description: Start of metadata section -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

START_TIME.description: Start time of the data -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

STOP_TIME.description: Stop time of the data -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PARTICIPANT_1.description: First participant in the TDM -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PARTICIPANT_2.description: Second participant in the TDM -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PARTICIPANT_3.description: Third participant in the TDM (if applicable) -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PARTICIPANT_4.description: Fourth participant in the TDM (if applicable) -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PARTICIPANT_5.description: Fifth participant in the TDM (if applicable) -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9, max participants

MODE.description: Mode of TDM -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PATH_1.description: First path in TDM -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

PATH_2.description: Second path in TDM (if applicable) -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

RECEIVE_DELAY_2.description: Receive delay for second participant -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

RECEIVE_DELAY_3.description: Receive delay for third participant -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

META_STOP.description: End of metadata section -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

DATA_START.description: Start of data section -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

TRANSMIT_FREQ_1.description: Transmit frequency for first participant -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

DATA_STOP.description: End of data section -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-9

TIMETAG_REF.description:
Additional properties as required by the specific application of the TDM...
Reference for time tagging -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-10

ANGLE_TYPE.description:
Type of angle data -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12
Can be AZEL, RADEC, XEYN, XSYE, or another value with provided ICD

ANGLE_1.description: First angle value -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12

ANGLE_2.description: Second angle value -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12

RANGE_RATE.description: Rate of change of range -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1

RANGE_MODE.description: Mode of range data -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-10

RANGE_MODULUS.description: Modulus value for range data -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-10

CORRECTION_ANGLE_1.description: First correction angle -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12

CORRECTION_ANGLE_2.description: Second correction angle -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12

CORRECTIONS_APPLIED.description: Indicator of corrections applied -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-12

TROPO_DRY.description: Dry component of tropospheric delay -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-14

TROPO_WET.description: Wet component of tropospheric delay -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-14

STEC.description: Slant total electron content -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-13

CLOCK_BIAS.description: Clock bias values -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-15

CLOCK_DRIFT.description: Clock drift values -  CCSDS 503.0-B-1, Page D-15

SIGNAL_TO_NOISE.description:
SDS EXTENSION beyond CCSDS 503.0-B-1. Open-loop (non-coherent) Doppler
quality metrics, one entry per observation, parallel to the other
observation arrays and reconstructed on the same OBSERVATION_START_TIME +
i * OBSERVATION_STEP_SIZE grid.

Signal-to-noise ratio of the detection.

SPECTRAL_MAX.description: SDS EXTENSION. Normalised spectral maximum of the detection.

DOPPLER_NOISE_HZ.description:
SDS EXTENSION. 1-sigma noise on the measured Doppler frequency, Hz. The
measured sky frequency itself is carried by RECEIVE_FREQ; this is its
uncertainty, which CCSDS 503.0-B-1 has no field for.

TRANSMIT_RAMPS.description:
SDS EXTENSION beyond CCSDS 503.0-B-1. Uplink transmitter frequency ramp
table covering this segment, ordered by START_TIME and non-overlapping.
Required in practice for ramped uplinks, where TRANSMIT_FREQ_1 alone
cannot reconstruct the observables. Absent for unramped tracking, which
leaves the record exactly CCSDS-conformant.

OBSERVATIONS.description: Data-section observations for a SINGLE-segment TDM, in file order.

SEGMENTS.description: All metadata+data segments of a MULTI-segment TDM, in file order.

TRANSMIT_FREQ_2.description:
Additional transmit frequencies by participant, Hz. TRANSMIT_FREQ_1
already exists above; 2..5 had no carrier.

TRANSMIT_FREQ_RATE_1.description:
Transmit frequency rates by participant, Hz/s. A constant rate here is
the single-interval degenerate case of TRANSMIT_RAMPS.

DATA_TYPES.description: Comma-separated list of the data keywords present in the data section.

PATH.description:
Signal path through the participants as an ordered comma-separated list,
e.g. "1,2,1". Distinct from the numbered PATH_1 / PATH_2 above.

EPHEMERIS_NAME_1.description: Name of the ephemeris used to generate the data, per participant.

RANGE_UNITS.description:
Units of the RANGE observable: "km", "s" or "RU" (range units).
RANGE is meaningless without it.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
Reference frame for angle and position data, as the verbatim CCSDS
keyword value (503.0-B-2 annex B).

INTERPOLATION.description: Recommended interpolation method for the observations.

FREQ_OFFSET.description: Frequency offset applied to the observations, Hz.

RECEIVE_DELAY_1.description:
Receive delay for the first participant, s. (RECEIVE_DELAY_2 and
RECEIVE_DELAY_3 already exist on the TDM root.)

DOPPLER_COUNT_ROLLOVER.description: Whether the Doppler counter rolls over (CCSDS YES/NO).

CORRECTION_RANGE.description:
Corrections that a consumer must apply, or that were applied when
CORRECTIONS_APPLIED is "YES". Units follow the corrected observable.

CryptoKey.description:
Represents cryptographic key information.

The publication paradigm is "literal public keys, not derivation
material": a published EPM carries the PUBLIC_KEY bytes that verify
the record's SIGNATURE (signing) or encrypt to the entity (encryption),
and NOTHING about how those keys were derived. XPUB, KEY_PATH and
KEY_ADDRESS are PRIVATE / operational — they belong to the wallet that
produced the keys, never to the record a peer resolves.

Requiredness is PROFILE-ENFORCED, never a flatc `(required)` attribute:
a `(required)` on PUBLIC_KEY would make the flatbuffers Verifier reject
every pre-flip secp256k1 record that legitimately omitted it (the
2026-07-27 dual-curve regime allowed xpub-derivation for secp at
non-hardened paths). A published record is self-describing instead —
PUBLIC_KEY present, XPUB/KEY_PATH/KEY_ADDRESS absent — and a conformance
checker asserts that profile (see scripts/check-epm-published-profile.mjs).

Rotation is by republish: a new signing or encryption key means a new
PUBLIC_KEY, a re-signed SIGNATURE, and a re-published EPM at the same
peer-addressed location. The PeerID (multihash of the libp2p identity
pubkey) is the stable anchor across rotations.

PUBLIC_KEY.description:
Public part of the cryptographic key, in hexadecimal format. AUTHORITATIVE
in a published record: this is the verifying/encrypting key, and no other
field yields it. Required-in-practice (profile-enforced, not flatc
`(required)`) so that pre-flip secp256k1 records without it still decode.

XPUB.description:
Extended public key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic
wallets), "Extended keys". PRIVATE / operational: present only in the
wallet that derived the keys, ABSENT from published records. A verifier
never derives a child key from XPUB — the PUBLIC_KEY is the verification
material.

PRIVATE_KEY.description: Private part of the cryptographic key in hexidecimal format, should be kept secret

XPRIV.description: Extended private key, as specified by BIP-32 (hierarchical deterministic wallets), "Extended keys".

KEY_ADDRESS.description:
Address generated from the cryptographic key. PRIVATE / operational in a
published EPM: a chain address is bound through a ChainProof attestation,
not carried as a standalone KEY_ADDRESS on the CryptoKey. ABSENT from
published records.

ADDRESS_TYPE.description:
Type of the address generated from the cryptographic key. An address
format tag only — NOT a curve or algorithm designator; the algorithm
lives in ALGORITHM

KEY_TYPE.description: Type of the cryptographic key (signing or encryption)

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of this key from the entity root
(e.g., "m/44'/0'/0'/0/0" secp256k1 non-hardened, "m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'"
ed25519 hardened). PRIVATE / operational: how the key was derived belongs
to the wallet, not to a published record. ABSENT from published records.

ALGORITHM.description:
Key algorithm/curve (e.g., "ed25519", "secp256k1"). ABSENT means
ed25519: every record published before this field existed verifies
unchanged under that default. The verifier dispatches on ALGORITHM (not
on ADDRESS_TYPE, which is an address-format tag only).

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format produced by this key (e.g., "raw-ed25519",
"compact"). ABSENT means the canonical encoding of ALGORITHM
(raw-ed25519 for ed25519, compact for secp256k1)

REGION.description: Region of the address (e.g., state or province)

LOCALITY.description: Locality of the address (e.g., city or town)

ChainProof.description: Proves a blockchain key derives from the same HD wallet as the signing key

KEY_PATH.description: BIP-44 derivation path (e.g., "m/44'/0'/0'/0/0")

SIGNATURE.description: Signature over the attestation payload (hex-encoded)

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed (hex-encoded)

ENCODING.description: Signature encoding format (e.g., "compact", "raw-ed25519")

DomainProof.description:
Proves control of a DNS domain by the same HD wallet as the signing key —
the EPM-record mirror of the DNS TXT wire form (which is deliberately
NON-SDS: a base64 FlatBuffer would not fit a 255-byte TXT record). The
canonical statement is 6 fixed LF-terminated lines prefixed
"sdn-domain-proof/1", and it verifies by BYTE-REPLAY of the verbatim
SIGNED_PAYLOAD (ChainProof precedent) — never by JCS.

DOMAIN.description: Fully-qualified domain name the proof binds (e.g., "node.example.org")

KEY_PATH.description:
BIP-32 / SLIP-10 derivation path of the proving key. The signer is the
Ed25519 EPM/publication key at m/44'/0'/0'/0'/0'

SIGNATURE.description: Signature over the attestation payload (hex-encoded)

SIGNED_PAYLOAD.description: The canonical payload that was signed, verbatim (hex-encoded)

ENCODING.description:
Signature encoding format. ABSENT means the canonical encoding of
ALGORITHM (raw-ed25519 for ed25519)

LEGAL_NAME.description: Common name of the entity (person or organization)

FAMILY_NAME.description: Family name or surname of the person

GIVEN_NAME.description: Given name or first name of the person

ADDITIONAL_NAME.description: Additional name or middle name of the person

HONORIFIC_PREFIX.description: Honorific prefix preceding the person's name (e.g., Mr., Dr.)

HONORIFIC_SUFFIX.description: Honorific suffix following the person's name (e.g., Jr., Sr.)

KEYS.description: Cryptographic keys associated with the entity

MULTIFORMAT_ADDRESS.description: Multiformat addresses associated with the entity

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature over canonical EPM content (hex), produced by the entity's
signing key under the algorithm declared in SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM
(absent declaration = Ed25519)

SIGNATURE_TIMESTAMP.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the EPM was signed

CHAIN_PROOFS.description: Chain binding proofs linking blockchain keys to the same HD wallet

ENTITY_TYPE.description: Type of entity represented by this profile

SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm that produced SIGNATURE (e.g., "ed25519",
"secp256k1"). ABSENT means ed25519 — this single default is what keeps
every EPM signed before this field existed verifying unchanged, so the
field MUST NOT be made required. The signing key is the first CryptoKey
in KEYS with KEY_TYPE Signing whose ALGORITHM matches this declaration
(an absent CryptoKey.ALGORITHM likewise means ed25519)

DOMAIN_PROOFS.description:
DNS domain binding proofs linking domains to the same HD wallet —
symmetric with CHAIN_PROOFS

FlatBufferTypeRef.description: Payload-schema identity for a stream frame or an accepted port type.

SCHEMA_VERSION.description: Optional semver or schema revision string.

ROOT_TYPE.description: Optional root type name within the schema.

SCHEMA_HASH.description: Optional schema hash bytes for stronger compatibility checks.

ACCEPTS_ANY_FLATBUFFER.description: True when this port/type set accepts any FlatBuffer frame.

WIRE_FORMAT.description: Logical wire format for this accepted type.

FIXED_STRING_LENGTH.description: Fixed string length for aligned-binary string fields, when applicable.

BYTE_LENGTH.description: Byte length for fixed-size aligned-binary records, when applicable.

REQUIRED_ALIGNMENT.description: Required start alignment for aligned-binary records, when applicable.

TAB.description: Typed Arena Buffer — one descriptor for a payload slot in a shared arena.

OFFSET.description: Byte offset of the payload body within the arena.

SIZE.description: Byte length of the payload body.

ALIGNMENT.description: Required start alignment of the payload body (in bytes).

FRAME_ID.description: Optional opaque frame identifier for stream bookkeeping.

PORT_ID.description:
Optional port identifier for frames that route to/from a named
input or output port on a method (maps to
`PLG.PLGPortManifest.PORT_ID`). Empty for arena frames that carry
no port routing hint.

CCTCategory.description:
One ratified category in the taxonomy.

DISPLAY_NAME, SUMMARY and SLUG are required: a category cannot be published
without the label a surface will render, the sentence a browse row will
show, and the route a link will target. This is what stops each consumer
from inventing its own wording for the same code.

CODE.description: The ratified category code. This is the join key every consumer uses.

DISPLAY_NAME.description:
Canonical human-readable label, rendered verbatim. MUST equal the display
name stated in the CODE member's doc comment.

SUMMARY.description: One-sentence description shown on browse rows and category headers.

SLUG.description:
Route-safe identifier: the CODE identifier lowercased with `_` replaced by
`-`. Published explicitly rather than derived so every surface routes
identically.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer editorial description for a category landing page.

PARENT.description:
Parent category for hierarchical browse. UNSPECIFIED means this is a
top-level category. A category MUST NOT name itself as its parent.

SORT_ORDER.description:
Presentation order within its parent, ascending. Ties break on
DISPLAY_NAME.

KEYWORDS.description:
Search synonyms and alternate phrasings that resolve to this category.
Feeds type-ahead; never rendered as the category label.

ICON_KEY.description:
Key of a self-hosted icon or capsule asset for this category. A KEY, not a
URL: consuming node surfaces load zero external-origin bytes, so the
consumer resolves this against its own local asset set.

CCTCategoryRollup.description:
An observed count of catalogue items in one category.

Counts are VOLATILE and are never part of the ratified taxonomy itself. A
rollup exists only with COUNTED_AT and SOURCE_CATALOG_ID, so a published
count can never omit when it was taken or what it was taken over. A consumer
that needs a live number computes it from the items; a consumer rendering a
published rollup MUST show it as of COUNTED_AT.

CODE.description: Category being counted.

ITEM_COUNT.description:
Number of catalogue items whose PRIMARY_CATEGORY or CATEGORIES include
CODE, counted over SOURCE_CATALOG_ID at COUNTED_AT.

SOURCE_CATALOG_ID.description: Identifier of the catalogue the count was taken over.

COUNTED_AT.description: Unix seconds when the count was taken.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

TAXONOMY_ID.description: Stable identifier of this taxonomy publication.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:
The ratified categories. Every capabilityClass member a consumer may
encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.

PLGAcceptedTypeSet.description:
Accepted schema family for a port. When a port accepts multiple wire
formats (canonical FlatBuffer + aligned-binary), each ALLOWED_TYPE
entry carries its own TAB.FlatBufferTypeRef with the schema identity,
and the enclosing PLGPortManifest advertises both wire formats via
ALLOWED_WIRE_FORMATS. Per SDK contract: a port that advertises
aligned-binary MUST also advertise the canonical flatbuffer fallback
for the same schema and file identifier in the same set.

The one ratified $CCT category this module is shelved under. This is the
category a storefront capsule, a library shelf and a breadcrumb show when
exactly one must be chosen. UNSPECIFIED means the publisher did not
classify the module; a consumer renders it ungrouped and never guesses.

This supersedes PLUGIN_TYPE for all storefront, library and search
surfaces. PLUGIN_TYPE remains on the wire and is not removed, but its
`pluginCategory` vocabulary mixes capability families with node-internal
plumbing, carries a legacy vendor-derived member, holds a real family at
ordinal 0, and admits only one value. Canonical migration, applied by a
publisher rewriting an old manifest:
Sensor->SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE, Propagator->PROPAGATION,
Renderer->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING,
Analysis->MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS,
DataSource->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, EW->ELECTRONIC_WARFARE,
Comms->RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS, Physics->SPACE_ENVIRONMENT,
Shader->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING, Parser->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST,
Validator->DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY, Interpolator->PROPAGATION,
Exporter->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, Foundation->FOUNDATION_AND_MATH,
Infrastructure->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE, Licensing->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING,
Storefront->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING, Publisher->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE,
Basilisk->PROPAGATION, Maneuver->MANEUVER_PLANNING,
Flow->FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION, Unspecified->UNSPECIFIED.

and per-category counting. A module MAY carry several. If nonempty it
MUST include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Codes MUST NOT repeat. An empty list with
a set PRIMARY_CATEGORY means the module belongs to that one category.

PMMTrustAnchor.description:
The single key identity every signature in this manifest resolves to, and
the two external anchors that give that key its weight: the DNS proof that
binds it to the domain, and the Adversarial-Security bond that prices
trust in it.

PROVIDER_DOMAIN.description:
Domain the node key is bound to. MUST equal `PMM.PROVIDER_DOMAIN` and
MUST equal the origin the manifest was fetched from.

NODE_PEER_ID.description: libp2p peer id of the provider node.

NODE_XPUB.description:
BIP-32 account xpub of the node identity, verbatim as advertised in the
node's `$EPM`.

SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY.description:
Hex-encoded public key that verifies `PMM.SIGNATURE` and every
`PMMModuleEntry.ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE`, derived from the node key.

SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.description:
Signature algorithm identifier, e.g. "ed25519",
"secp256k1-compact-ethereum". Empty means "ed25519".

EPM_CID.description: IPFS CID of the provider node's `$EPM`.

DNS_PROOF_RECORD_NAME.description:
Fully-qualified DNS name of the TXT record carrying the signed
domain-to-nodekey proof, e.g. "_sdnkey.example.org". A verifying client
resolves this itself (DNS-over-HTTPS) rather than trusting the copy
below.

DNS_PROOF_TXT.description:
Verbatim TXT value of that proof, carried only so a client can detect
disagreement with what DNS returns. The resolved record always wins.

DNS_PROOF_STATEMENT.description:
The canonical statement the DNS proof signs, verbatim, when the proof
format keeps it out of the TXT value.

BOND_ADDRESSES.description:
Chain addresses derived from this same node key that hold the provider's
Adversarial-Security bond. Each entry proves, through `ChainProof`, that
the address derives from the key that signed this manifest.

BOND_ATTESTATION_URL.description:
Optional URL of a machine-readable bond attestation (bonded value,
duration unspent) for clients that price trust rather than gate on it.

MODULE_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS module identity, e.g. "com.orbpro.sgp4-propagator". Stable
across versions. Required and unique within the manifest.

PLUGIN_ID.description:
`$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` of the full listing for this module, when one is
published.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the offered artifact.

EPOCH.description:
Monotonic publication counter for this MODULE_ID. Increases on every
re-publication, including a rebuild at the same VERSION.

CONTENT_HASH.description:
64 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding SHA-256 of the module's
portable (pre-AOT, publication-trailer-stripped) WASM bytes. Identical
in meaning to `$APP.APPModuleRef.CONTENT_HASH`: this is the identity
capability and signature policies key on.

ARTIFACT_SIZE_BYTES.description: Size of those portable WASM bytes.

ARTIFACT_PATH.description:
Path, relative to the provider origin, from which the artifact is
fetched. Relative on purpose: the bytes must come from the same origin
whose domain the DNS proof binds.

ARTIFACT_CID.description: IPFS CID of the artifact, for content-addressed retrieval.

ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE.description:
Detached signature by the key in `PMMTrustAnchor.SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY`
over the 32 raw bytes of `CONTENT_HASH`. Lets a client reject an entry
before spending a byte of bandwidth. The artifact's own publication
trailer remains authoritative after download.

DEFAULT_ENABLED.description:
True when the provider ships this module enabled by default. A recorded
user choice overrides it permanently.

ACCESS_POLICY.description: What the client must hold to fetch and run it.

RUNTIME_TARGETS.description:
Opaque runtime-target tags this artifact is built for, e.g. "browser",
"wasmedge". Same vocabulary as `$PLG.RUNTIME_TARGETS`.

REQUIRED_SCHEMAS.description: SDS schema codes at this module's invoke surface, e.g. "OMM", "OEM".

MIN_PERMISSIONS.description:
Minimum host permissions the module needs, same vocabulary as
`$PLG.MIN_PERMISSIONS`. Surfaced so a client can show what an
anonymously-loaded CORE module is allowed to do.

LICENSE.description: SPDX license identifier of the module.

SUPERSEDES_CONTENT_HASH.description: `CONTENT_HASH` this entry replaces, when it supersedes an earlier build.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) of
the last change to this entry.

PLUGIN_TYPE.description:
Family this module belongs to. Mirrors `$PLG.PLUGIN_TYPE` verbatim and
is the ONLY sanctioned way to group an offering: a client grouping a
catalogue MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer family from the shape
of `MODULE_ID`, which carries no normative structure. Defaults to
`Unspecified`, which a client MUST render as ungrouped — never silently
as `Sensor`. Present here, rather than only on
the linked `$PLG`, so an anonymous client can section the catalogue at
boot without fetching one `$PLG` per module.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified `$CCT` category this module is shelved under. Mirrors
`$PLG.PRIMARY_CATEGORY` verbatim and SUPERSEDES `PLUGIN_TYPE` as the
sanctioned way to group an offering: `pluginCategory` is single-valued,
holds a real family at ordinal 0, mixes capability families with
node-internal plumbing, and carries a deprecated vendor-derived member.
Present here, rather than only on the linked `$PLG`, so an anonymous
client can section the catalogue at boot without fetching one `$PLG` per
module. `UNSPECIFIED` MUST render as ungrouped, never as a real category.

SIGNATURE SEAM — normative. Under the `SDN-MODULE-MANIFEST-V1` canonical
statement this field is NOT covered by `PMM.SIGNATURE`, exactly like
`NAME`, `DESCRIPTION` and `ICON_URL`. It is an UNVERIFIED PROVIDER CLAIM
resting on a signed content hash. A consumer that shelves, filters or
counts by this field MUST NOT present the resulting grouping as
authenticated, and MUST keep the verified identity (`MODULE_ID`,
`CONTENT_HASH`, `ARTIFACT_SIGNATURE`, `TRUST_TIER`) visually separable
from provider-supplied presentation. Extending the canonical statement to
cover presentation fields is a `SDN-MODULE-MANIFEST-V2` change that moves
every verifier in lockstep and is not made implicitly by adopting this
field.

CATEGORIES.description:
Every ratified `$CCT` category this module belongs to, for browse, filter
and per-category counting. Mirrors `$PLG.CATEGORIES`. If nonempty it MUST
include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Carries the same unsigned-claim caveat as
PRIMARY_CATEGORY.

PMM.description:
Provider Module Manifest — what one provider node offers, signed by that
node's key.

PROVIDER_DOMAIN.description:
Domain of the provider, e.g. "node.example.org". Required. MUST equal
the origin the manifest was served from.

DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable summary of what the provider serves.

EPOCH.description:
Monotonic manifest epoch. A client MUST reject an epoch lower than the
highest it has already verified for `PROVIDER_DOMAIN`.

TRUST.description: The key identity and its external anchors.

CANONICAL_URL.description: Canonical absolute URL this manifest is served from.

CREATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was created.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
when the manifest was last signed.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ)
after which a verifier MUST refuse anonymous CORE loading from this
manifest and re-fetch. Required in practice for anonymous trust: an
unexpiring signed manifest cannot be withdrawn.

SIGNATURE.description:
Signature by `TRUST.SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY` over the canonical statement
defined in this file's header.

SIGNED_STATEMENT.description:
The canonical statement, verbatim. A verifier MUST rebuild it from this
record and reject any difference.

FlatBufferTypeRef.description: Payload-schema identity for a stream frame or an accepted port type.

SCHEMA_VERSION.description: Optional semver or schema revision string.

ROOT_TYPE.description: Optional root type name within the schema.

SCHEMA_HASH.description: Optional schema hash bytes for stronger compatibility checks.

ACCEPTS_ANY_FLATBUFFER.description: True when this port/type set accepts any FlatBuffer frame.

WIRE_FORMAT.description: Logical wire format for this accepted type.

FIXED_STRING_LENGTH.description: Fixed string length for aligned-binary string fields, when applicable.

BYTE_LENGTH.description: Byte length for fixed-size aligned-binary records, when applicable.

REQUIRED_ALIGNMENT.description: Required start alignment for aligned-binary records, when applicable.

TAB.description: Typed Arena Buffer — one descriptor for a payload slot in a shared arena.

OFFSET.description: Byte offset of the payload body within the arena.

SIZE.description: Byte length of the payload body.

ALIGNMENT.description: Required start alignment of the payload body (in bytes).

FRAME_ID.description: Optional opaque frame identifier for stream bookkeeping.

CCTCategory.description:
One ratified category in the taxonomy.

DISPLAY_NAME, SUMMARY and SLUG are required: a category cannot be published
without the label a surface will render, the sentence a browse row will
show, and the route a link will target. This is what stops each consumer
from inventing its own wording for the same code.

CODE.description: The ratified category code. This is the join key every consumer uses.

DISPLAY_NAME.description:
Canonical human-readable label, rendered verbatim. MUST equal the display
name stated in the CODE member's doc comment.

SUMMARY.description: One-sentence description shown on browse rows and category headers.

SLUG.description:
Route-safe identifier: the CODE identifier lowercased with `_` replaced by
`-`. Published explicitly rather than derived so every surface routes
identically.

DESCRIPTION.description: Longer editorial description for a category landing page.

PARENT.description:
Parent category for hierarchical browse. UNSPECIFIED means this is a
top-level category. A category MUST NOT name itself as its parent.

SORT_ORDER.description:
Presentation order within its parent, ascending. Ties break on
DISPLAY_NAME.

KEYWORDS.description:
Search synonyms and alternate phrasings that resolve to this category.
Feeds type-ahead; never rendered as the category label.

ICON_KEY.description:
Key of a self-hosted icon or capsule asset for this category. A KEY, not a
URL: consuming node surfaces load zero external-origin bytes, so the
consumer resolves this against its own local asset set.

CCTCategoryRollup.description:
An observed count of catalogue items in one category.

Counts are VOLATILE and are never part of the ratified taxonomy itself. A
rollup exists only with COUNTED_AT and SOURCE_CATALOG_ID, so a published
count can never omit when it was taken or what it was taken over. A consumer
that needs a live number computes it from the items; a consumer rendering a
published rollup MUST show it as of COUNTED_AT.

CODE.description: Category being counted.

ITEM_COUNT.description:
Number of catalogue items whose PRIMARY_CATEGORY or CATEGORIES include
CODE, counted over SOURCE_CATALOG_ID at COUNTED_AT.

SOURCE_CATALOG_ID.description: Identifier of the catalogue the count was taken over.

COUNTED_AT.description: Unix seconds when the count was taken.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:

encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.
